Title: Knowledge Engineer
Location: Tallahassee, Orlando, Jacksonville, Miami and Tampa
Description:
About Cook Systems

For over 30 years, Cook Systems has partnered with organizations across the country to solve technology challenges and build strong technology teams. As a veteran-owned IT consulting company, we combine decades of industry experience with a continued focus on how technology, AI, and the way people work are evolving.

Our work spans technology consulting, talent development, and AI-enabled solutions. We value people who take ownership, adapt quickly, communicate well, and care about the quality of their work. Whether you’re early in your career or bringing years of experience, you’ll have the opportunity to keep building your skills, contribute to meaningful client work, and grow with a company that continues to evolve with the industry.

Summary: We are seeking an experienced Knowledge Management Architect who will develop the infrastructure and processes necessary to capture, share, and utilize organizational knowledge gained through successful system interventions. The role involves overseeing the identification of critical knowledge, its usage, availability, and aligning it with the needs of various business groups. The ideal candidate will facilitate the development of knowledge architecture and standards, partnering with operations staff to ensure the delivery of knowledge and information to appropriate groups.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and implement infrastructure and processes to capture and share organizational knowledge.
  • Oversee the identification and utilization of critical knowledge across business groups.
  • Model information sources, flows, and critical paths to understand how information is transformed into knowledge.
  • Facilitate the development of supporting knowledge architecture and standards.
  • Define an operational framework to implement delivery systems, systems management, and security frameworks.
  • Collaborate with IT groups to ensure cohesive cross-functional decision-making.
  • Provide leadership in making complex IT and business decisions.
  • Coach and mentor junior technical staff, acting as a subject matter expert on high-complexity projects.

  • A minimum of 7 years of IT and business/industry work experience.
  • Expertise in process and data modeling, architectural development methodologies, and IT planning methodologies.
  • Strong knowledge of document management, groupware, relational database systems, data warehouse, and data mining.
  • Experience in web and systems analysis/development.
  • Proven leadership skills with the ability to gain credibility with business leaders and stakeholders.

Title: Knowledge Manager
Description:
Join our team at Core One! Our mission is to be at the forefront of devising analytical, operational and technical solutions to our Nation's most complex national security challenges. In order to achieve our mission, Core One values people first! We are committed to recruiting, nurturing, and retaining top talent! We offer a competitive total compensation package that sets us apart from our competition. Core One is a team-oriented, dynamic, and growing company that values exceptional performance!

*This position requires a TS/SCI Clearance.* 

*This position is contingent on award*

*This position may require up to six months of deployment annually*

Responsibilities:

 

  • Support the alignment of business processes, technologies, and workflows to facilitate information sharing and collaboration among analysts, organizations, and mission partners supporting intelligence production.
  • Utilize centralized and peripheral databases, content management systems, records management systems, and other knowledge management capabilities to support the organization, accessibility, and dissemination of intelligence information.
  • Analyze and refine workflows, processes, and information management practices to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of analytical production and knowledge-sharing activities.
  • Compile, analyze, and report performance, utilization, and operational metrics to assess the effectiveness of existing knowledge management capabilities and identify areas for improvement.
  • Assess current and future knowledge management requirements related to information search, discovery, storage, retrieval, formal intelligence production, taskings, and information sharing.
  • Coordinate the dissemination of intelligence products across separate networks, systems, and portals in accordance with applicable security requirements, policies, and procedures.
  • Support the identification and implementation of enhancements to knowledge management processes, technologies, and capabilities to improve information accessibility, discoverability, and analytical production.

 

Levels:

  • Junior: Minimum of one year of experience conducting analysis relevant to this Labor Category
  • Mid: Minimum of three (3) years of experience conducting analysis relevant to this Labor Category
  • Senior: Minimum of eight (8) years of experience conducting analysis relevant to this Labor Category
  • Expert: Minimum of twelve (12) years of experience conducting analysis relevant to this Labor Category

Qualifications:

 

  • At least three (3) years of experience conducting analysis directly relevant to the specific labor category, with at least a portion of the experience gained within the preceding two (2) years.
  • Experience applying comprehensive mission knowledge, technical skills, and tradecraft gained through the required developmental training and experience for the labor category.
  • Experience analyzing and communicating insights from incomplete, indirect, highly complex, disparate, or technically advanced information and synthesizing reporting from multiple sources, analytic perspectives, organizations, and intelligence disciplines.
  • Experience identifying trends and developing analytical judgments by integrating reporting, contextual information, and alternative analytic perspectives to produce well-supported assessments.
  • Experience independently planning, prioritizing, and executing analytical and mission-support activities with minimal oversight and direction while meeting established quality and production requirements.

  • Experience developing concise, insightful, comprehensive, and well-supported intelligence products tailored to defense intelligence requirements and senior stakeholder audiences.
  • Experience leading teams in researching and addressing multifaceted, complex, or critical intelligence problems and providing guidance on the selection, design, and application of appropriate analytic methodologies.
  • Experience applying structured analytic techniques, argument evaluation, and validated analytic methodologies to assess competing hypotheses, challenge differing perspectives, identify analytical gaps, and strengthen the rigor and objectivity of intelligence assessments.

 

Security Clearance:

  • TS/SCI Clearance

Title: Mission Operations & AI Enablement Lead
Description:
Mission Operations & AI Enablement Lead

OceanX Singapore

About OceanX:

OceanX is a nonprofit working to unlock the ocean’s sustainable potential. Through a dual focus on science and education, we’re building a new paradigm where humanity and the ocean mutually thrive. Our approach is fueled by exploration, leveraging advanced research, multimedia educational programs, cross-sector partnerships, and advanced technology to help transform how people understand and value the ocean. Our work strives to fortify biodiversity and increase the sustainable use of ocean resources to help ensure the ocean remains a foundation for human wellbeing and potential. OceanX is a nonprofit operating program of Dalio Philanthropies.

For more information, visit www.oceanx.org and follow OceanX on Facebook, Instagram, X, TikTok, LinkedIn, and YouTube.   

Position Summary:

OceanX is seeking a Mission Operations & AI Enablement Lead who will oversee global expedition planning and execution while driving the adoption of AI-enabled systems, workflow automation, and operational technologies across the Missions function. This role serves as a key operational partner, ensuring mission readiness, efficient execution, and continuous improvement across OceanX’s scientific expeditions.

The ideal candidate brings experience in operations, project management, systems implementation, or complex global initiatives. This is a hands-on, systems-focused role requiring ownership of mission planning, cross-functional coordination, data-driven reporting, and AI-enabled process improvement, with the ability to translate operational complexity into scalable, efficient workflows.

OceanX Missions advances its work through operational excellence, innovation, and collaboration, leveraging integrated systems, automation, and data-informed decision-making to support successful global expeditions.

Position Location:

Singapore

Duties and Responsibilities:

Mission Operations & Execution

  • Oversee mission planning and execution across all phases, including pre-expedition planning, mission execution, post-expedition assessment, and continuous operational improvement.
  • Manage operational planning related to international permitting, customs, immigration, documentation, logistics, and regulatory compliance to support successful expedition execution across global jurisdictions.
  • Coordinate with internal teams, research institutions, external partners, vendors, logistics providers, and government agencies to ensure successful mission execution while balancing scientific priorities and operational requirements.
  • Partner with Marine Operations to support vessel scheduling, mission scenario planning, routing, fuel considerations, port availability, seasonal planning, weather analysis, and overall operational readiness.

AI Enablement, Systems & Integration

  • Implement AI-enabled workflows, automations, and operational systems that streamline mission planning, coordination, execution, and reporting.
  • Build and maintain integrations across mission management platforms (including Smartsheet, Jira, Notion, Monday.com, Marine Facilities Planner, and related systems) to automate workflows, improve data accuracy, and reduce manual processes.
  • Develop practical AI agents, templates, reporting tools, and workflow automations that improve team efficiency and reduce repetitive manual work.
  • Identify opportunities to simplify processes, strengthen operational visibility, and improve information flow through AI-enabled solutions and systems integration.

Data Management & Reporting

  • Maintain the integrity, governance, and accessibility of mission data, ensuring timely reporting and visibility for leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Develop and maintain mission planning tools, executive dashboards, reporting systems, and operational documentation that support informed decision-making across the organization.
  • Create automated reporting and dashboards that communicate mission status, approvals, financials, milestones, action items, operational risks, and key performance indicators.
  • Conduct post-expedition operational reviews and leverage data analytics to identify trends, improve planning processes, and drive continuous improvement.
  • Research and evaluate international maritime regulations, permitting requirements, and operational constraints to support long-term mission planning and mitigate execution risks.

Operational Leadership & Continuous Improvement

  • Drive the continued evolution of OceanX's mission operations capabilities, operational standards, systems, and best practices to support future expedition planning and organizational growth.
  • Foster collaboration across OceanX's Science, Marine Operations, Education, Media, Partnerships, Data, and Business Operations teams to ensure mission priorities are effectively aligned and executed.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

  • Professional Experience:
    • Bachelor’s Degree or higher, preferably in marine sciences or a business/project management or related field.
    • 5+ years of project management, operations management, or systems implementation experience in dynamic, global organizations.
    • Strong project management capabilities with a proven track record managing complex, multi-stakeholder initiatives across international contexts.
    • Demonstrated experience building and implementing AI solutions: specifically experience with AI agents, GPT-based language models, or automation tools for business process optimization, data analytics, and workflow management.
    • Hands-on experience with API integration and systems connectivity, including practical knowledge of connecting enterprise platforms (Jira, Smartsheet, Notion, Monday.com, or similar) to create automated workflows.
    • Experience in maritime operations, vessel logistics, oceanographic research, or scientific expedition planning highly desirable.
    • Willingness to work flexible hours, including early mornings or late evenings, to support cross-time zone collaboration.
    • Adaptable to varying workloads, balancing periods of focused execution with lighter operational phases.
  • Personal Attributes:
    • Determined, resourceful, and practical. An independent, self-starter, with a “roll up your sleeves” attitude and strong work ethic
    • Agility, with a track record of getting things done
    • Strong project management capabilities
    • Organized, reliable, and meticulous
    • Ability to work and thrive in an entrepreneurial, rapidly evolving environment, with significant ambiguity
    • Ability to prioritize, meet tight deadlines, anticipate needs, and maintain high-quality work
    • Ability to identify patterns and design practical technical solutions that create order from complexity with moderate guidance.
    • Strong interpersonal and communication skills (written and verbal)
    • Maintains high standards
    • Highly collaborative
    • Interest in ocean science, exploration, conservation, or other mission-driven scientific initiatives

Compensation and Benefits:

Compensation for the role includes a competitive salary (inclusive of a merit-based bonus, dependent on years of experience, level of education obtained, as well as applicable skillset) and an excellent benefits package, including a comprehensive employer-paid medical plan and CPF.

Title: Director of Sales Enablement, Training & Go-to-Market
Location: San Francisco, CA; New York City, NY; Atlanta, GA; Chicago, IL; Denver, CO; Washington D.C.; Austin, TX; Phoenix, AZ; Los Angeles, CA; Seattle, WA; Boston, MA
Description:
About the Role

DoorDash is seeking a Director of Sales Enablement, Training & Go-to-Market to lead the design, delivery, and execution of programs that accelerate the productivity, effectiveness, and growth of our global Sales organization. You will scale enablement across our multi-faceted business model, from SaaS solutions to Ads and Marketplace partnerships, ensuring sellers are equipped with the skills, product expertise, content, and insights to win in every conversation.

You will own the full enablement lifecycle: onboarding, ongoing skill development, sales methodology, manager coaching, content strategy, certification, tooling, and the operating cadence that ties them together. You will partner deeply with Sales, Product, Marketing, and Operations leaders to translate strategy into execution, making sure new capabilities are adopted quickly and consistently across all sales segments.

As part of this mandate, you will also lead the deployment of AI tools, including Claude, across the Sales organization. AI is becoming core to modern selling, and you will own the strategy for embedding it into seller workflows while serving as the Sales voice in cross-functional GTM forums shaping how AI is rolled out to adjacent customer-facing teams (Customer Success, Partnerships, Marketing, and Support).

By pairing operational rigor with sales coaching excellence and applied AI fluency, you will drive faster ramp times, higher productivity, stronger product adoption, and sustainable revenue growth.

You’re Excited About This Opportunity Because You Will:

Core Sales Enablement

  • Own the Onboarding Experience: Design and continuously improve new-hire onboarding for SDRs, AEs, and AMs across SMB, Mid-Market, and Enterprise segments, with clear milestones, certifications, and ramp targets that demonstrably shorten time-to-productivity.
  • Build Continuous Learning Programs: Run a year-round curriculum of skills training, product education, segment-specific bootcamps, and sales kickoff content that keeps reps sharp and aligned with strategy.
  • Embed a Sales Methodology: Select, customize, and operationalize a sales methodology (Challenger, MEDDIC, SPIN, or similar) across the org, with reinforcement built into pipeline reviews, deal inspection, and manager coaching.
  • Tailor Enablement Across Business Models: Deliver differentiated playbooks and training for SaaS, Ads, and Marketplace solutions, equipping reps to position value, handle objections, run effective discovery, and cross-sell seamlessly.
  • Own Sales Content Strategy: Build and govern a content system (pitch decks, one-pagers, case studies, battle cards, ROI tools, email templates) that is easy to find, easy to use, and continuously refreshed based on rep and customer feedback.
  • Lead Product Adoption & Expertise: Partner with Product, Ads, and Marketing to launch new features and offerings into the field with clear positioning, training, certification, and measurement of seller readiness.
  • Coach & Develop Sales Talent: Build a coaching culture by enabling frontline managers with frameworks, call review rituals, deal coaching playbooks, and tools to consistently raise the performance bar.
  • Run the Enablement Operating Rhythm: Establish the cadence (intake, prioritization, launch calendar, feedback loops, post-mortems) that makes enablement predictable and trusted by Sales leadership.

AI & Sales Productivity

  • Lead AI Deployment for Sales: Own the strategy, rollout, and adoption of Claude and other AI tools across the Sales org. Build prompt libraries, AI-assisted workflows, and certification paths that turn every seller and manager into an AI power user.
  • Elevate Sales Productivity with AI-First Workflows: Drive adoption of AI-powered workflows for prospecting, account research, call prep, proposal generation, deal coaching, and post-call follow-up. Replace manual work with intelligent automation wherever it creates leverage.
  • Drive Measurable AI ROI: Define and track the business impact of AI in Sales, including hours saved, pipeline generated, win-rate lift, content velocity, and quality improvements, and continuously expand the use cases that move the needle.
  • Influence GTM-Wide AI Direction: Represent Sales in cross-functional GTM AI working groups, share what’s working with CS, Marketing, Partnerships, and Support leaders, and help shape enterprise-wide standards for tooling and prompts, without owning execution outside Sales.
  • Support Responsible AI Use: Partner with Legal, Security, and IT to apply DoorDash’s AI usage guidelines, data handling policies, and quality controls within Sales, and feed Sales learnings back into enterprise policy.

Leadership & Impact

  • Own Business Impact Metrics: Define and track KPIs including ramp time, quota attainment, seller productivity, content utilization, certification rates, and incremental revenue growth attributable to enablement programs.
  • Strengthen XFN Partnerships: Act as the connective tissue between Sales and cross-functional stakeholders (Product, Ops, Marketing, IT, Legal), ensuring alignment on GTM priorities, seamless rollouts of new initiatives, and continuous feedback loops to Product and Ops.
  • Lead and Inspire: Manage and develop a high-performing global team of enablement managers, trainers, instructional designers, coaches, and GTM program leads.

We’re Excited About You Because:

  • 12+ years of experience in Sales Enablement, Training, or Sales Leadership in high-growth SaaS, Ads, or Marketplace companies, with at least 5+ years leading enablement teams.
  • Proven track record of designing onboarding and continuous-learning programs that measurably reduced ramp time and increased quota attainment at scale.
  • Deep knowledge of modern sales methodologies (Challenger, MEDDIC, SPIN) and demonstrated experience embedding them across a multi-segment sales org.
  • Strong content strategy chops, including governance, taxonomy, sales content tooling, and measurement of content effectiveness.
  • Skilled at designing and leading manager coaching frameworks, call review programs, and deal inspection rituals that improve win rates and deal velocity.
  • Experience tailoring enablement to multiple business models (e.g., SaaS subscriptions, Ads, Marketplace) and multiple segments (SMB, Mid-Market, Enterprise).
  • Applied AI deployment experience: You have personally rolled out LLM-based tools (Claude, ChatGPT Enterprise, Copilot, or similar) to a sales org and can speak credibly to prompt design, workflow integration, change management, adoption metrics, and measurable outcomes.
  • AI fluency in practice, not just theory: Comfortable with prompt engineering, evaluating model outputs, designing human-in-the-loop workflows, and integrating AI with CRM, enablement, and conversation intelligence platforms.
  • Experienced in building cross-functional partnerships with Product, Marketing, and Operations, and comfortable representing Sales in broader GTM forums.
  • Strategic GTM thinker able to translate complex product roadmaps into clear, actionable sales motions.
  • Exceptional leadership and team-building skills with a global mindset.
  • Excellent communication, facilitation, and executive presence, with a data-driven approach.
  • Familiarity with enablement platforms (Highspot, Seismic, Mindtickle), conversation intelligence (Gong, Chorus), LMS tools, CRM systems (Salesforce preferred), and enterprise AI platforms (Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Google).

Compensation

The successful candidate’s starting pay will fall within the pay range listed below and is determined based on job-related factors including, but not limited to, skills, experience, qualifications, work location, and market conditions. Base salary is localized according to an employee’s work location. Ranges are market-dependent and may be modified in the future.

We are looking for a strategic, highly collaborative, and execution-oriented operator to help shape how Marketing uses AI across the org. This role will lead AI enablement for Marketing, support the intake and prioritization of AI opportunities, and partner with teams to turn promising ideas into repeatable workflows, tools, and operating practices.

This role is designed to help Marketing move from fragmented experimentation to a unified, workflow-aligned AI operating model that creates measurable business value. It is a blend of strategy, program management, change management, and hands-on enablement.

You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…

Title: Operations Enablement Partner
Description:
EverDriven is opening doors to a brighter future for every student and every community through safe, reliable transportation. We partner with school districts to serve students who need it most—including those experiencing homelessness, living with disabilities, or outside traditional bus routes—through a tech-powered, human-led model that gets every student to school safe, calm, and ready to learn.
We live three cultural pillars: we do the right thing, leading with integrity and taking ownership of what matters most. We work together, bringing diverse skills and strengths to solve complex challenges as one team. And we never settle, staying curious and driven, guided by data, always raising the bar for students, families, and school districts.

 

Position Summary 

EverDriven is investing in new technology, new processes, and new ways of working across our operations, and that investment only pays off when people adopt it. The Operations Enablement Partner is accountable for two connected responsibilities. 

The first is change adoption. This person builds and runs the end-to-end change and enablement plan for every operational initiative, from kickoff through 90-day reinforcement, defining who is impacted, what changes for them, how they learn it, how managers reinforce it, and whether it held. This role will from time to time run enablement for cross-functional teams where the change impact is largest on operations but broader change management is required.  

The second is job readiness for the operations function. This person owns new-hire and ongoing training for Contact Center, Field Operations, and Inside Operations team members on the systems, processes, and service standards required to do their jobs. They develop and oversee the Field Operations onboarding program, delivered via a train-the-trainer model.  Company and HR onboarding remains with the People team; this role owns the operational craft. 

The two responsibilities reinforce each other: the person who teaches the job is well positioned to lead its change. Content for both should be AI-first, drafted with AI tools and refined by the Partner, so materials are built once and leveraged across teams just in time. 

Salary Range: $90,000 - $105,000/year, based on experience + bonus potential 

Location: Greenwood Village, CO. Hybrid role - 4 days in the office and 1 day remote. 

Responsibilities 

Change Enablement and Adoption

  • Build and execute the end-to-end change and enablement plan for operational initiatives: stakeholder change profiles, communications, training, manager reinforcement asks, and adoption measurement, embedded in each initiative's project plan. 
  • Partner with initiative sponsors and project leads at kickoff to define who is impacted, what specifically changes, and the adoption metrics. 
  • Equip front-line supervisors and managers to carry each change: talking points, coaching prompts, and reinforcement activities they deliver in their own teams. 
  • Track adoption at 30, 60, and 90 days after launch, feed results into the enablement scorecard, and recommend boosters when behavior is drifting. 

Operations Onboarding and Training 

  • Own job-readiness onboarding for the operations function: design and deliver the new-hire training that teaches Contact Center, Field Operations, and Inside Operations team members how to do their jobs. 
  • Own and deliver Field Operations onboarding via a train-the-trainer model: ensure field-designated trainers know what they're doing, have the right materials, and provide oversight to confirm onboarding training is completed in the field. 
  • Train and support our offshore trainers and monitor the quality of BPO-delivered training, providing oversight, coaching, and guidance to ensure vendor partners deliver training that meets our standards. 
  • Hold onboarding to fixed service-level commitments; new-hire classes run on schedule regardless of what else is launching. 
  • Run continuous training driven by QA results, product updates, and process changes, including targeted coaching interventions and role-specific boosters. 

Process and Systems Focus 

  • Translate process and system changes (CRM, routing, compliance, scheduling, and support tools) into clear, teachable workflows; partner with process improvement and product teams from the design stage. 
  • Own rollout readiness for new operational tools: pilot feedback, wave planning support, job aids, and go-live support models. 
  • Keep SOPs, knowledge content, and training in sync with how the work actually runs, in partnership with knowledge management. 

AI-First Content Development 

  • Use AI tools daily to draft training modules, job aids, communications, and assessments, then edit for accuracy and voice. 
  • Build asynchronous-first: on-demand modules, microlearning, and flipped-classroom paths that scale across a dispersed workforce, with live sessions reserved for practice and coaching. 
  • Contribute to one shared enablement content library; build once, reuse everywhere. 
  • Administer LMS content for operations: assignments, reporting, and upkeep. 

Facilitation 

  • Facilitate live and virtual sessions across operations audiences, from frontline CSR classes to field leadership workshops. 

Requirements 

  • 3+ years in enablement, training, or change execution supporting operations, contact center, or field teams. 
  • Train-the-trainer experience: you've built or run a train-the-trainer model for a distributed team (field, offshore, or vendor-delivered), including creating trainer materials and monitoring training quality against a standard. 
  • Hands-on change execution: you have played a core role in at least one end-to-end change or adoption effort (communications, training, reinforcement, measurement), owned major pieces of it, and can walk us through the plan and what you would do differently. Full ownership of a change is a plus; the appetite to own one here is required. 
  • AI-first mindset: you already use AI tools as your default way to draft content and design learning, and you can show examples. AI speeds your drafting; your judgment makes it right. 
  • Working knowledge of process mapping and systems thinking; comfortable reading a workflow, spotting where it breaks for the people doing it, and teaching the fix. 
  • Strong facilitation and coaching skills, live and virtual, across frontline and leadership audiences. 
  • Experience with an LMS and adoption or performance data; you measure whether behavior changed after the training. 
  • Bachelor's degree preferred; equivalent experience in operations, training, or enablement considered in lieu of a degree. 

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Full ownership of an end-to-end change or adoption plan. 
  • Change management certification (Prosci, CCMP, or similar). 
  • Contact center training experience, including QA-driven coaching. 
  • Experience overseeing offshore or BPO training vendors. 
  • Rollout experience with CRM or workforce systems (Service Cloud, WFM, routing or dispatch tools). 
  • Experience in K-12, logistics, transportation, or other dispersed field operations.

  • Medical, Dental, Vision insurance
  • Virtual Doctor Visits with $0 Co-Pay
  • Life Insurance (company paid)
  • Short Term Disability Insurance (company paid)
  • Long-Term Disability Insurance (company paid)
  • Flexible Time Off (FTO)
  • Paid Holidays
  • Paid Time to Volunteer
  • Flex Spending Account (FSA)
  • 401K Plan (with an awesome employer match!)
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • Employee Discounts Program

Title: Manager, PAR Ecosystem Enablement
Description:
The Company:

Faraday Future is a California-based technology company focused on the design, engineering, and development of intelligent, connected electric vehicles and related artificial intelligence–enabled technologies.

Founded in 2014, the Company’s mission is to disrupt the automotive and technology industries by creating user-centric, technology-first experiences. The Company, together with its controlled subsidiaries, operates across multiple technology-driven areas, including AI electric vehicles, robotics, and its crypto business (AIXC), all under its upgraded Global EAI Industry Bridge Strategy, marking the beginning of a new chapter in AI mobility and Web3 integration. The Company aims to leverage the latest technologies and world’s best talent to realize exciting new possibilities across all of these lines. Faraday Future’s automotive business exemplifies its vision for luxury, innovation, and performance, while its FX strategy aims to introduce mass production models equipped with state-of-the-art luxury technology derived from the FF brand, targeted towards a broader market with middle-to-low price range offerings. FF is committed to redefining mobility through AI innovation. Join us in shaping the future of intelligent transportation and technology by creating something new, something connected, and something with a true global impact.

Your Role:

The Manager, PAR Ecosystem Enablement is a senior cross-functional leadership role within the PAR Business team. This person will own and lead FF’s dealer/partner (FF Par) enablement function end-to-end — architecting the enablement strategy, building and scaling the program infrastructure, and driving measurable improvements in dealer readiness, productivity, and satisfaction. Working at the intersection of business, legal, content, and multiple sales pillars, this role sets the direction for how FF equips and develops its external partner ecosystem.

This is a strategic yet hands-on leadership role requiring strong program ownership, cross-functional influence, and excellent bilingual communication skills in both English and Mandarin Chinese. The ideal candidate brings proven experience leading multi-stakeholder programs in a B2B or channel context, and the ability to operate effectively at both the strategic and execution levels. Work location is El Segundo, CA; domestic and international travel may be required to support dealer engagements and partner events.

Key Responsibilities:

  1. Enablement Strategy & Program Ownership
  • Define and own the overall PAR dealer enablement strategy, establishing a clear vision for how FF develops and sustains a high-performing dealer ecosystem.
  • Lead the design, launch, and continuous improvement of structured enablement programs covering dealer onboarding, product training, go-to-market readiness, and commercial capability building.
  • Translate business objectives from PAR leadership into executable enablement roadmaps with defined milestones, resource requirements, and success metrics.
  • Act as the accountable owner for enablement program outcomes, regularly reviewing KPIs and adjusting strategy based on data, dealer feedback, and business performance.
  1. Cross-functional Leadership & Stakeholder Management
  • Lead cross-functional enablement initiatives by aligning and coordinating stakeholders across Business, Legal, Content, Marketing, and Sales pillars — setting direction, managing dependencies, and driving decision-making.
  • Serve as the senior point of contact for enablement-related topics in leadership discussions, representing the PAR team’s dealer development needs and progress.
  • Build strong working relationships with functional leaders and subject matter experts to ensure enablement programs reflect the latest product, commercial, and compliance requirements.
  • Proactively identify gaps, risks, and opportunities across the dealer ecosystem and bring structured proposals to leadership for prioritization.
  1. Dealer Development & Ecosystem Growth
  • Lead the design of scalable dealer development frameworks that enable FF’s partner network to grow in capability, coverage, and commercial performance over time.
  • Oversee dealer-facing communications strategy, ensuring consistent, professional, and bilingual messaging across the PAR network.
  • Drive the planning and execution of dealer development events, training programs, and partner engagement initiatives — from strategy through logistics.
  • Build feedback loops with the dealer ecosystem and translate insights into program improvements and strategic recommendations for PAR leadership.
  1. Legal, Compliance & Policy Integration
  • Work closely with Legal and Compliance to ensure all dealer-facing enablement materials, onboarding processes, and partner communications meet FF’s regulatory and governance standards.
  • Own the compliance dimension of dealer enablement, including qualification checkpoints, certification tracking, and audit-readiness of program documentation.
  • Lead the update process for compliance-sensitive enablement content, ensuring materials remain current with regulatory changes and internal policy updates.
  1. Content & Knowledge Management Leadership
  • Direct the development of bilingual enablement content — including training curricula, product guides, sales playbooks, and partner portal resources — in partnership with the Content team.
  • Establish and maintain content governance standards, version control processes, and distribution channels to ensure the dealer network always has access to accurate, up-to-date resources.
  • Build internal knowledge management systems for the PAR Enablement function, enabling institutional knowledge to scale with the team.
  1. Performance Management & Continuous Improvement
  • Define, own, and report on key performance indicators (KPIs) for dealer enablement programs, including onboarding completion, training engagement, partner readiness scores, and program ROI.
  • Present regular program performance reviews to PAR leadership with data-driven insights, trend analysis, and clear recommendations for program evolution.
  • Foster a culture of continuous improvement within the enablement function, regularly benchmarking against industry best practices and incorporating learnings into program design.
  1. Team & Capability Building
  • Provide mentorship and guidance to more junior team members or cross-functional contributors involved in enablement activities.
  • Develop the PAR team’s overall enablement capability by introducing frameworks, tools, and best practices that raise the standard of partner program management across the organization.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor Degree in related field
  • Minimum 5 years of professional experience in program management, sales enablement, partner/channel operations, or a closely related cross-functional leadership role. Experience managing programs with significant cross-functional scope and measurable business impact is required.
  • Program Leadership: Demonstrated track record of owning and delivering complex, multi-stakeholder programs end-to-end — from strategy through execution — in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment.
  • Bilingual: in Mandarin Chinese (written and verbal) is required, as this role involves frequent communication with internal teams and dealer partners.
  • Cross-functional Influence: Proven ability to lead without direct authority — aligning stakeholders, driving alignment across functions, and influencing outcomes at multiple levels of the organization.
  • Strategic Thinking: Ability to develop and articulate a clear enablement strategy, connect it to business objectives, and translate it into actionable, measurable programs.
  • Communication & Presentation: Excellent written and verbal communication skills; able to present complex program updates and strategic recommendations to senior leadership with clarity and confidence.
  • Work Ethic: Self-directed and resilient; comfortable setting priorities, managing trade-offs, and leading through ambiguity in a high-growth startup environment.
  • Technical Skills: Proficiency in Microsoft PowerPoint, Word, and Excel; familiarity with project management tools (e.g., Notion, Asana, or similar); comfort with AI productivity tools.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Sales Enablement or Channel Enablement Leadership: Prior experience leading a sales enablement or partner enablement function, particularly in a dealer, distributor, or franchise channel model.
  • China Market Expertise: Deep familiarity with China-based dealer or partner ecosystems, including business norms, regulatory considerations, and communication expectations.
  • Content & Curriculum Development: Demonstrated experience building bilingual training programs, sales playbooks, or partner certification curricula at scale.
  • Cross-border Business Leadership: Experience leading programs in US-China cross-border business environments or managing enablement across multiple geographies.
  • Industry Fit: Background in automotive, EV, robotics, smart hardware, or consumer technology industries.
  • Big Firm Exposure: Experience at a top-tier professional services, consulting, or large enterprise organization (e.g., Big 4, MBB, or Fortune 500) in a program management or commercial capacity.
  • Legal & Compliance Familiarity: Working knowledge of commercial agreements, dealer contracts, or regulatory compliance requirements in a B2B or channel context.

Salary Range:

($90,000-$105,000 DOE), plus benefits and incentive plans

Perks + Benefits

  • Healthcare + dental + vision benefits (Free for you/discounted for family)
  • 401(k) options
  • Casual dress code + relaxed work environment
  • Culturally diverse, progressive atmosphere
  • “Soul of Faraday” community outreach team

Title: Partner Enablement Manager
Description:
A little about us…Fleetio is a modern software platform that helps thousands of organizations worldwide manage their fleet operations. Transportation technology is a hot market, and we’re leading the charge with raving fans and new customers signing up every day. We raised $450M in our Series D funding round in March of 2025 and are on an exciting trajectory as a company. Fleetio is also a proud founding member of the Rails Foundation!

More about our team and company:

  • Fleetio overview video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YoXyXTFWbkg
  • Our careers page: https://www.fleetio.com/careers

About the Role

Fleetio is looking for a Partner Enablement Manager to build and run the programs that make our reseller partners — Fleet Management Companies (FMCs), telematics providers, and VARs — genuinely effective at selling, implementing, and supporting Fleetio. This is a program-management-first role with a strong enablement mandate: you'll own the full onboarding curriculum for new partners and, just as importantly, you'll be the reason existing partners stay current as Fleetio's product, pricing, and messaging evolve. Enablement here isn't a one-time event — it's an ongoing operating rhythm.

You'll be the connective tissue between our reseller partners and Fleetio's internal functions — Sales, Marketing, Product, and Support — translating what's changing inside Fleetio into what partners need to know, do, or say differently, and translating what partners need back into clear asks for the right internal team.

What You'll Do

  • Own and run structured onboarding programs for newly signed reseller partners, covering technical/platform onboarding, sales training, value-selling methodology, and partner marketing enablement — able to run multiple onboarding cohorts concurrently without dropping details.
  • Build and maintain the partner enablement curriculum: onboarding tracks, certification/training materials, playbooks, battlecards, and value-selling frameworks tailored to each partner type (FMC, telematics, VAR).
  • Establish an ongoing enablement cadence beyond onboarding — proactively pushing updates to partner-facing teams whenever there's a platform release, new feature, pricing/packaging change, or updated marketing messaging, so partners are never selling or supporting an outdated version of Fleetio.
  • Act as the internal conduit for partner enablement needs: gather requirements from partners, route them to the right function (Product, Marketing, Sales Enablement, Support), and close the loop once addressed.
  • Partner closely with the Partner Account Management team to identify enablement gaps surfaced through partner health, ramp speed, or performance data, and build programs to close them.
  • Enhance and maintain partner-facing training content and documentation (onboarding guides, LMS content, recorded trainings, quick-reference materials) in a consistent, on-brand format.
  • Track and report on enablement effectiveness — onboarding completion/time-to-ramp, training engagement, certification rates — and use that data to continuously improve programs.
  • Coordinate cross-functional stakeholders (Product, Marketing, Support, Legal where relevant) to ensure enablement content stays accurate and is delivered on time around major releases or go-to-market changes.
  • Support partner-facing events (kickoffs, QBRs, partner summits) with enablement content and materials.
  • Maintain accurate, up-to-date records of partner enablement status (onboarding stage, certifications completed, training gaps) in Salesforce/partner tracking tools.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of experience in partner enablement, sales enablement, channel program management, or partner onboarding — ideally in B2B SaaS, fleet, telematics, or a related vertical.
  • Proven ability to design and run structured onboarding/enablement programs from scratch, not just execute an existing playbook.
  • Exceptionally polished and organized — comfortable managing multiple onboarding programs and partner cohorts simultaneously, each at a different stage, without losing precision or missing deadlines.
  • Strong program management instincts: able to build a repeatable operating cadence (not just one-off training events) and hold cross-functional stakeholders accountable to it.
  • Comfortable operating across the full enablement spectrum — technical/platform onboarding, sales training, value-selling methodology, and partner marketing enablement — rather than specializing in just one lane.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills; able to translate internal product/pricing/messaging changes into clear, partner-ready content.
  • Experience building training content, playbooks, or certification programs (LMS experience a plus).
  • Comfortable acting as a cross-functional conduit — confident engaging Product, Marketing, Sales, and Support to get partner needs addressed.

Title: Head of Supplier Enablement
Description:
Change the way the world travels

Join the GetYourGuide journey to connect people with unforgettable travel experiences around the world. Millions look to us for unique activities they can trust, and it’s all powered by our commitment to make every single journey extraordinary - including yours. 

Ready to unlock your potential with a community of fellow explorers? Find your next role at our Berlin HQ or one of our local offices around the globe, from New York to Bangkok. Head to getyourguide.careers to take the first step.

Team mission

As Head of Supplier Enablement (Success), you will own  the global support engine suppliers rely on to run their business on GetYourGuide and its transformation into a true supplier success. Your teams make sure suppliers get fast, reliable, correct operational support – whether or not they have an account manager – and that complex issues are owned, escalated, and resolved end‑to‑end. You will continue the evolution of this ops function into a supplier success function.

You will lead three teams:

  • Supplier Experience – daily supplier support and experience
  • Principal Model Operations – execution of Principal Model practices and standards(inventory acquisition)
  • Connectivity Support – support for APIs and connectivity partners

You report into the Director of Care, act as a peer lead within the department  and work closely with Product and Supply to reduce friction for suppliers and protect marketplace health.

Your mission

  • Own the supplier support engine
    • Own the end‑to‑end supplier support experience across all regions and channels.
    • Set and manage KPIs (e.g. response times, First contact resolution, quality, supplier CSAT/NPS, backlog health).
    • Ensure consistent support for all suppliers, regardless of service model.

  • Drive operational excellence and escalations
    • Act as the senior escalation point for major supplier operational issues (Principal Model, payouts, policies, incidents, connectivity).
    • Improve processes, playbooks, and policies to handle recurring issues efficiently and consistently.
    • Build monitoring and reporting to spot trends early and trigger cross‑functional fixes.
    • Measurably contribute to supplier retention and activation
  • Lead Supplier Experience, Principal Model Ops, and Connectivity Support ( 3 teams reporting to you)
    • Set clear goals, ownership, and standards for each team.
    • Ensure strong routing, case ownership, and handovers between teams and other Care functions.
    • Keep documentation, workflows, and standards simple, current, and easy to use.

  • Partner cross‑functionally
    • Work with Supply, Sales, Product, Finance, Legal, and Communications on changes that impact suppliers, ensuring the support engine is ready. You are comfortable asserting influence without structural authority.
    • Represent supplier operational needs in new product, policy, and marketplace initiatives.
    • Provide regular, simple reporting on supplier support health and key risks to senior leadership.

  • Lead leaders and build culture
    • Lead and develop people managers and senior Independent Contributors; build leadership capacity in your teams.
    • Foster a high‑trust, high‑accountability culture focused on ownership, simplicity, and continuous improvement.
    • Champion diversity and inclusion within your teams.

Your toolkit

  • Experience
    • 8+ years in operations, customer success, or service delivery, with proven experience in a two-sided marketplace or platform business, managing supply-side partners rather than enterprise accounts alone.
    •  4+ years leading leads. managing people who themselves manage teams, across a multi-team organization of comparable scale (30+ people).
    • Proven track record running complex support/ops functions with clear KPIs and continuous improvement.
    • Proven experience shifting a function from reactive to proactive, with measurable outcomes in retention, activation, or supplier satisfaction
  • Leadership & Mindset
    • Empathetic, hands‑on people leader with a high performance bar.
    • Strong operations mindset: comfortable with queues, SLAs, workflows, capacity planning, and process design.
    • Able to operate in ambiguity and create clarity, focus, and simple priorities for teams.

  • Analytical & Execution Skills
    • Strong analytical skills; confident using data and dashboards to understand performance and set priorities.
    • Experience standardizing processes and driving operational improvements across regions or functions.
    • Familiarity with support tooling, automation, in operations.
    •  Hands-on, current use of AI tools in your own workflow, able to speak concretely about specific tools and problems solved.

  • Collaboration & Communication
    • Excellent stakeholder management across Product, Tech, Supply and regional teams.
    •  Comfortable quantifying the business impact of your work in specific, concrete terms, not just describing the process behind it.
    • Clear, concise communicator in English, able to adapt from frontline to C‑level audiences.

Extras that give you an edge

  • Marketplace/Travel Marketplace industry experience
  • Sales team particular account management experience

  • Work from anywhere in the world for 30 days per year

Title: Senior Backend Engineer, Platform Enablement
Description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As a Senior Backend Engineer, Performance Enablement, you'll make performance testing and analysis easier for engineering teams to adopt and own. You'll build platforms, tooling, guidance, and artificial intelligence-assisted workflows that help teams identify performance risks during development and before they roll changes out to production.

We're moving from a hands-on consulting model to a self-service model. Service teams own their performance tests, analysis, thresholds, and evidence. We provide the paved road, documentation, skills, and expert support for challenging problems and new capabilities.

This is a backend and platform engineering role with room to grow in scope and influence. You'll help shape how Performance Enablement supports engineering teams, using artificial intelligence thoughtfully to accelerate design, implementation, testing, debugging, documentation, and automation.

You'll support work such as:

  • Enabling modular feature teams, including Orbit and Artifact Registry, to run performance testing through their own development and continuous integration workflows
  • Building reusable performance tooling, including component-level testing, load testing, performance analysis, and artificial intelligence-assisted engineering skills
  • Improving performance results, reporting, and trend visibility so teams can make informed decisions from their own evidence
  • Establishing the documentation, templates, and guidance needed to expand self-service adoption across research and development

What you’ll do

  • Build and evolve reusable backend platforms and tooling for performance testing and analysis.
  • Create self-service workflows, documentation, templates, diagnostics, and artificial intelligence skills that reduce the need for bespoke support.
  • Use development practices that apply artificial intelligence to accelerate implementation, testing, debugging, and technical documentation.
  • Influence engineering teams to make performance testing part of normal development and release preparation.
  • Turn early hands-on engagements into generalized capabilities that many teams can adopt independently.
  • Provide technical expertise for difficult performance questions, tooling enhancements, and new platform capabilities.

What you’ll bring

  • Experience building backend or platform software.
  • Experience building internal platforms or developer-facing tooling.
  • Experience partnering with development teams to improve their day-to-day workflows.
  • Experience using development practices that apply artificial intelligence across the software lifecycle.
  • Experience with software performance, such as performance analysis, optimization, benchmarking, or leading performance-related improvements.
  • Practical experience with Kubernetes, k6, and Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud Platform, or similar cloud infrastructure.
  • Experience building durable solutions that support broad adoption using systems thinking.
  • Communicate clearly in writing and influence teams without direct authority.

About the team

Performance Enablement is part of Platform Enablement within Developer Experience and Infrastructure Platforms. We help GitLab teams make performance part of the software lifecycle.

Our goal is to make performance a shared responsibility of service-owning teams while providing a strong platform and center of expertise when teams need help. We work asynchronously, collaborate broadly across research and development, and focus on building capabilities that scale beyond individual team engagements.

Title: GTM Enablement Manager
Description:
About Glean:
 
Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles.
 
At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level.
 
Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality.
 
If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more - deeply embedded where people get things done. You’ll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company.

About the Role:

Glean is seeking a Product Enablement Manager to sit at the intersection of Product, Product Marketing, and GTM Enablement. In this role, you will be the connective tissue between a fast‑moving Work AI platform and our customer‑facing teams, turning launches, roadmap bets, and complex product capabilities into clear, usable narratives, workflows, and trainings that drive adoption and revenue impact across the go‑to‑market organization.

You will also be a key builder and collaborator on our AI‑first enablement vision: using Glean and agents to turn fragmented launch signals into role‑aware guidance, in‑flow practice, and visible readiness signals. Instead of relying on point‑in‑time trainings alone, you’ll design and build an always‑on, AI‑assisted enablement system that keeps GTM teams current on what changed, why it matters, and how to use it in real deals. For this role, you must be excited to use AI to build new workflows and processes from a first principles, AI-first approach. 

You will: 

  • Own the GTM‑facing layer of product enablement, translating release notes, specs, and technical documentation into “what this means for the field” guidance: when to use new capabilities, which personas and use cases to target, and what proof points and stories to lean on.
  • Build and maintain a scalable product enablement program for GTM teams (Initially the focus will be Sales, but can expand and overlap to SEs/SAs, Customer Outcomes, Support, Partnerships), covering launches, core product foundations, advanced AI capabilities, and platform‑level narratives.
  • Design and deliver high‑impact enablement sessions on new features, packages, and workflows, with a focus on active practice, demos, and application to real customer scenarios, not just slides.
  • Partner closely with Product, Product Marketing, Competitive, Sales, Technical Enablement, and Customer Outcomes to ensure GTM teams are launch‑ready for Tier 1 and Tier 2 releases, with clear talk tracks, demo flows, objection handling, and enablement bundles.
  • Work with Field and Technical Enablement peers to embed product learning into broader programs such as onboarding, certifications, deal coaching, and manager enablement, so product knowledge shows up in how we sell and support, not just in standalone trainings.
  • Design and operate an AI‑first “launch‑to‑enable” loop: help define how product changes (release notes, docs, support patterns) become structured launch briefs, role‑based guidance, and in‑flow practice using Glean and agents as the backbone.
  • Partner with Technical Enablement and AI product teams to build and maintain AI‑powered enablement surfaces (e.g., role‑aware “what’s new” views, browser‑overlay guidance, agent‑driven labs) that deliver just‑in‑time coaching in the tools where GTM already works.
  • Act as a champion and co‑designer of our AI‑first enablement system by collaborating on 30‑/60‑/90‑day MVPs (e.g., an enablement‑owned launch hub, role‑aware readiness signals, agent‑assisted certifications) and feeding field feedback back into our AI enablement roadmap.

About you:

  • 5+ years in B2B SaaS go‑to‑market roles such as product enablement, sales/revenue enablement, product marketing, solutions engineering, or similar roles with heavy product ownership and field interaction.
  • Proven track record translating complex, technical, or AI‑heavy product concepts into simple, compelling narratives, talk tracks, and trainings that GTM teams actually use in the field.
  • Strong familiarity with modern value‑based sales methodologies (e.g., Command of the Message, MEDDICC/MEDDPICC, or similar) and how product stories must align to business problems, outcomes, and proof points, not just features.
  • Solid understanding of how AI products work at a conceptual level (e.g., large language models, retrieval‑augmented generation, knowledge graphs, security and permissions), even if you are not a deep technical expert, and curiosity about how Work AI changes selling and customer workflows.
  • Hands‑on experience using AI tools to design, deliver, or scale enablement, for example, using AI to draft curricula, build interactive labs, power self‑serve Q&A, or run lightweight, agent‑assisted certifications.
  • Strong project and program management skills: able to juggle multiple launches, stakeholder groups, and content streams while keeping timelines, dependencies, and success metrics clear.
  • Comfortable operating in ambiguity and a high‑change environment, you can keep up with a fast product release cadence, find signal in the noise, and quickly determine what the field actually needs versus what would be “nice to have.”
  • A systems thinker who gets excited about turning one‑off trainings into durable, AI‑powered enablement experiences, you think in terms of loops, signals, and workflows, not just events.

Location

  • This role is hybrid (4 days a week in one of our office locations NYC, Nashville, SF, Mountain View)

Compensation & Benefits:

The standard base salary range for this position is $140,000 - $187,000 annually. Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for variable compensation, equity, and benefits.

We offer a comprehensive benefits package including competitive compensation, Medical, Vision, and Dental coverage, generous time-off policy, and the opportunity to contribute to your 401k plan to support your long-term goals. When you join, you'll receive a home office improvement stipend, as well as an annual education and wellness stipends to support your growth and wellbeing. 

We are a diverse bunch of people and we want to continue to attract and retain a diverse range of people into our organization. We're committed to an inclusive and diverse company. We do not discriminate based on gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion, civil or family status, age, disability, or race.

 #LI-HYBRID

 
AI-First Mindset at Glean:
 
At Glean, AI fluency is core to how we work and we're committed to ensuring every new hire feels confident integrating AI into their everyday work. As part of the interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about, design, and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today — prior Glean experience isn't required.

In this role, you will be the connective tissue between a fast‑moving Work AI platform and our customer‑facing teams, turning launches, roadmap bets, and complex product capabilities into clear, usable narratives, workflows, and trainings that drive adoption and revenue impact across the go‑to‑market organization.

You will also be a key builder and collaborator on our AI‑first enablement vision: using Glean and agents to turn fragmented launch signals into role‑aware guidance, in‑flow practice, and visible readiness signals. Instead of relying on point‑in‑time trainings alone, you’ll design and build an always‑on, AI‑assisted enablement system that keeps GTM teams current on what changed, why it matters, and how to use it in real deals. For this role, you must be excited to use AI to build new workflows and processes from a first principles, AI-first approach. 

You will: 

  • Own the GTM‑facing layer of product enablement, translating release notes, specs, and technical documentation into “what this means for the field” guidance: when to use new capabilities, which personas and use cases to target, and what proof points and stories to lean on.
  • Build and maintain a scalable product enablement program for GTM teams (Initially the focus will be Sales, but can expand and overlap to SEs/SAs, Customer Outcomes, Support, Partnerships), covering launches, core product foundations, advanced AI capabilities, and platform‑level narratives.
  • Design and deliver high‑impact enablement sessions on new features, packages, and workflows, with a focus on active practice, demos, and application to real customer scenarios, not just slides.
  • Partner closely with Product, Product Marketing, Competitive, Sales, Technical Enablement, and Customer Outcomes to ensure GTM teams are launch‑ready for Tier 1 and Tier 2 releases, with clear talk tracks, demo flows, objection handling, and enablement bundles.
  • Work with Field and Technical Enablement peers to embed product learning into broader programs such as onboarding, certifications, deal coaching, and manager enablement, so product knowledge shows up in how we sell and support, not just in standalone trainings.
  • Design and operate an AI‑first “launch‑to‑enable” loop: help define how product changes (release notes, docs, support patterns) become structured launch briefs, role‑based guidance, and in‑flow practice using Glean and agents as the backbone.
  • Partner with Technical Enablement and AI product teams to build and maintain AI‑powered enablement surfaces (e.g., role‑aware “what’s new” views, browser‑overlay guidance, agent‑driven labs) that deliver just‑in‑time coaching in the tools where GTM already works.
  • Act as a champion and co‑designer of our AI‑first enablement system by collaborating on 30‑/60‑/90‑day MVPs (e.g., an enablement‑owned launch hub, role‑aware readiness signals, agent‑assisted certifications) and feeding field feedback back into our AI enablement roadmap.

About you:

  • 5+ years in B2B SaaS go‑to‑market roles such as product enablement, sales/revenue enablement, product marketing, solutions engineering, or similar roles with heavy product ownership and field interaction.
  • Proven track record translating complex, technical, or AI‑heavy product concepts into simple, compelling narratives, talk tracks, and trainings that GTM teams actually use in the field.
  • Strong familiarity with modern value‑based sales methodologies (e.g., Command of the Message, MEDDICC/MEDDPICC, or similar) and how product stories must align to business problems, outcomes, and proof points, not just features.
  • Solid understanding of how AI products work at a conceptual level (e.g., large language models, retrieval‑augmented generation, knowledge graphs, security and permissions), even if you are not a deep technical expert, and curiosity about how Work AI changes selling and customer workflows.
  • Hands‑on experience using AI tools to design, deliver, or scale enablement, for example, using AI to draft curricula, build interactive labs, power self‑serve Q&A, or run lightweight, agent‑assisted certifications.
  • Strong project and program management skills: able to juggle multiple launches, stakeholder groups, and content streams while keeping timelines, dependencies, and success metrics clear.
  • Comfortable operating in ambiguity and a high‑change environment, you can keep up with a fast product release cadence, find signal in the noise, and quickly determine what the field actually needs versus what would be “nice to have.”
  • A systems thinker who gets excited about turning one‑off trainings into durable, AI‑powered enablement experiences, you think in terms of loops, signals, and workflows, not just events.

Location

  • This role is hybrid (4 days a week in one of our office locations NYC, Nashville, SF, Mountain View)

Compensation & Benefits:

The standard base salary range for this position is $140,000 - $187,000 annually. Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for variable compensation, equity, and benefits.

We offer a comprehensive benefits package including competitive compensation, Medical, Vision, and Dental coverage, generous time-off policy, and the opportunity to contribute to your 401k plan to support your long-term goals. When you join, you'll receive a home office improvement stipend, as well as an annual education and wellness stipends to support your growth and wellbeing.

Title: GTM Enablement Manager
Description:
About Glean:
 
Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles.
 
At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level.
 
Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality.
 
If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more - deeply embedded where people get things done. You’ll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company.

Title: AI Knowledge Analyst I
Description:
Role Summary

The AI Knowledge Analyst is a member of the Customer Care and Managed Services team, responsible for ensuring the knowledge ecosystems that power GHX's operations and AI platforms are accurate, well-governed, and continuously improving.  This role works closely with leadership, SMEs, data scientists, and operational teams to identify content gaps, manage knowledge lifecycles, and translate business needs into structured, AI-ready information assets. The AI Knowledge Analyst is equally comfortable working through a detailed content audit and presenting a structured recommendation to leadership.  Strong organizational skills, clear communication, and a bias for action are required. This is a role for someone who treats knowledge gaps as solvable problems and can move from gap identification to resolution with minimal direction.

Core Focus Areas

Knowledge Governance & Lifecycle Management

Maintain, organize, and govern the knowledge assets that support Customer Care and Managed Services teams. This includes managing intake, triage, and routing of knowledge requests; driving SME review cycles; and ensuring content is accurate, current, and ready for both human use and AI ingestion.

AI Knowledge Readiness

Identify, structure, and groom content that feeds GHX's AI platform. Partner with AI and data teams to ensure knowledge assets are formatted, accurate, and optimized for ingestion. Monitor AI solution performance and drive content improvements that translate into measurable efficiency gains.

Roles & Responsibilities

Knowledge Management & Content Quality

  • Manage the intake, triage, and routing of knowledge-related requests from operational teams.
  • Maintain content lifecycle through SME review checkpoints — flagging material for update, review, or archival on a consistent cadence.
  • Identify obsolete, duplicate, or conflicting content and drive resolution through appropriate stakeholders.
  • Conduct knowledge audits and implement improvement cycles based on performance data and stakeholder feedback.
  • Translate operational knowledge into structured, AI-ingestible formats ensuring accuracy, consistency, and taxonomy compliance.

AI Knowledge Readiness & Technology

  • Structure and groom knowledge content for ingestion into GHX's AI platforms; ensure format, tagging, and taxonomy standards are met.
  • Monitor AI platform performance related to knowledge quality; recommend and track content-driven improvements.
  • Partner with data scientists and AI developers to understand ingestion requirements and close content gaps.
  • Stay current on trends in AI knowledge management, large language model content requirements, and KM tooling.

Process Improvement & Analysis

  • Analyze and document knowledge workflows, identifying gaps or structural issues that reduce content usability or AI accuracy.
  • Interpret usage data, feedback trends, and engagement metrics to recommend improvement opportunities.
  • Support implementation of governance standards, taxonomy structures, and documentation templates.
  • Learn and apply Lean/Six Sigma and knowledge-centered service (KCS) frameworks where applicable.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement

  • Partner with SMEs, operational leaders, and AI teams to promote adoption of AI-enabled knowledge systems.
  • Provide end-user training and support on knowledge tools, systems, and updated content resources.
  • Collect stakeholder requirements and develop content solutions that meet operational team needs.
  • Present knowledge health findings and recommendations to leadership with clear next steps.

Required Skills

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to tailor message by audience.
  • Familiarity with knowledge management systems (Confluence/Atlassian, Salesforce Knowledge, ServiceNow, or equivalent).
  • Analytical mindset with ability to interpret usage data and translate findings into action.
  • Detail-oriented with ability to manage multiple knowledge domains and adjust priorities as needed.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft 365 (Word, Excel, SharePoint, Forms); CRM familiarity a plus (Salesforce preferred).
  • Self-directed learner who identifies gaps and takes initiative to close them.
  • Understanding of how content structure and taxonomy affect AI/ML model performance preferred.

Education & Experience

  • 2+ years of related experience in knowledge management, operations enablement, content governance, or business analysis.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and maintaining content for both human consumption (training, SOPs) and machine ingestion (AI platforms, knowledge bases).
  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Information Management, Organizational Development, or related field; or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Change management or KM certification (Prosci, KCS, ACMP) a plus.

We bring together healthcare providers and manufacturers and distributors in North America and Europe - who rely on smart, secure healthcare-focused technology and comprehensive data to automate their business processes and make more informed decisions.

It is our passion and vision for a more operationally efficient healthcare supply chain, helping organizations reduce - not shift - the cost of doing business, paving the way to delivering patient care more effectively.
