If you receive communication from any other domain, please be cautious, as it is likely fraudulent.

Title: Learning & Knowledge Systems Lead
Description: Learning & Knowledge Systems Lead Harper is an AI-native commercial insurance company in San Francisco. We're not bolting AI onto insurance — we're rebuilding the entire business as software, on a simple bet: turning expert human judgment into compute is one of the largest transitions left to make, and a trillion-dollar industry still run 90% by hand is the place to prove it. We've grown ~100x in the last year and we move at that speed — on-site, in person, long days, very high standards. Almost no one joins Harper for insurance ; they join to build the company that replaces how it works. The role in one line You turn the judgment locked inside Harper's best operators into AI-legible knowledge — living docs, decision logs, and retrievable skills the agents can actually call — and you get the rest of the company running against it. Why this role exists now AI doesn't understand a company by default. It works only when the business is documented clearly enough for a system to retrieve the right context, recognize the workflow, handle the edge case, and escalate when human judgment is required. Right now most of how Harper operates lives in people's heads: how a top rep sequences quotes, how service handles the weird bind, how market routing actually works, what a customer means when they push back. That holds at small scale. It breaks at ~1,000 new customers a month. Every undocumented process is a future failure mode; every AI-generated playbook that dies in a chat thread is throughput left on the floor. The next bottleneck here isn't engineering. It's knowledge — and how fast people can absorb it. This role removes that bottleneck. Be clear about what this is not. This is not corporate L&D. No LMS, no slide decks, no e-learning project, no making-the-Notion-pretty. This is knowledge engineering: sit with operators, extract how they actually think, and turn it into structured knowledge a human and a model can use. What you'll do Two tracks, running in parallel, at the intersection of Operations, Engineering, and RevOps. Build the operating memory. Embed with sales, intake, service, placements, and renewals. Sit with operators, listen to calls, shadow workflows, and document what people "just know." Turn transcripts, Slack threads, Looms, and one-off explanations into source-of-truth docs, decision logs, playbooks, process maps, glossaries, and system-boundary docs (what each internal system does, where one stops and the next begins, and what gets misread). Graduate stabilized rules into skills the agents can call , and partner with engineering on refresh automations so docs stay alive instead of going stale. Hunt the edge cases — reworks, escalations, stale quotes, market follow-ups, binder/payment gaps, customer confusion — and write them down before they bite again. Get the company to run against it. When a rich AI-generated playbook lands, distill it into an executable plan: named owners, the first three moves, a rollout cadence and date. The plan doesn't run itself; you make it run. Build the onboarding paths and setup scripts that get a new hire into Cursor, Claude Code, and the harness within a week. Run cohort rollouts, drive adoption, and make activity visible — we should know who's actually in the harness. Shape meetings in real time so they produce useful artifacts: decisions, owners, definitions, edge cases, open questions, next steps. When the same problem shows up three times, turn it into a playbook, a QA check, a skill, or a product requirement. You'll work directly with the CEO when extraction calls for it. Who you are An exceptional writer and synthesizer. You can take a messy transcript to a clear operating doc, and a clear doc to something a team actually executes against. AI-native in practice — this is the bar. Not "I use ChatGPT." You have taste for when an output is structurally wrong, not just stylistically off. You prompt for extraction (decisions, contradictions, owners, edge cases), not just summarization. You know good output depends on good context, and you engineer that context upstream. Cursor, Claude Code, MCP servers, agent memory files, Granola, structured prompting are tools you reach for without thinking. Genuinely curious about how organizations work, and happy to sit with operators to find out. Structured but not bureaucratic. You care whether documentation changes behavior, not whether it looks polished. Able to operate in chaos without becoming chaotic. Low-ego, persistent, and allergic to "someone should probably document that." Backgrounds that can work (the skill matters more than the title): modern enablement at an AI-native company, qualitative/academic research, ethnography, instructional or curriculum design, knowledge management, product ops, technical writing, research ops, implementation, chief of staff roles, library and information science, AI ops / human-in-the-loop work, or startup operations where the systems were messy and someone had to make them legible. Requirements 3–8 years in a relevant field (see above). Exceptional written communication and strong information-architecture instincts. Real AI-tool fluency in practice: Cursor, Claude Code, MCP servers, agent memory files, Granola, structured prompting, AI-assisted synthesis. Demonstrated ability to interview stakeholders, extract operational detail, and turn messy conversations into clear decisions and source-of-truth docs. A track record of running an adoption rollout that actually changed how a team worked. Comfort in a fast-moving, ambiguous startup. Based in San Francisco or willing to relocate. Nice to have: experience at an AI-native or dev-tools company; authoring Claude/agent skills or similar capability modules; RAG/search systems, data labeling, evals on knowledge systems, or human-in-the-loop QA; working with engineering on living-doc refresh automations; translating operator feedback into product requirements; taxonomy/metadata/content governance; insurance, fintech, B2B services, or another high-volume operational environment. The reality On-site in San Francisco, in the building with the operators whose knowledge you're extracting — this work doesn't happen remotely. The hours are long and the standards are high, because a rebuild this large doesn't happen part-time. The people who thrive here want it that way. If you want to walk into ambiguity, find the hidden logic, and turn it into systems the whole company runs against at AI speed, this is the seat. Compensation & benefits Salary: $110,000–$170,000 + performance bonuses & equity Location: San Francisco, in-office hours matching the rest of the company. Schedule: Monday–Friday, in-office hours that match the rest of the company. The hours are long. Benefits: Uber commuter benefits; breakfast, lunch, and dinner provided; snacks/drinks/coffee daily; free gym membership; health, dental, and vision insurance. Process One to two screening calls — alignment on mission, pace, and role fit. On-site super day — sit with operators, review transcripts, meet product and engineering, and show how you think.

Title: Staff Software Engineer - RnD Enablement.
Description: The Opportunity As a Staff Software Engineer on Hinge Health’s Service Enablement team , you will build the platforms, services, and engineering practices that other teams at Hinge Health rely on to ship software safely and quickly. Service Enablement treats Hinge Health engineers as its customers. The team builds paved roads, automation, and platform capabilities in developer experience, cloud and service platforms, reliability, observability, security, CI/CD, and AI/ML enablement. The goal is to remove friction, improve operational maturity, and make the default path the easiest one for product and infrastructure teams. This is a hands-on Staff Engineer role. You will write production code, lead architecture and design reviews, participate in operational response, and coach engineers toward stronger technical ownership. Expect to turn broad engineering needs into technical strategy, lead initiatives that span several teams, and set standards that get adopted beyond your own pod. You will work closely with Engineering, Product, Security, Data, ML, and Infrastructure to balance delivery speed against reliability, security, cost, and maintainability. As Hinge Health expands its use of AI across the software development lifecycle and the care platform, you will also help make those AI and ML workloads reliable, cost efficient, and responsibly run. The problems in this role are foundational. Fixing them makes every engineering team at Hinge Health more effective, and the software they ship helps make healthcare more accessible and affordable. What You’ll Accomplish Own a multi-quarter technical roadmap for one or more Service Enablement domains, based on what internal engineering teams actually need. Lead architecture and design for highly available, secure, and maintainable platforms and services that cross pod boundaries. Build and maintain paved roads for service development, deployment, observability, reliability, and operational ownership. Improve developer productivity with automation, reusable frameworks, self-service workflows, and documentation that people can follow. Set practical standards for SLOs, alerting, incident response, capacity management, service ownership, and production readiness. Work with product and engineering teams to run AI and ML workloads reliably and cost efficiently, including inference systems where they make sense. De-risk ambiguous problems with prototypes, spikes, and experiments that produce measurable results. Write and lead RFCs, design reviews, and technical decision records. Explain trade-offs clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders. Take part in production operations and eliminate recurring failure modes with systemic fixes. Deliver large initiatives from strategy through production adoption, and measure the result: platform adoption, developer productivity, reliability, cost, or reduced operational toil. Mentor engineers, coach senior engineers into broader technical leadership, help with hiring, and raise the bar for engineering practice across the organization. Hinge Health Hybrid Model We believe that remote work and in-person work have their own advantages and disadvantages, and we want to be able to leverage the best of both worlds. Employees in hybrid roles are required to be in the office 3 days/week. This is a Bengaluru-based role that involves regular interaction and collaboration with Hinge Health colleagues in San Francisco, CA. Time zones: San Francisco is in the Pacific Time Zone, which is 12 hours and 30 minutes behind India Standard Time (e.g., 8am in San Francisco is 8:30pm in Bengaluru). Hours: Applicants should be open to meetings in the late evening following India Standard Time to align with San Francisco working hours (8:30 pm - 10:30pm IST). Basic Qualifications Bachelor’s Degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Engineering or related technical field 10+ years of professional software development, or equivalent depth building and operating production systems. 4+ years with at least one modern programming language such as TypeScript/JavaScript,Go, Python. 4+ years across the full software development lifecycle: design, implementation, testing, deployment, and production operations. 4+years of experience in cloud infrastructure and containerized workloads such as AWS, Kubernetes, or EKS. Experience in software design and distributed systems fundamentals: reliability, scalability, performance, failure modes, and API or platform contracts. Experience operating production systems, including observability, incident response, root cause analysis, and reliability improvement. Experience treating internal platforms and developer experience as products, with attention to usability, adoption, and measurable outcomes. Experience with using AI tools such as Github copilot, Cursor, Claude etc Preferred Qualifications Experience building internal developer platforms, service templates, golden paths, CI/CD systems, or self-service infrastructure. Experience with platform security, identity and access management, compliance controls, or secure-by-default engineering. Experience supporting AI/ML teams with inference infrastructure, model serving platforms, evaluation workflows, or cost and performance optimization. Experience defining and maintaining SLOs and SLAs, using error budgets, service-health metrics, alerting, on-call practices, incident response, and root-cause analysis to improve reliability. Experience with event-driven systems, workflow orchestration, service networking, or large-scale data and messaging infrastructure. Experience defining platform metrics such as adoption, deployment lead time, change failure rate, availability, developer satisfaction, or operational toil. Experience mentoring senior engineers or acting as technical lead for a platform migration, modernization effort, or organization-wide launch. Experience working in healthcare, privacy-sensitive, regulated, or otherwise high-trust environments. About Hinge Health At Hinge Health, we’re using technology to scale and automate the delivery of healthcare – starting with musculoskeletal (MSK) conditions, which affect over 1.7 billion people worldwide. With an AI-powered human-centered care model, Hinge Health leverages cutting-edge technology to improve outcomes, experiences and costs to help people move beyond their pain. The platform addresses a broad spectrum of MSK care – from acute injury, to chronic pain, to post-surgical rehabilitation – through personalized, evidence-based care. As the preferred partner to 50+ health plans, PBMs and other ecosystem partners, Hinge Health is available to over 20 million people across more than 2,550 employers. The company is headquartered in San Francisco with additional offices in Montreal and Bangalore. Learn more at http://www.hingehealth.com/ What You'll Love About Us Inclusive healthcare and benefits: In addition to comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, we provide employees and their family members with Group Medical Coverage (GMC), Group Term Life Insurance (GTL), and Group Personal Accident Insurance (GPA). Well-being & Growth: We offer a lifestyle stipend to support your overall well-being, along with learning and development opportunities to help you grow both personally and professionally. Ownership: Grow with us through discounted company stock through our ESPP with easy payroll deductions. Culture & Engagement Hinge Health is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind. We make employment decisions without regards to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, veteran status, disability status, pregnancy, or any other basis protected by federal, state or local law. By submitting your application you are acknowledging we are using your personal data as outlined in the Personnel and Candidate Privacy Policy . Beware of Phishing Attempts: We've noticed an increase in phishing where fraudsters impersonate employees and send fake job offers to steal sensitive information. We'll never ask for financial details during the hiring process and only use "@ hingehealth.com " emails. If you receive a suspicious offer, stop communication and report it to the US FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center. To verify an email from our recruiting team, forward it to security@hingehealth.com .

Title: Learning and Client Enablement Associate
Description: About hyperexponential (hx) At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry, which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms. Until now, insurance has been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence. Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx. What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates. What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure. If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next. About the Client Education team Every hx customer's success depends on their teams knowing how to use our platform well - not just how to click through it, but how to build genuinely good pricing models with it. Client Education exists to make that happen. We sit at the intersection of Product, Partnerships, and Customer teams, turning new features and platform capability into training, certification, and documentation that our clients and delivery partners can actually learn from. The team owns the full learning journey: onboarding new clients, building certification pathways, producing courses and video content, and supporting partners who deliver training on our behalf. As hx's product surface has grown - Decision Engine, Pricing & Rating, Portfolio Intelligence, Submission Triage, and our AI agents - so has the volume and complexity of what we need to teach, and we're growing the team to keep pace. We're looking for a Client Education Associate to join as a core part of this effort. Your focus will be delivering technical training directly to clients and partners, and supporting the team in building and maintaining the courses and certifications that make that training possible. You'll need enough technical grounding to be credible in front of a room of actuaries and developers, and enough teaching instinct to make complex material land. What you'll be doing Deliver technical training sessions, live and online, to clients and partners - covering everything from platform fundamentals to how to build pricing models using hx's AI agents and product tooling. Build and maintain high-quality course content (online modules, video tutorials, workshop materials) that keeps pace with new product releases and evolving client needs. Support the design and delivery of certification assessments, including practical exercises where candidates build real pricing tools in the hx platform. Partner with Product, Customer, and Partnerships teams to translate new features into training material clients can actually use from day one. Contribute to our partner enablement programme, helping external delivery partners onboard and deliver hx training to a consistent standard. Help maintain and improve our course health and documentation processes, flagging content that's fallen out of date or out of line with current product naming and messaging. What you'll need to have done Delivered training, workshops, or technical explanations to a non-technical or semi-technical audience, and can point to material you've built or taught from. Studied Computer Science or a related technical discipline, or built equivalent hands-on comfort with programming languages (Python or similar) through experience. Worked hands-on with SaaS tools, APIs, or similar technical products, even without a formal software engineering background. Taken the initiative to build or improve a course, process, or piece of learning content, rather than just following someone else's structure. Communicated confidently and clearly with clients or external stakeholders, adjusting technical depth to fit the audience in front of you. Worked well in an environment where scope shifts and you're expected to figure things out rather than wait for a fully defined brief. You're unlikely to thrive here if You'd rather follow a fixed curriculum than build and adapt training material as the product changes under you. You're not comfortable being hands-on with technical concepts and tooling, even at a foundational level. You prefer working in isolation rather than pulling in context from Product, Customer, and Partnerships teams to get training right. If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you'll do your best work. We're building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us. Compensation At hx, we're committed to salary transparency. You'll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we're working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally. Because we're building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don't always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that's competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make. Equity: We offer equity across all roles at hx, making it a significant component of total compensation. Your talent partner will be able to share more details about this. Benefits £5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development. 25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total). Company pension scheme via Penfold. Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life . Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno. Private healthcare insurance through AXA. Income protection and Life Insurance. Cycle to Work Scheme Additional perks Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.). Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights. Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry. Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together. Interview Process Initial call with our Talent team to kick things off (30 minutes) Manager interview with Dom (60 minutes) Practical training assessment: build and present a short curriculum plan for a real hx feature, followed by discussion (60-90 minutes) Values interview (60 minutes) Meet the CEO We offer! Our commitment to Diversity hxer's are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive. Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure. If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team. Next steps If this opportunity resonates with you, we encourage you to apply or share it with your connections! Our dedicated talent team reviews all applications, and we promise to provide feedback regardless of the outcome. For more information about applying and to view other opportunities, you can visit our careers page. Please note that background checks will be conducted as part of the hiring process to ensure compliance with our governance policies. We handle all background checks sensitively and in full compliance with relevant regulations. All applicant data will be processed in accordance with data protection regulations and our privacy policy.

Title: Sales Enablement Lead
Description: About Juicebox Juicebox is on a mission to help teams win the talent war . In the age of AI, human ingenuity is the ultimate scarce resource. Recruiting is a zero-sum game where you either compete or lose. Teams at Ramp, Notion, and leading AI labs use Juicebox to power their hiring, alongside 5,000+ customers from early-stage startups to Fortune 500 companies. We are on the path to $100M in ARR with 20%+ monthly growth , powering thousands of searches every day and making Juicebox one of the fastest-growing AI SaaS companies in the world. Juicebox has raised over $116M in funding from lead investors including Sequoia Capital, DST Global, and NFDG. Read more about our $80M Series B here. Additional investors in Juicebox include Y Combinator, Coatue, Bond, Lux, Verified Capital, and Committed Capital. About the Role We're looking for a Sales Enablement Lead to build the systems, programs, and content that help our rapidly growing Sales team perform at its best. Today, Juicebox has a strong foundation of sales playbooks, onboarding, and training, but much of it has been built and delivered directly by Sales leadership. As our team scales, we need someone to turn what works today into a repeatable, measurable, and AI-native enablement engine. You'll initially be heavily focused on enablement: rebuilding our onboarding and ramp program, evolving our sales playbooks, leading ongoing training, and ensuring every seller has the knowledge and resources they need to win. You'll also partner closely with Product and Product Marketing to translate a fast-moving product roadmap into clear messaging, training, and collateral that sellers can immediately put into practice. This is a highly visible, hands-on IC role with significant ownership and the opportunity to define what world-class Sales Enablement looks like at Juicebox. You Will… Own and revamp our Sales onboarding program , building a scalable experience that gets new AEs and SDRs productive quickly and consistently. Build and maintain the Juicebox sales playbook , codifying our best practices across discovery, messaging, positioning, objection handling, competitive differentiation, demos, and deal execution. Create an ongoing enablement cadence across training, role-playing, certifications, call reviews, and reinforcement to continuously raise the bar for seller performance. Lead product launch enablement , partnering with Product and Product Marketing to translate new capabilities into compelling customer-facing messaging, talk tracks, training, and sales plays. Own and continuously improve our core sales materials , including the central sales deck, battlecards, talk tracks, competitive resources, and other field-facing content. Partner closely with Sales leadership to identify skill and knowledge gaps, then build targeted programs that translate into stronger execution in the field. Use data and feedback to measure enablement effectiveness , including rep readiness, ramp time, content adoption, and performance trends, and continuously iterate on programs. Rethink enablement through an AI-native lens , experimenting with AI-powered coaching, content creation, personalized learning, simulations, knowledge management, and other new approaches that make our sellers better and faster. Turn what our best sellers do into repeatable systems , ensuring that great sales execution scales as quickly as our team does. All with the goal of supporting the GTM team to close bigger deals, faster! You Have… 2+ years of experience in Sales Enablement or a closely related sales role , ideally within a high-growth B2B SaaS company. Hands-on experience building or delivering sales onboarding, training, coaching, or enablement programs. A strong understanding of the sales process and what makes sellers effective—you may have built your career in enablement or started as an AE/SDR before moving into enablement. A track record of growth and increasing ownership in your career; we're especially excited by candidates who have been promoted or consistently expanded their scope. The ability to turn complex product information into simple, compelling messaging and practical resources sellers can actually use. Excellent presentation and facilitation skills, with the confidence to lead training and coach sellers across different experience levels. Strong project management and organizational skills—you can build structure around a fast-moving organization without slowing it down. A builder mindset. You're excited to create, test, iterate, and improve rather than inherit a fully established enablement machine. A highly collaborative approach and the ability to work effectively across Sales, Product, Product Marketing, and other GTM teams. Curiosity and fluency with AI tools, with strong instincts for how AI can fundamentally improve the way enablement is built and delivered. Comfort operating in a fast-paced, high-growth environment where the product, team, and playbook are constantly evolving. Title: Senior AI Enablement Specialist - FE
Description: Are you ready to unlock intelligence? If you don’t think you meet all of the criteria below but are still interested in the job, please apply. Nobody checks every box - we’re looking for candidates that are particularly strong in a few areas, and have some interest and capabilities in others. About the Role: Kong's IT team is standing up a new capability: a small, specialized group that goes directly into business functions and builds AI into how work gets done. We call them AI Enablement Specialists — and we're looking for a senior practitioner to help lead that effort. This isn't an advisory role. You'll be hands-on with the teams you support, building tools that solve real problems and helping people develop new skills they'll carry forward. The scope is company-wide — Sales, Marketing, Finance, HR, Legal, Customer Success, and beyond. You'll have the autonomy to prioritize where your time creates the most value, and the backing of IT leadership to get things done. If you've already done this kind of work — transforming how people and teams operate through AI — and you're looking for an environment where you can do it at scale with real ownership, this is the role. What You'll Do: Spend time inside business teams to understand how they actually work — their tools, processes, pain points, and highest-priority outputs. Build AI-powered workflows, automations, and custom tools that address real bottlenecks and deliver measurable time savings. Help team members develop their own AI skills through one-on-one coaching, working sessions, and structured practice — moving them from early experimentation to confident, independent use. Recognize when a solution built for one team applies to others, and do the work to make it reusable across the organization. Establish a clear framework for tracking AI adoption progress across business units and report findings to IT leadership on a regular cadence. Set documentation standards for the team — every tool, workflow, and lesson learned should be captured so it doesn't live only in your head. Help develop Kong's internal AI governance standards in partnership with IT, Security, and Engineering. Mentor junior team members and interns, giving them hands-on experience and clear feedback. Stay current on AI developments and translate what's relevant into practical applications for Kong's business context. What You'll Bring: Minimum Requirements 5+ years of experience in a technical or cross-functional role that required problem-solving across teams and functions. A track record of building AI-powered tools, automations, or workflows that changed how real work gets done — with specific examples you can speak to. Experience helping others develop new technical skills, whether through formal training, one-on-one coaching, or team enablement programs. Clear, concise communication skills — you can explain a technical concept to someone who's never thought about it before, without talking down to them. Comfort with ambiguity and self-direction; you don't need a detailed roadmap to know where to start. Experience working in or with an IT organization, or a comparable role supporting business operations across multiple functions. Preferred Qualifications: Hands-on experience with AI development platforms and tools such as Claude, Claude Code, MCPs, LLM APIs, custom agent frameworks, or workflow automation platforms. Background in change management, organizational development, or a large-scale rollout that required bringing skeptical stakeholders along. Experience in consulting, solutions engineering, or a client-facing technical role where you had to earn trust and deliver results quickly. Familiarity with the enterprise SaaS tools Kong runs on: Okta, Slack, Google Workspace, Salesforce, Jira, or Freshservice. Experience creating internal toolkits, playbooks, or training programs that outlived your involvement and were adopted at scale. Familiarity with Kong Konnect, Kong Gateway, or API management concepts — understanding how APIs and AI models connect will help you build smarter tools. #LI-KH1 About Kong: Kong Inc., the AI Connectivity Company, is building the connectivity layer of AI. Title: Customer Support & Enablement Specialist
Description: At MedScout, our mission is to empower MedTech commercial teams with the data, insights, and tools they need to deliver life-changing medical innovations to the patients who need them most. We're creating a best-in-class revenue acceleration platform that unites the latest medical claims intelligence with an intuitive user experience built specifically for sales professionals at medical device and diagnostic companies. MedScout's customer success team currently absorbs a lot of operational and technical work by default; ticket triage, troubleshooting, account admin, one-off training, on top of managing relationships and driving expansion. We're hiring a dedicated Customer Support & Enablement Specialist to own that workload directly, so CSMs can stay focused on strategy and growth. You'll be the first point of contact when something breaks, when a user is confused, or when an account needs upkeep, and you'll build the systems (docs, macros, a real knowledge base) that make the next ticket faster than the last. This is a foundational role for our support function. Right now this work is spread across our CSMs by default, and you'll be the first person who owns it end to end, including building out an Intercom instance that today only handles live chat into a real self-serve platform. You'll report to the VP of Customer Success, working as an individual contributor from day one with a lot of latitude to shape how the function runs. The right person has done this kind of build-from-scratch work before, gets energy from turning chaos into process, and is ready to leave their fingerprint on how support works at MedScout for years to come. How will you help us build the company? Support & Troubleshooting Act as the primary support contact and manage Intercom Livechat to address inbound product navigation and usage questions. Provision and manage user accounts and permissions Assign and refresh sales territories for new and existing users Triage inbound issues and escalate the right ones to engineering or CS with clear repro steps (Jam/Loom, logs, screenshots) Investigate and resolve billing/invoicing discrepancies, looping in finance as needed Enablement & Content Own and grow our Intercom instance beyond chat. Today it's live conversations only. You'll evaluate, configure, and roll out the parts of the platform we're not using yet (help center/knowledge base, workflows and automation, the resolution bot) to cut down repetitive tickets and give customers more ways to self-serve. Deliver one-off training for new or stuck users. Build out a knowledge base covering the most common questions so customers can self-serve. Partner with product marketing on customer-facing content What's the ideal background? You've supported B2B SaaS customers directly: 1–3 years in customer support, support ops, or technical support, ideally at a B2B SaaS company — you know what a good ticket queue looks like and what a bad one feels like. You've configured a support platform, not just worked inside one: hands-on experience setting up a tool like Intercom or Zendesk, help centers, macros, workflows, or bots, rather than only answering tickets in it. You write and troubleshoot clearly: you can turn a messy bug report into a clean, reproducible ticket, and explain a fix to a non-technical user without losing them. You build repeatable systems: you're as energized by writing the FAQ that prevents twenty future tickets as you are by solving the one in front of you. You pick up new tools fast: Intercom is your home base, but you don't need hand-holding to learn the next platform. Bonus points if you've administered Intercom specifically (Fin/resolution bot, product tours, workflows), worked in healthcare, life sciences, or health-tech SaaS, or been part of a fast-paced startup. Are you a good fit? At our stage, how you operate matters more than what you'll do day-to-day. We're looking for strong alignment with our four core values: Effort on our inputs: We prepare diligently, leave it all on the "field," and move on quickly. Focusing on good habits and work ethic, not individual outcomes, ultimately creates a winning culture and a successful company. Earn Trust: We keep our commitments to our customers, partners, and each other. We listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully. We strive to demonstrate empathy, inclusion, and intellectual honesty. We are a Learning Organization: The only sure path to continuous improvement is a hypothesis-driven approach that prioritizes focus, decisive experimentation, rapid learning, and iteration. We expect low ego and a high degree of collaboration to enable us to find the right answer as quickly as possible. “Top Right” is the Expectation: We hire and reward driven, innately curious individuals who work hard to gain a deep understanding of our market, their craft, and the outcomes we strive to deliver for our partners. What can you expect from us? Fully covered healthcare, plus vision, dental, and 401k Remote-first culture with quarterly onsites — we stay in nice hotels and eat well Generous budget for learning, development, and tools that make you more effective You will feel heard. You'll hear “Yes, let's do that” — and then have the opportunity to execute What's our interview process? Intro call with our Head of People Ops. We'll discuss what you're looking for in your next chapter and answer your initial questions. Background Deep Dive with one of our team members, going deeper on the specifics of your experience and how this role impacts MedScout. Practical exercise where we get to see your work in action with some of our team members. Values Interview: A meeting with 3 members of the cross-functional team to learn more about how we're living out our values and what they mean to you. A note about our interview process MedScout embraces diversity and equal opportunity in a serious way. We are committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We believe the more inclusive we are, the better our work will be. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation who need it. We want you to be able to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. If you require any accommodation please let us know!

Title: People Enablement Lead, Payroll and HR Systems-US
Description: Mission Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear. In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Title: Workflow + Process Designer (AI Enablement)
Description: Who We Are Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together . We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion. Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work. About the Role: Own how our Foundations business teams design, automate, and operate their most important workflows. Notion is growing quickly, and the processes that run our business — intake, triage, execution, approvals, escalations, reporting — need to scale without adding headcount or losing auditability. This role exists to redesign those processes end to end and to embed AI directly into them, so the work moves faster and the system stays trustworthy. What's different at Notion: you'll build on Notion as customer zero. You'll design multi-system workflows spanning Notion, Slack, email, support tooling, and internal data, then ship the custom agents, skills, and automations that run them — partnering with Finance, Legal, People, Ops, Data, and Engineering to drive real adoption, not just documentation. This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days. What You'll Achieve: Redesign cross-functional processes end to end: Map and optimize core and cross-functional flows for Foundations business teams, making them simpler, faster, and more consistent than the operating models they replace. Architect multi-system workflows: Design workflows spanning Notion, Slack, email, support tooling, and internal systems and data, with clear states, routing, permissions, and auditability. Design for failure, not just the happy path: Identify edge cases, controls, and handoffs so workflows are resilient, reviewable, and easy for a business team to operate without you. Embed AI with clear human-in-the-loop patterns: Define where AI assists, automates, approves, and audits — and make it obvious what AI did and why. Build and maintain custom agents and skills: Ship the agents, structured skills, and runbooks that power intake triage, summarization, routing, escalation, and reporting for business teams. Instrument everything you ship: Define success metrics (cycle time, deflection, quality, adoption), measure them, and iterate based on data and stakeholder feedback. Set the standards others build on: Establish best practices for AI safety, permissions, transparency, and workflow documentation so the patterns hold as more teams adopt them. Drive adoption and change management: Partner with business stakeholders so tooling gets used because it's intuitive and reliable, and measurably improves day-to-day work. Skills You'll Need to Bring: Process and systems design depth: 2–6 years in operations design, service design, product operations, business systems, or internal tools, with a portfolio showing systems thinking and measurable outcomes. Complex workflow experience: Demonstrated ability to design for intake, triage, routing, approvals, escalations, and reporting across teams and tools, including states, permissions, and auditability. Process mapping rigor: Hands-on experience mapping and improving business processes through journey maps, service blueprints, operating models, and SOPs. AI-native builder mindset: Experience designing or building with AI assistants and agents, workflow automation, or internal tooling — including prompt design, tool selection, and evaluation for quality, reliability, and edge cases. This role requires AI fluency. Lightweight automation ability: Comfort building with Notion custom agents and automations, structured skills, and integrations across systems (APIs, webhooks, connectors). Hands-on preferred. Clear communication and stakeholder judgment: Ability to convey design intent using whatever artifact fits the problem, and to present and defend tradeoffs across multiple tools and teams. Comfort with ambiguity: Experience operating in fast-moving environments and collaborating deeply with engineers and PMs to shape decisions, not just execute them. Title: IT Software Architect, SaaS Enablement and Governance
Description: About the Team The SaaS and Software Governance team sits within Corporate IT and helps OpenAI scale from startup-speed tooling to mature enterprise architecture. The team owns practical governance for software, SaaS, integrations, APIs, identity, data access, and agent-enabled workflows, with a mandate to improve security, reduce software sprawl, and help business teams move faster through better foundations. About the Team OpenAI is scaling from an emerging, high-velocity startup into a mature enterprise operating model. The IT Software Architect will help shape the software, SaaS, Data integration, and agent-enabled architecture that lets the company move quickly while improving security, compliance, data quality, and customer, partner, and employee experience. This role is not a traditional ivory-tower architecture function. It is a hands-on governance and enablement role that partners with business teams, IT operations, Security, Procurement, Business Platforms, Applied teams and Data Engineering to guide software decisions, reduce unmanaged sprawl, and build reusable enterprise foundations. Why This Role Matters OpenAI’s software footprint is expanding rapidly across SaaS, internally built tools, agents, integrations, APIs, third-party platforms, and application systems that OpenAI. The company needs a stronger tools architecture layer that can help teams make good decisions early, avoid duplicate tools, govern sensitive data and identities, and identify where OpenAI should build instead of buy. The person in this role will help turn software governance from an approval checkpoint into an enterprise capability: a system that improves speed, reliability, security, and business outcomes. What You'll Do Own the target architecture for enterprise software, SaaS, integrations, APIs, and agent-enabled business systems across Corporate IT. Drive deprecation and consolidate targets for enterprise software. Build lightweight governance patterns that guide teams before software and integration decisions become hard to unwind. Create architecture standards for identity, access, data movement, API usage, admin rights, auditability, observability, and vendor integration. Partner with Security to ensure software architecture addresses SSO, SCIM, MFA, privileged access, non-human identities, secrets, token storage, data residency, encryption, retention, and incident response readiness. Partner with Procurement and Finance to evaluate renewals, rationalization opportunities, enterprise agreements, and build-versus-buy decisions. Partner deeply with application verticals such as GTM, Finance, Legal, HR, Research, Product, and Operations teams to evaluate agentic business workflows and translate them into scalable enterprise system patterns. Review proposed SaaS and internally built tools for overlap, risk, integration quality, ownership, lifecycle, supportability, and long-term fit. Develop reusable architecture blueprints for common capabilities such as intake, workflow, approvals, knowledge management, customer/partner 360, data integration, reporting, content management, learning, surveys, and collaboration. Help define where OpenAI-native GPT or agent-built solutions should replace or enable point SaaS tools. Create clear decision records and architecture artifacts that are understandable by business leaders, engineers, security reviewers, and procurement partners. Drive software catalog maturity by connecting tool inventory, business owner, system owner, integration path, data classification, access model, renewal, risk posture, and support model. Core Architecture Domains SaaS governance and software catalog maturity Enterprise integration architecture, including APIs, event flows, middleware, and system-of-record boundaries Identity, access, and admin model design across internal and external users Data architecture for SaaS, customer, supplier, employee, partner, product, consumption, and connected business models. Agentic workflow architecture and GPT-built replacement patterns Vendor architecture reviews and enterprise agreement leverage across strategic platforms. Security, compliance, ITGC, audit evidence, and operational readiness Support model design, ownership, SLAs, escalation paths, and lifecycle management What You'll Bring 10+ years of experience in enterprise architecture, business systems architecture, IT architecture, SaaS governance, integration architecture, or a related technical leadership role. Strong understanding of SaaS operating models, software lifecycle management, software asset management, and vendor/platform governance. Experience designing integrations across systems, experience in large scale SaaS such as CRM, ERP and Marketplace platforms. Practical knowledge of identity and access patterns including SSO, OIDC, SAML, SCIM, RBAC/ABAC, privileged admin models, service accounts, OAuth apps, and token governance. Ability to evaluate software from multiple angles: business value, architecture fit, security posture, data exposure, cost, supportability, user experience, and vendor strategy. Comfort operating in ambiguity, building structure where little exists, and influencing senior stakeholders without relying only on formal authority. Ability to write clear architecture decision records, governance standards, system diagrams, business cases, and executive-ready recommendations. Strong partner orientation: able to help teams move faster while raising the quality of decisions. Curiosity about AI-native enterprise architecture and where GPT, Codex, and agentic workflows can replace or enable traditional SaaS patterns. Customer focus and motivated to become an expert on our industry, customers, product, ecosystem, and competitors. Active contributor to communities online and/or in-person Bonus: you currently have an engaged following online and an interest in growing your personal audience Who You'll Be Working With You will directly be working with our Marketing Lead, Open Source Lead, co-founders, Product Engineers, and Product Designers. At this early stage, you'll have the ability to work cross-functionally with many members of the team and solve a wide array of problems. When You'll Work We don’t have a particular time-zone preference for this role. We have a flexible schedule that allows you to work collaboratively with other team members and asynchronously when needed. What You'll Receive To determine your salary, we use a number of market and data-driven salary sources. We review all salaries every 6 months to ensure we stay in line with the market. 📈 In addition to our cash compensation, we offer generous perks and benefits. Below are some of the highlights: $4000/yr Travel Stipend to travel anywhere anytime to work alongside other Roboflowers $350/mo Productivity stipend to spend on things that make your work environment more productive, like high-speed internet at home or a co-working space $350/mo AI Tools $150/mo Team lunch $500/one time Home office Cover up to 100% of your health insurance costs for you and your partner or family Equity in the company so we are all invested in the future of computer vision Interview Process Below is the interview process you can expect for this role. Introduction Phase: [45m] Meet with hiring manager, Trevor Lynn to assess for overall mindset and skill set Team Interview Phase: [2 x 60m] Meet with the team [30m] Meet with hiring manager Use this time to review specifics about the job description and ask questions before the project phase begins. Project Phase: You’ll build a project with Roboflow within a specified amount of time. We check references and conduct a background check. Final Interview Stage: [60m] Meet with Co-founder & CTO [60m] Meet with CEO [30m] Meet with Head of Operations to discuss culture Note: you are welcome to request additional conversations with anyone you would like to meet and we will accommodate as best we can. Not sure if this is you? We want a diverse, global team, with a broad range of experience and perspectives. Roboflow is an equal opportunity workplace; we welcome people from all backgrounds, communities, and experiences. The trajectory is steep and it's still early. We're a Series C company with 170+ people, $200M raised, and $100M ARR in sight this year. We’re growing fast and looking for people who are driven by this mission to join us! Our Values: The Principles That Guide Us Our values are the operating system for how we work together and with our partners. They aren't just words on a wall; they are the principles we bring to every decision, every day. We are transparent, upfront and direct. We operate with honesty and clarity. We share information openly, the good and the bad, and believe that direct, respectful feedback is the foundation of trust and progress. We value speed of iteration. We are building something new, which means we learn by doing. We prioritize rapid iteration and getting solutions into the hands of users, believing that progress is more valuable than perfection. We give 110% effort, 30% of the time. We are passionate about our mission, and there are moments that require us to go the extra mile. We believe in focused intensity when it counts, balanced by a sustainable pace that keeps our team energized for the long run. We empathize with customers to a fault. When our users face a problem, we own it. Instead of asking them to change, we ask ourselves, "How can we make this better?" We believe true innovation comes from deep empathy and a relentless focus on solving the real-world challenges of healthcare. "Manager" describes the scope of the function, not a headcount. We sell to health systems, discharge planners, case managers, and post-acute partners: clinical-first buyers who decide on turnaround time, reliability, and patient outcomes rather than feature lists. Our commercial team is growing faster than the informal ways we have trained it. This is our first dedicated enablement hire and the foundation of what becomes a larger function. Success is measurable. Reps ramp faster, more of them hit quota, and the pitch holds up in front of a skeptical case manager no matter who delivers it. What You'll Do Build and run onboarding for every commercial role, covering product, market, clinical vocabulary, systems, and the pitch. Own time-to-first-deal as your primary number. Write and maintain the core narrative, discovery framework, objection responses, and competitive positioning, with a single source of truth in Notion. Partner with Sales Managers as your primary channel for reinforcement. Equip them with call rubrics, scorecards, and coaching guides they will actually use, and join their team meetings and 1:1s so training continues after your session ends. Run a standing working session with Sales Managers to surface field gaps early, and prioritize your roadmap against what they bring rather than what you assume. Run weekly call reviews in Gong, score calls against a rubric you define, and deliver specific, repeatable coaching to individual reps. Use AI to mine transcripts for the objection and loss patterns worth coaching against. Define and enforce a qualification framework and stage exit criteria, in partnership with Revenue Operations, Product Marketing, and Sales Managers. Translate how DME works (intake, documentation, payer requirements, delivery, patient setup) into training reps can hold a real conversation with. Partner with product and product marketing to launch every new capability with positioning, talk tracks, and a demo the team has practiced. Assist Sales Management with pitch certifications, role-plays, and refreshers, and retire content that is no longer accurate. Own the content library, the Gong scorecards, and the AI tooling reps use to prep for calls, including driving adoption and teaching reps what to verify before they trust it. Use AI to compress the gap between a field need and a shipped asset, drafting briefs, talk tracks, and summaries in days rather than weeks, with your judgment on what is accurate enough to ship. What You Bring Experience 4+ years of combined experience in sales and sales enablement. You've carried a number yourself, or you've coached people who do and earned their respect. Ownership of a ramp program end to end, not delivery of someone else's curriculum. You don't need to have managed a team, since this is an IC role, but you should have owned outcomes, not just sessions. Strong project and stakeholder management. You can hold a program together across sales, marketing, product, and clinical operations without a mandate to make people do it. Willingness to be the least comfortable person in the room while you learn a clinical domain, then become the person others come to. Technical Skills Gong or a comparable call recording platform, with a clear point of view on what separates a good call from a bad one. Salesforce reporting. You can find where deals stall and build training against the gap rather than a hunch. Hands-on use of AI tools in your day-to-day work, with examples of what you shipped faster and where they failed you. Notion or a comparable knowledge system, and the discipline to maintain one source of truth. Soft Skills Strong writing. Most of this job is making complicated things short and sayable. Direct, specific feedback. You can tell a rep exactly what went wrong on a call without them shutting down. A bias toward shipping a usable v1 this week over a perfect program next quarter. Bonus Points Healthcare, DME, home health, or post-acute experience, or any background enabling teams that sell to clinical and operational buyers inside a health system. Experience enabling a team that sells to both providers and payors, where the economic buyer and the end user are different people. You've built or configured an AI assistant, agent, or custom GPT that other people relied on, with opinions on where it helped and where it produced confident nonsense. First-in-seat experience. You've built an enablement function where none existed, with no budget and no team. Familiarity with a formal methodology (MEDDPICC, Command of the Message, Challenger) without being religious about any of them. The People You'll Work With You will report to the Head of Revenue Operations. Your closest working relationship is with our Sales Managers. They own the day-to-day coaching, and your programs only stick if they carry them. You will also work daily with AEs, SDRs, account management, marketing, and clinical operations, and partner closely with Revenue Operations, who own the data that shows where training is needed. Our stack: Salesforce, Gong, Slack, and Notion. We build much of our own GTM tooling, including AI agents on top of Salesforce and Gong. Title: AI Enablement Lead [gn] Data Intelligence
Description: The AI Enablement Team is the catalyst for internal transformation and product acceleration across Actian. In the modern data landscape, AI is not a siloed experimental lab; it is a core capability that must be embedded into our product DNA and our engineering workflows. We are looking for an AI Enablement Lead who will architect, scale, and own our AI enablement strategy end-to-end. You are not a theoretical researcher or a passive prompt engineer; you are a highly practical, technical driver who builds the foundational platforms, tooling, and frameworks that allow other product and engineering teams to deploy AI safely, rapidly, and at scale. You will democratize AI across the organization, establish modern LLMOps/MLOps practices, and directly impact the Actian Data Intelligence Platform by introducing agentic workflows, intelligent data pipelines, and cutting-edge capabilities. Core Responsibilities: Internal AI tooling: Design and maintain the core AI orchestration layers, centralized API gateways, and reusable frameworks (e.g., advanced RAG architectures, agentic frameworks) for company-wide consumption. Product AI Integration: Collaborate directly with core engineering teams to embed production-ready generative AI and machine learning features into the Actian Data Intelligence Platform. LLMOps & Governance Infrastructure: Establish strict guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and monitoring tools to track model performance, bias, data privacy, and security across all AI implementations. Cost & Latency Optimization: Actively monitor and manage cloud and API compute spend (token management, open-source vs. commercial models) and optimize execution latency for production AI features. Cross-Functional Upskilling: Lead workshops, design blueprints, and create documentation to empower non-AI engineering teams to build and maintain their own AI-driven features confidently. Rapid Prototyping (PoC to Production): Drive the engineering execution of high-impact AI proof-of-concepts, ensuring they are built with production-grade code that scales seamlessly. Standardization of Tooling: Define and enforce the organization's official AI stack, from vector database selection and vector embeddings strategies to semantic caching mechanisms. Vendor & Open-Source Strategy: Evaluate and manage partnerships with AI model providers and lead the technical assessment of cutting-edge open-source models to keep Actian at the vanguard of innovation. Data-Driven Impact Tracking: Define and track operational metrics for the AI Enablement function, such as developer adoption rates, reduction in time-to-market for AI features, and ROI of implemented AI tools. Qualifications & Profile: Technical Background: Strong background as a Senior AI/ML Engineer, LLMOps Engineer, or Software Architect who has successfully built and scaled AI-powered applications in enterprise SaaS or complex data platforms. AI & Engineering Mastery: Deep technical expertise in Python or Go, semantic search, vector databases (e.g., Pinecone, Milvus, pgvector), orchestration frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex), and fine-tuning or prompt engineering of state-of-the-art Large Language Models (LLMs). Extreme Ownership: High-agency mindset. You don’t wait for product teams to ask for AI capabilities; you proactively build the frameworks that solve their bottlenecks before they even identify them. Software Engineering Rigor: You treat AI development as software engineering. You understand CI/CD, unit testing for AI (evaluation datasets), containerization (Docker/Kubernetes), and clean code architecture. Influence Without Authority: Exceptional leadership and communication skills. You can inspire and align disparate engineering teams around a shared technical vision without being their direct line manager. Communication: Exceptional verbal and written English communication skills. Ability to demystify complex AI anomalies or architectures into clear business value for internal stakeholders and executives. What We Offer: The chance to be part of an innovative, fast-growing company making a significant impact in the data management space. Collaboration with a passionate and diverse team. Competitive salary and benefits package. Flexible work arrangements (remote or hybrid). Opportunities for professional growth and development. Why Join Us? At Actian, we are passionate about innovation and teamwork. This role is perfect for someone who thrives in a dynamic environment, loves creating an efficient and welcoming workspace, and enjoys working closely with a talented team. Interested? We’d love to hear from you! Let’s discuss how you can contribute to our success while growing your career with us. We value diversity at our company. Title: AI Enablement Technical Lead
Description: At Electric Mind, Engineering is where strategy meets action. Our team helps organizations cut through complexity—aligning business ambition with technology execution to unlock real, lasting change. You’ll work alongside curious, driven people tackling high-impact challenges for everyone from scaling startups to global enterprises. Each engagement is different, pushing you to learn, adapt, and grow. Electric Mind’s Technology Practice brings together deep engineering expertise, modern delivery disciplines, and pragmatic architectural thinking to help clients execute complex, mission-critical transformation. We design and implement scalable, secure, high-impact technology solutions that accelerate business outcomes. About the Role Act as the accountable Electric Mind (EM) technical leader across a number of client teams, for a large scale AI Enablement program. The Tech Lead owns the adoption approach to Electric Mind’s AI-enablement delivery method and coaches Client Tech Leads, QE Leads, and Architects as required so the AI adoption practices across the different client teams remain consistent . This role is distinct from a typical Tech Lead role: the Electric Mind Tech Lead owns the AI adoption across multiple client team, whereas a typical tech lead owns the technical delivery. Our Technical Leads will work closely with the Program Engineering Lead to foster AI adoption and will escalate any issues or blockers to adoption that fall outside of their remit to the Engineering Lead. What You’ll Do Act as the single point of Electric Mind technical accountability across its assigned pods — the owner of technical direction and decisions for how the AI-enabled delivery method is adopted technically. As the technical accountability point, the Tech Lead must be able to: Own AI adoption for the technical aspects of the Software Delivery Lifecycle : this comprises, but may not be limited to, how AI-assisted engineering, code, and QE practices are introduced, sequenced, and embedded across the client teams. Coach Client Tech Leads, QE Leads, and Architects as required, building their capability to foster adoption of AI enablement best practices within their own teams. Reinforce a review-based culture and make sure the processes around solution design review, code review, QE plan and test review are strong and disciplined, focused on correctness against acceptance criteria rather than style. As AI compresses authoring, review becomes the real bottleneck, and review discipline is frequently a pre-existing team weakness that must be addressed. Own accountability for the integration of the QE approach into the AI enabled lifecycle. Description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Software Engineer II (AI Enablement) based in United States. The Senior Software Engineer II will build and operate the platform infrastructure that enables organization-wide adoption of AI and agentic technologies. You will own critical systems spanning MCP gateway infrastructure, plugin distribution, model routing, observability, and AI platform tooling. The role combines deep platform engineering with direct business impact, including measurable effects on AI adoption, inference performance, and technology spend. You will work across backend services, developer platforms, security, infrastructure, and AI tooling in a highly collaborative environment. Your work will support both engineers and non-engineers by making agentic capabilities easier, safer, and more scalable to use. This is a hands-on platform role for an experienced engineer who enjoys solving complex problems with real users, operational ownership, and measurable outcomes. Accountabilities: Own and extend the MCP Gateway and connector platform, building and hardening integrations with enterprise systems such as Glean, Slack, Jira, Snowflake, Salesforce, Monday, Tableau, and Databricks. Design and maintain authentication, authorization scopes, tenancy, rate limiting, and read/write policy enforcement for connected tools, partnering with Security and platform owners to establish safe-by-default access patterns. Own the plugin distribution layer and marketplace publishing pipeline, including versioning, CI/CD, plugin pull request reviews, release hygiene, and developer tooling synchronization. Build and maintain shared plugins, skills, hooks, and Spec-Driven Development tooling used across engineering teams. Create and maintain authoring documentation and guides that enable other teams to contribute to the platform independently. Define model-routing strategies and develop benchmarks and evaluation harnesses that support evidence-based decisions about model selection and performance. Extend infrastructure that transforms agent outputs into browsable, searchable, and collaborative experiences, including discovery, tagging, engagement instrumentation, comments, expiration, and sharing notifications. Run technical enablement activities such as office hours and educational sessions focused on agentic coding and plugin-authorship practices. Mentor engineers on AI platform development patterns, plugin creation, and effective use of agentic coding tools. Triage and consolidate incoming platform feature requests and help prioritize improvements based on user needs and platform impact. Participate in on-call responsibilities for marketplace-published artifacts and gateway availability. Requirements: Bachelor's degree or higher in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field. 5+ years of professional software engineering experience. Demonstrated production ownership of a backend service or developer platform, such as an API gateway, service proxy, SDK/CLI, internal developer platform, or comparable system, including responsibility for authentication, releases, and operational health. Strong production experience with at least one modern application stack such as Python, TypeScript/Node, Go, or a comparable technology. Strong experience with modern CI/CD practices and production software delivery. Hands-on experience implementing authentication and authorization for machine-to-machine traffic, including OAuth2, OIDC, M2M credentials, token scoping, and secret management. Demonstrated ability to instrument owned systems using metrics, structured logging, tracing, usage analytics, or similar observability practices and use resulting data to inform technical decisions. Direct hands-on experience with agentic coding tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, Cody, Copilot agents, Aider, or equivalent tools in production or near-production environments. Strong written communication skills, including the ability to create technical documentation, runbooks, and educational resources for engineering teams. Experience authoring or maintaining MCP servers, Claude Code plugins, skills, hooks, or comparable LLM-tooling integrations is preferred. Experience operating an LLM gateway or inference proxy in production, including routing, fallback, caching, quotas, and cost attribution, is preferred. Experience building evaluation harnesses or benchmarks for LLM systems, including A/B comparisons of prompts, tools, or model versions, is a plus. Experience operating a package registry, plugin ecosystem, or extension marketplace, including publishing pipelines, semantic versioning, compatibility management, and deprecation processes, is beneficial. Background in healthcare technology, HIPAA-regulated environments, or systems handling protected health information is preferred. Familiarity with business associate agreements and data-residency considerations for third-party tooling is a plus. Experience with technologies such as Python/FastAPI, Vue/TypeScript, Postgres, AWS, Auth0, Datadog, or Sumo Logic is beneficial but not required. Comfort working across frontend, backend, and infrastructure boundaries. Experience as an early engineer on an internal platform where adoption must be earned through product quality and user value is a plus. Strong collaboration, mentoring, problem-solving, ownership, and cross-functional communication skills. Ability to work effectively in a remote environment and manage prolonged periods of computer-based work. Benefits: Remote work arrangement within the United States. Title: Data Enablement Lead
Description: We are seeking a versatile, highly motivated Data Enablement Lead to bridge the gap between complex backend data infrastructure and business-facing analytics solutions. In this role, you will be the core engine driving analytics, reporting, and self-service data products for our Business Unit (BU). While our central data infrastructure team handles enterprise-wide platform needs, you will take ownership of our BU's specific data stack—coordinating with the central team to manage existing upstream pipelines while building and maintaining our own localized data pipelines when speed and agility are required. Beyond standard dashboards and data pulls, your goal is to revolutionize how non-technical stakeholders interact with data. You will design next-generation data consumption tools—ranging from high-performance data cubes to AI-driven query bots—empowering our BU to get answers instantly. What we seek: Hands-On Engineering & Tooling Data Pipelines & Backend : Build, maintain, and optimize data pipelines feeding our BU’s analytics layer. Work across our core data platform ( Apache Hive ) and high-performance OLAP backend ( Apache Doris ). Next-Gen Data Tools: Architect non-data-person-facing tools to automate data access, such as setting up data cubes/semantic layers and building AI/LLM-powered data bots (e.g., text-to-SQL / natural language data querying). Architecture & Standards: Establish best practices for data modeling, pipeline monitoring, and data quality within our BU's local repository Technical Project Management & Coordination Cross-Team Collaboration: Act as the primary technical interface between analytics / operational team and the central platform data engineering team. Project Delivery: Scope, prioritize, and manage the end-to-end lifecycle of analytics engineering projects, translating non-technical needs into clear technical specifications. Enablement & Stakeholder Management: Educate and support operational team on self-serve tools, documentation, and data literacy initiatives. What you'll need: Technical Skills Data Engineering & Warehousing: 5+ years of experience in data engineering, analytics engineering, or technical data product management. Stack Expertise: Strong proficiency in SQL and Python . Solid experience with large-scale data warehouses ( Apache Hive ) and modern OLAP engines ( Apache Doris , ClickHouse, StarRocks, or similar). Data Product & AI Innovation: Demonstrated interest or experience in building interactive data tools (e.g., Cube.js, semantic layers) or leveraging AI/LLM frameworks (e.g., LangChain, OpenAI APIs, Text-to-SQL pipelines) to simplify data retrieval. Data Modeling: Deep understanding of dimensional modeling, star schemas, data aggregation, and query optimization techniques. Project & Stakeholder Management Proven ability to coordinate across cross-functional engineering teams with competing business priorities. Strong project management skills—able to track dependencies, mitigate risks, and manage stakeholder expectations clearly without micro-managing. Pragmatic approach to the "Build vs. Coordinate" tradeoff—knowing when to rely on central platforms versus when to build lightweight local solutions.
