Title: Design Program Manager
Description:
The Role

As a Design Program Manager at Everlaw, you'll establish the operating system for our growing product design team, bringing structure, visibility, and predictability to how we design AI-powered litigation tools. As our first dedicated Design Program Manager, you'll absorb operational friction and cross-functional complexity so product designers can focus entirely on craft, quality, and solving complex user workflows.

This is a full-time, exempt position based in our Oakland, CA office with a hybrid work schedule: in office M/W/Th with the option to work from home on Tu/Fr.

What you'll do

  • Own the design operating model for planning and delivery — define how design work is estimated, sequenced, and handed off, and maintain the system that makes dependencies and timeline risk visible before they become escalations.
  • Define design readiness criteria and coordinate pre-launch quality reviews to ensure shipped features meet high standards for craft, responsiveness, accessibility, and edge cases.
  • Own the working interfaces between Design, Product Management, Engineering, User Research, and Technical Writing — define how scope is agreed, how dependencies are tracked, and where conflicts get decided, so those questions have a standing answer instead of being renegotiated per project. 
  • Build and champion lightweight design operations rhythms, frameworks, and templates—such as design briefs and critique structures—to streamline team workflows.
  • Manage design resourcing and bandwidth tracking to inform staffing decisions, highlight capacity constraints, and help leadership plan for future team growth.
  • Own how design's work is represented to the business — build and maintain the reporting layer (capacity, throughput, readiness) that lets product and executive leadership plan against design, rather than assembling narrative updates each cycle. 

About You

  • You have at least 5 years of experience in Design Program Management or Design Operations supporting product design teams in complex, enterprise B2B SaaS or data-heavy environments.
  • You excel at balancing competing priorities across multiple stakeholders, steering teams through ambiguity with structure, clear prioritization, and empathy.
  • You've built and scaled lightweight design operations frameworks, delivery plans, and resource tracking processes without stifling creative momentum.
  • You bring excellent communication and storytelling skills, with a proven ability to translate design progress and complex trade-offs into business-relevant narratives for leadership.
  • You bring a strong understanding of user-centered design methodologies, modern UX workflows, and tools like Figma.
  • You have experience working with project tracking tools like Jira or emerging AI tools (e.g., Cursor, Claude Design).
  • You operate with a low-ego, highly collaborative style, finding genuine fulfillment in making design teams visible and successful.
  • You are authorized to work in the United States without restrictions. Please note that at this time, Everlaw is not sponsoring F-1 visas, including OPT, for this role.

VISTA REAL CHARTER HIGH SCHOOL

Full Time, Monday - Friday; 8:00 AM - 2:00 PM

 

COMPENSATION:

Clear Credential: $79,500.00 - $100,700.00 / year with sign on bonus of $16,000
Preliminary Credential: $68,900 / year with sign on bonus of $16,000
Intern Credential: $66,144 / year with sign on bonus of $3,500
Extras: $4,000 / year IEP Stipend

 

Help Us Change Lives

We live by the motto that “There is a Student in Front of Everything We Do” and we are very passionate about it.  Do you have a passion to work with students? If so, then this is an exciting opportunity for you! You’ll have the opportunity to work with a diverse group of students supporting their growth and development. Remember the person who made a difference in your life? Now it’s your turn.

Learn more about us at https://learn4life.org/

 

How You Will Make an Impact

The Special Education Teacher will teach in a personalized instructional environment, work with students and/or parents to determine and evaluate the student’s academic plan, manage, and provide services according to the student’s Individual Education Plan (IEP). This position involves collaboration with other instructional staff and school personnel and reports to the Principal or the designee. 

 

RESPONSIBILITIES/DUTIES: This job description is intended to accurately reflect the duties, responsibilities, and requirements of the position. It is not intended to be and should not be construed as an all-inclusive list of all the responsibilities, skills, or working conditions associated with this classification. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job. 

  • Plan, organize and implement daily lessons in accordance with the approved curriculum.
  • Conduct pre- and post-testing using standardized tests for each student. 
  • As a part of a team, write and implement goals as outlined in each student's IEP. 
  • Schedule and chair Schedule, write, and chair IEP meetings including 30-day review IEP meetings for all students.
  • Responsible to manage a student’s behavior. 
  • Demonstrate competency in all subject areas. 
  • Participate in the identification of students with possible disabilities post intervention phase.
  • Provide direct student instruction.
  • Provide academic assessments.
  • Meet special education timeline requirements as specified by education code.
  • Collaborate with general education teachers.
  • Work with Special Education Program Specialists and school support staff to support student instruction.
  • Participate in authorized school district trainings, school events, and meetings.
  • Maintain documentation of communications with students, families, and other services providers.
  • Maintain documentation of daily activities.
  • Complete reports and forms as required.
  • Travel to other school sites to render Special Education teaching services. 
  • Perform administrative duties, responsibilities, and activities as assigned. These may be changed or modified from time to time.    

Qualifications

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES:

  • Knowledge of California Teaching Standards. 
  • Knowledge of core academic subject (s) assigned.
  • Knowledge of high school credits, graduation requirements, interventions, and alternative educational programs, including independent study. 
  • Knowledge and understanding of Independent Study, Personal Learning, and Distance Learning education models. 
  • Knowledge of research-based instructional strategies necessary for effective instruction of all student populations, including students at-risk of academic failure. 
  • Ability to work effectively with students from diverse racial, ethnic, linguistic, disability, and socioeconomic groups.  
  • Ability to work effectively with parents, staff members, and community representatives in providing a rigorous educational program. 
  • Ability to communicate effectively, including giving clear and concise instructions, using academic language, an appropriate delivery level, listening without bias, and providing proper feedback/reinforcement. 
  • Ability to make independent judgments, meet deadlines and maintain accurate student records.  

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited university is required.
  • Valid California credential Specialist with authorization for the Special Education disability and level assigned or intern eligible is required. 
  • English Learner Authorization or eligible to obtain EL Authorization is required.
  • Autism Authorization is required or eligible to enroll and complete a Commission-approved professional preparation program in the special education specialty area requested, including successful completion of supervised field study is required.
  • Demonstrated competency in the core academic subject area assigned is required.
  • Knowledge of Student Information Systems (SIS) and related Educational Systems. 
  • Proficient level of skills in MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) and other technology applications. 
  • Ability to travel up to 5% In the performance of job duties are required.  

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Vision: Ability to read small print and view a computer screen for prolong periods, prepare, or inspect documents and operate office equipment. 
  • Hearing: Ability to hear average or typical conversations and receive ordinary information.
  • Speech: Ability to be understood in face-to-face communication, in person or virtually, to speak with a level of proficiency and volume to be understood over a telephone or computer. 
  • Mental Demands: Ability to read, write, understand, interpret, and apply information at a moderately complex level essential for successful job performance; math skills at a high school proficiency level; judgement and the ability to process information quickly; learn quickly and follow verbal procedures and standards; give verbal instruction; rank tasks in order of importance; copy, compare, compile and coordinate information and records. Frequent multi-tasking, changing of task priorities, repetitious exacting work. Understand how to manage stress. high workflow management, high project coordination, and high people engagement.
  • Upper Body Mobility: Ability to use fingers to make small movements such as typing, picking up small objects, or pinching fingers together, use hands to grasp, and manipulate small objects; twist and bend at wrist and elbow; extend arms to reach outward and upward; use hands and arms to lift objects; turn, raise, and lower head.
  • Strength: Ability to lift, carry, push, and pull objects weighing up to 10 pounds. 
  • Environmental Requirements: Ability to encounter constant work interruptions; work cooperatively with others; work independently; work indoors. Prolonged period sitting at a desk and working on a computer. Work in a moderate to high noise environment with frequent deadline pressures.

Description:
Educational Consultant

 

Details about this opportunity:

  • Location: Westchester County,  NY
  • Status: Fee for Service 
  • Hours: 8am - 3pm primarily during the school day
  • Compensation:  $60-$85/hour (FFS)

 

**Please note this is a range. Rates are determined by the service provided, professional experience and license/certifications held. In addition the position posted may be either full-time or fee-for-service (FFS), depending on the current caseload which will be discussed during the interview. This arrangement can vary and is subject to change.**

 

 

What we have to offer YOU: 

PART TIME BENEFITS: 

We are excited to offer a range of valuable benefits for our employees who work 25 or more hours per week (Medical, Dental, Vision, FSA and  Pet Insurance)*

  • Employee Assistance Program 
  • Referral Program
  • Professional Development Assistance 
  • Team Building events
  • Incentive Program

 

Responsibilities:  

As a Educational Consultant, you will:

  • Partner with school administrators, special education teachers, teaching assistants, aides, related service providers, and families to develop and implement individualized, evidence-based educational and behavioral supports.
  • Provide consultation and coaching to Special Education teams, with a focus on strengthening instructional practices, classroom systems, student engagement, independence, and implementation of individualized supports.
  • Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to identify student strengths and needs and develop practical strategies that support academic, behavioral, social, communication, and adaptive skill development.
  • Support Special Education staff in implementing specially designed instruction (SDI), accommodations, modifications, and individualized instructional strategies within classroom and center-based settings.
  • Collect, analyze, and interpret student data to monitor progress, evaluate intervention effectiveness, and make data-driven recommendations for instructional and behavioral adjustments.
  • Provide classroom-based consultation, observation, modeling, and performance feedback to support consistent implementation of educational and behavioral strategies.
  • Collaborate with school and center-based teams to support implementation of Individualized Education Programs (IEPs) and ensure instructional and behavioral programming aligns with student goals.
  • Participate in Committee on Special Education (CSE) meetings, when requested, to provide information regarding student progress, consultation recommendations, and ongoing support needs.
  • Provide consultation and support within designated center-based service locations to promote consistent implementation of BIS, ABA, and Special Education services.
  • Collaborate with Clinical Supervisors, Special Education staff, and other providers to support coordinated service delivery and promote consistency across instructional, behavioral, and clinical programming.
  • Support the development and implementation of individualized service schedules and center-based service models designed to increase student access to educational services.
  • Provide ongoing coaching, modeling, and performance feedback to providers and classroom staff to strengthen implementation of individualized interventions and instructional strategies.
  • Develop and facilitate professional development workshops and staff trainings related to special education, behavior management, data collection, , classroom strategies, student independence, instructional practices, and other identified areas of need.
  • Support staff in developing sustainable classroom and service-delivery systems that promote student independence, engagement, skill acquisition, and generalization across people and settings.
  • Maintain consistent communication with Clinical Supervisors, Clinical Managers, Assistant Directors, Directors, school administrators, and other appropriate team members regarding student progress, consultation needs, staffing considerations, and service delivery.
  • Complete timely and accurate documentation, including consultation notes, progress reports, behavioral assessments, data summaries, professional development documentation, and other required service documentation.
  • Contribute to quarterly or periodic program reviews and progress reports by summarizing consultation activities, implementation progress, staff development, student outcomes, and recommendations for continued support.
  • Maintain confidentiality of student records and protected information in accordance with HIPAA, FERPA, and company policies.
  • Participate in ongoing professional development, clinical supervision, and collaborative meetings to continuously strengthen educational, behavioral, and consultation practices.
  • Maintain professionalism, ethical standards, and a solution-focused approach in all interactions with students, families, district personnel, providers, and colleagues.
  • Travel between assigned school districts, schools, and designated EBSS/center locations to provide on-site consultation, coaching, observation, professional development, and service support.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.

Title: Manager, PAR Commercial Operations & Governance
Description:
The Company:

Faraday Future is a California-based technology company focused on the design, engineering, and development of intelligent, connected electric vehicles and related artificial intelligence–enabled technologies.

Founded in 2014, the Company’s mission is to disrupt the automotive and technology industries by creating user-centric, technology-first experiences. The Company, together with its controlled subsidiaries, operates across multiple technology-driven areas, including AI electric vehicles, robotics, and its crypto business (AIXC), all under its upgraded Global EAI Industry Bridge Strategy, marking the beginning of a new chapter in AI mobility and Web3 integration. The Company aims to leverage the latest technologies and world’s best talent to realize exciting new possibilities across all of these lines. Faraday Future’s automotive business exemplifies its vision for luxury, innovation, and performance, while its FX strategy aims to introduce mass production models equipped with state-of-the-art luxury technology derived from the FF brand, targeted towards a broader market with middle-to-low price range offerings. FF is committed to redefining mobility through AI innovation. Join us in shaping the future of intelligent transportation and technology by creating something new, something connected, and something with a true global impact.

Your Role:

The Manager, PAR Commercial Operations & Governance is a senior leadership role within the PAR Business team, with dual ownership over China customer relationship management and the PAR team’s local compliance and governance function. This person will take strategic ownership of a defined portfolio of China-based customers and dealer partners — building high-trust relationships, overseeing commercial operations, and ensuring consistent execution across the account lifecycle. In parallel, this role leads the PAR team’s governance mandate, designing and maintaining the compliance infrastructure necessary to meet local regulatory requirements.

This is a senior, externally-facing role that requires a mature balance of commercial acumen, operational rigor, and compliance expertise. The ideal candidate brings proven experience managing complex customer relationships in China-facing business environments, as well as a working familiarity with local compliance obligations in a B2B commercial context. Work location is El Segundo, CA; regular coordination with China-based contacts is expected, and some travel may be required.

Key Responsibilities:

  1. China Customer Relationship Management & Strategic Account Ownership
  • Own the commercial relationship with an assigned portfolio of China-based customers and dealer partners, serving as the senior point of contact for strategic and operational matters.
  • Build deep, trust-based relationships with key customer and partner stakeholders, positioning FF as a reliable and valued long-term business partner.
  • Lead regular business reviews and strategic check-ins with assigned accounts, identifying growth opportunities, surfacing risks, and driving joint action plans.
  • Act as an internal advocate for China customers and partners — representing their needs, priorities, and feedback in cross-functional discussions and leadership forums.
  • Manage escalations with professionalism and urgency, coordinating resolution across internal teams and maintaining customer confidence throughout.
  1. Commercial Operations Management & Performance Tracking
  • Own the end-to-end management of China PAR (investor) accounts, including business negotiation, contract execution, payment tracking, incentive claims, and settlement procedures.
  • Design and maintain robust tracking systems and reporting frameworks that provide real-time visibility into account status, commercial commitments, and operational health.
  • Prepare and present regular account performance reviews to PAR leadership, delivering data-driven insights and actionable recommendations.
  • Drive continuous improvement in commercial operations workflows, identifying and resolving systemic inefficiencies and implementing process enhancements.
  • Coordinate closely with Finance, Legal, Supply Chain, and Sales teams to ensure seamless execution across the commercial lifecycle.
  1. Local Compliance Strategy & Governance Leadership
  • Lead the PAR team’s local compliance function, owning the design, implementation, and ongoing management of compliance processes required to meet regulatory and internal governance standards.
  • Serve as the primary liaison with Legal, Finance, and external compliance stakeholders on all matters related to local regulatory obligations affecting China customer operations.
  • Build and maintain a robust compliance documentation infrastructure — including filing systems, audit trails, and version-controlled records — that supports regulatory review and internal oversight.
  • Monitor developments in relevant regulatory frameworks and proactively assess their implications for PAR commercial operations, presenting findings and recommendations to leadership.
  • Lead the preparation of compliance reports and governance summaries for PAR leadership, regulators, and internal audit functions as required.
  1. Partner Onboarding & Qualification Oversight
  • Oversee the onboarding process for new China-based partners, setting standards for qualification, KYC, documentation, and initial commercial setup.
  • Ensure all new partners are onboarded in full compliance with FF’s contractual and regulatory requirements, with a consistent and professional experience.
  • Develop and maintain onboarding frameworks and partner-facing documentation that can scale with the growth of the China dealer network.
  1. Cross-functional Leadership & Internal Coordination
  • Lead cross-functional coordination for China account management and compliance activities, ensuring clear ownership, timely handoffs, and consistent communication across teams.
  • Represent the PAR Commercial Operations & Governance function in internal leadership discussions, providing strategic input on China market operations and regulatory matters.
  • Mentor and support junior team members on account management practices, compliance protocols, and professional communication standards.
  • Contribute to PAR-wide strategic initiatives as directed by leadership, drawing on deep expertise in China customer operations and governance.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience
  • 5 years of professional experience in customer operations, account management, commercial operations, compliance, or a closely related function — with at least a portion of that experience in China-facing or cross-border business roles.
  • External Communication & Relationship Management: Proven track record of managing senior-level customer or partner relationships with professionalism, strategic depth, and a service-oriented mindset. Comfortable leading difficult conversations and managing escalations with poise.
  • Compliance & Governance Ownership: Demonstrated experience owning compliance processes, documentation, or regulatory coordination in a commercial or operational context. Ability to design and maintain governance frameworks that scale.
  • Analytical & Operational Rigor: Strong ability to manage complex, multi-account operations with high accuracy — maintaining clear tracking, identifying issues proactively, and delivering timely, well-organized reporting.
  • Fluency in Mandarin Chinese (written and verbal) is required. This role involves regular senior-level communication with China-based customers, partners, and potentially regulatory contacts.
  • English: Fluency in English (written and verbal) is required for internal leadership communication, reporting, and documentation.
  • Leadership & Influence: Ability to lead cross-functional coordination, influence without direct authority, and represent the function credibly in leadership discussions.
  • Technical Skills: Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel (including data tracking, pivot tables, and reporting); strong PowerPoint skills for executive presentations; familiarity with CRM systems and compliance documentation tools.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • China Market Expertise: Deep experience managing China-based customer or partner portfolios, with strong familiarity with Chinese business culture, regulatory environments, and commercial norms.
  • Compliance Leadership: Prior ownership of local compliance programs, regulatory filings, or governance frameworks in a cross-border or China-specific commercial context.
  • Strategic Account Management: Background in managing key accounts with defined commercial targets, performance tracking, and executive-level relationship ownership.
  • Cross-border Operations: Significant experience navigating US-China cross-border business environments, including time zone management, regulatory differences, and bilingual communication at a senior level.
  • Industry Fit: Background in automotive, EV, robotics, smart hardware, or consumer technology industries.
  • Big Firm Exposure: Experience at a top-tier professional services, consulting, or large enterprise organization (e.g., Big 4, MBB, or Fortune 500) in a commercial operations, account management, or compliance capacity.
  • Contract & Legal Familiarity: Working knowledge of commercial agreements, dealer contracts, and regulatory compliance requirements in a B2B or channel context.

Salary Range:

($120,000-$150,000 DOE), plus benefits and incentive plans.

Perks + Benefits

  • Healthcare + dental + vision benefits (Free for you/discounted for family)
  • 401(k) options
  • Casual dress code + relaxed work environment
  • Culturally diverse, progressive atmosphere

Title: Technical Program Manager (EG), Manufacturing
Description:
About MISUMI Americas

MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. By integrating a vast catalog of components with a world-class digital manufacturing platform, MISUMI Americas empowers engineers and procurement teams to accelerate innovation across the entire product lifecycle. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.

At Fictiv, we’re building a company that is developing the operating system for sourcing custom mechanical parts. We already enjoy manufacturing and delivering highly complex, high quality parts for our Fortune 500 customers who are building the future with products like autonomous electric vehicles, surgical systems, and industrial robots. As we scale our business, we are looking to expand our growth within India.

In your role as Technical Program Manager, you will be working directly with our MPs, you’ll be using your engineering background, manufacturing process knowledge and management experience, to develop and implement effective and efficient program plans to ensure we’re executing programs within scope, budget and timing; while meeting or exceeding our customer’s expectations. You will also be the customer’s point of contact; you will drive scope clarity (internally and externally), issue resolution, stakeholder management and program success. You will be responsible for overseeing multiple programs across multiple regions, proactively managing risk, addressing any customer requests and coordinating across corresponding regional operations teams to keep programs on track and provide the corresponding program updates/status reports.

As an experienced member of the team, you will be following our defined processes and driving their use in a new region with new manufacturing partners. Additionally, you will actively identify areas for improvement in your workflow and in the systems used by the Technical Program Management team, and will drive those improvements through cross functional projects. You will also be working cross functionally to support the development of robust processes which will ensure the successful introduction of new service offerings that Fictiv launches to the public.

You will report on-site to the Program Management Lead in our office in Bengaluru, India.

Why Join Us?

This is a high-impact role where you’ll help shape the future of hardware manufacturing through smart program leadership. If you thrive in fast-paced environments, enjoy building processes, and are excited about working on cutting-edge programs with global stakeholders, we’d love to meet you

   

Program Execution & Oversight

Lead end-to-end project execution, ensuring adherence to defined scope, budget, and timelines.
Oversee cross-functional coordination and execution across engineering, sourcing, manufacturing, logistics, and quality.

Program Planning & Risk Management

Develop comprehensive and realistic project/program plans.
Identify and proactively manage program risks and mitigation strategies, ensuring alignment with internal and external stakeholders.
Stakeholder & Partner Management
Engage regularly with internal teams, customers, and manufacturing partners to ensure alignment.
Build strong working relationships with stakeholders to facilitate quick decision-making and issue resolution.

Customer & Fulfillment Alignment

Understand and define customer requirements and fulfillment needs.
Drive resolution of open gaps to ensure program success and customer satisfaction.

Change Management

Own the evaluation and execution of post-sale change requests.
Balance scope, risk, and cost implications while maintaining overall program objectives.

Program Monitoring & Communication

Track and report on program performance using defined metrics (cost, time, quality, risk).
Escalate issues as necessary and keep leadership informed with timely updates and clear documentation.

Continuous Improvement

Identify areas for improvement across the program lifecycle and TPM workflow.
Drive both tactical and strategic improvements to enhance operational effectiveness and program quality.

   

 

Sitting and working at a computer for extended periods of time.
   
Travel 0- 10%   

Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering (or equivalent).
Minimum 7+ years of experience in a technical project or program management role within fast-paced manufacturing environments.
Proven track record managing programs through NPD (New Product Development) and Mass Manufacturing.
Hands-on experience managing suppliers/manufacturers and external stakeholders

Technical & Domain Knowledge

Must-Have: Deep experience with CNC Machining.
Good to Have: Familiarity with Composite and Sheet Metal Fabrication processes.
Solid understanding of quality systems, PPAP, and supply chain management (SCM).
Knowledge of logistics, sourcing, and finance related to project execution.

Soft Skills & Work Style

Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Fluent in English and any other Local Language
Strong interpersonal skills with a team-first mindset.
Ability to work independently, manage time effectively, and drive results in ambiguous environments.
Gritty, adaptable, and able to operate in under-defined or evolving processes.
Data-driven decision maker with a methodical and detail-oriented approach.
A systems thinker: capable of developing repeatable, flexible, and reliable processes.

We’re actively seeking teammates who:

  • Bring diverse perspectives and experience to our culture and company. 
  • Excel at being part of a strong, empathetic team.
  • Thrive in an environment emphasizing respect, honesty, collaboration, and growth.
  • Have an ‘always learning’ mindset that celebrates learning, not just wins. 
  • Help us continue to build a world-class organization that values the contributions of all of our teammates

We encourage applications from members of underrepresented groups, including but not limited to women, members of the LGBTQ community, people of color, people with disabilities, and veterans.

Title: Technical Program Manager (Operational Readiness) (Data Centers)
Description:
Who We Are:

Galaxy Digital Inc. (Nasdaq: GLXY) is a global leader in digital assets and data center infrastructure, growing the economy that runs on code. Galaxy delivers the onchain infrastructure that connects institutions to digital assets, including trading, advisory, asset management, staking, self-custody, and tokenization. Galaxy also develops and operates data center infrastructure to power AI and HPC workloads. Anchored by its Helios campus in Texas, Galaxy is building a multi-gigawatt pipeline of more than 5.7 GW of potential capacity, positioning it among the largest and fastest-growing data center developers in North America.

The Company is headquartered in New York City, with offices across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Additional information about Galaxy's businesses and products is available on www.galaxy.com.

What We Value:

We are a diverse team of free thinkers, and fast movers united to help investors and creators energize the global economy. We are looking for individuals who thrive in a culture of builders and overachievers and embrace high performance, transparent feedback, and a mission-first approach. Our culture shapes our way of working and gets us where we want to be.

  • Seek Excellence.
  • Be Selective To Be Effective.
  • Be Highly Aligned, Loosely Coupled.
  • Disagree Transparently.
  • Encourage Independent Decision-Making.
  • Build Dream Teams.

Who You Are:

The Technical Program Manager (TPM) is the operational readiness execution lead for each data center campus, owning the site-level workstream from early design coordination through final turnover. The TPM translates the VP of Operational Readiness's standards and frameworks into site-level execution, serving as the primary operations representative across Construction, Engineering, EHS, PMO, Commissioning agents, 3PDC operators, and tenants. Managing multiple sites concurrently across varying stages of development, the TPM ensures operational requirements are embedded early and carried through to a clean, accountable handoff. In close partnership with the Technical Operations Manager (TOM) and Technical Operations Engineer (TOE), the TPM validates 3PDC operator readiness, drives punch list items through completion, and executes a deliberate transfer of ownership to the TOM before transitioning to the next site in the portfolio.

What You'll Do:

 Operational Readiness & Design Coordination

  • Represent Operations as the primary site-level stakeholder during design and pre-construction phases, ensuring operational requirements, maintainability, and Galaxy's operating standards are reflected in project deliverables
  • Partner with Engineering & Operations Reliability and Construction teams to identify and resolve design gaps that could impact operational performance or safety post-turnover
  • Ensure that the site as built aligns with the operating model Galaxy intends to execute under, surfacing discrepancies early and driving resolution through the appropriate channels
  • Maintain visibility into project schedules and proactively surface risks to operational readiness timelines to the VP of Operational Readiness

Commissioning Oversight

  • Serve as Operations' site-level representative throughout the commissioning process, ensuring systems are commissioned in alignment with the technical standards set by Engineering & Operations Reliability
  • Coordinate between Commissioning agents, Engineering, Construction, and 3PDC operators to align on scope, sequencing, and acceptance criteria
  • Validate that commissioning outcomes meet the technical and operational thresholds required for turnover
  • Maintain commissioning records that support audit readiness and serve as reference documentation for the TOM post-handoff

3PDC Operator Readiness & Turnover

  • Work alongside the TOM and TOE to assess and validate 3PDC operator readiness ahead of turnover milestones — including procedure readiness, staffing, training records, and site familiarization
  • Ensure operators have the documentation, qualifications, and site-specific knowledge required to assume operational responsibility at RFS
  • Own the punch list process through final item completion, ensuring all outstanding items are resolved and formally accepted before turnover is executed
  • Execute a structured, documented handoff to the TOM upon turnover completion and disengage to focus on the next site in the portfolio

Cross-Functional Program Management

  • Serve as the primary operations liaison across all project stakeholders, maintaining alignment and accountability across PMO, Construction, Engineering, EHS, Commissioning agents, 3PDC operators, and tenants
  • Maintain a clear and current picture of each site's readiness status across all workstreams and communicate progress, risks, and decisions to the VP of Operational Readiness
  • Partner with PMO to ensure operational milestones are integrated into the master project schedule and tracked to completion
  • Drive the resolution of cross-functional dependencies that could impact readiness timelines or turnover quality

EHS & Compliance Integration

  • Ensure EHS requirements are accounted for throughout commissioning and turnover activities in coordination with the EHS team
  • Validate that site conditions, operator practices, and life-safety systems meet applicable standards prior to turnover
  • Ensure regulatory and compliance documentation is complete, accurate, and transferable to the TOM at handoff

Tenant Coordination

  • Where applicable, engage with tenants and their representatives throughout the commissioning and turnover process to ensure alignment on timelines, access, and operational expectations
  • Serve as the operational point of contact for tenant-facing questions and commitments during the pre-turnover phase, coordinating with the TOM on items that will carry forward post-handoff

What We’re Looking For:

  • 8+ years of experience in data center operations, commissioning, or critical facilities program management
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex, cross-functional programs in mission-critical environments
  • Strong technical foundation in electrical, mechanical, and controls systems common to data center environments
  • Experience owning commissioning and turnover processes in a structured, milestone-driven environment
  • Proven ability to manage multiple concurrent sites and stakeholder relationships without loss of detail or accountability
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to translate technical complexity for diverse audiences across organizational levels

Bonus Points:

  • Prior experience in hyperscale or large-scale data center environments
  • Familiarity with OSHA, NFPA, NETA, and relevant IEC/IEEE standards
  • Experience working within or alongside a formal PMO structure
  • Background in construction management, critical systems commissioning, or facilities engineering
  • Military, utility, or industrial operations background

What We Offer (Helios):

  • Competitive base salary and discretionary bonus
  • Paid Time Off
  • Company-paid Holidays (14)
  • Company-paid health and protective benefits for employees, partners, and other dependents
  • 3% 401(k) company contribution
  • Generous paid Parental Leave
  • Free coaching and counseling sessions through Headspace
  • Free breakfast and lunch daily
  • Smart, entrepreneurial, and fun colleagues in Employee Resource Groups

*Benefits may vary depending on location.

Apply now and join us as we grow the economy that runs on code. 

The base salary ranges included below will be commensurate with candidate experience, expertise and local market. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors, including candidate experience and expertise. At Galaxy, we maintain a total compensation philosophy which consists of a competitive base salary, annual bonus, and equity incentives.

Title: Content Creator
Description:
Gallery Media Group, voted Most Innovative Publisher, is a modern day publisher that builds brands that capture audience attention across content, experiences and talent. Our trusted network of editors, contributors, talent and experts drive our audience-first approach to ensure brand partnerships siphon our IP and relevance to drive business outcomes.

Gallery Media Group includes women’s lifestyle brand PureWow, the iconic fashion and style brand Coveteur, and a collection of social-first media brands, such as @cocktails on Instagram and TikTok that reach over 200M consumers. Additionally, GMG has an expansive experiential arm rooted in Gallery Houses—a fusion of social content, creators and cultural moments at scale—as well as a robust influencer marketing business.

The company was founded in 2010 by CEO, Ryan Harwood and is now part of VaynerX, the Gary Vaynerchuk-owned holding company.

About the Role

We're building @cocktails into the premier digital destination for cocktail culture and we're looking for a creative strategist who thrives at the intersection of storytelling, analytics, and content production. This role will lead the evolution of our content strategy, helping us create platform-native content that grows audiences, drives engagement, and establishes @cocktails as the leading voice in the category.

You'll work alongside our Content Creator, elevating the team's creative capabilities through collaboration, coaching, experimentation, and a relentless focus on what resonates with audiences.

Responsibilities

Content Strategy & Innovation

  • Develop and evolve a multi-platform content strategy across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, Pinterest, and emerging platforms
  • Generate fresh, data-informed content concepts that balance trends with evergreen storytelling
  • Identify opportunities to expand our content mix, including educational series, personality-driven content, behind-the-scenes features, and creator collaborations
  • Stay ahead of platform trends, algorithm changes, and emerging formats

Creative Leadership

  • Lead creative ideation sessions and maintain an active content pipeline
  • Produce high-quality, platform-native video content from concept through final edit
  • Raise the creative standard across all published content through strong storytelling, pacing, editing, and production techniques
  • Experiment with new formats and creative approaches to continuously improve performance

Performance & Analytics

  • Analyze content performance across all platforms to identify actionable insights
  • Translate analytics into creative decisions, testing hypotheses and iterating based on results

Title: Program Manager
Description:
Program Manager

Game Plan Tech is seeking an experienced and highly motivated Project Manager to lead and manage critical IT projects for our public sector clients. The Platform Readiness team is building an internal developer tooling capability that embeds platform readiness intelligence directly into GitLab's software development lifecycle to solve this problem.

GitLab is an open-core software company that develops the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps, used by more than 100,000 organizations and 50 million people. Our mission is to unlock every team to ship trusted software at the speed of imagination.

Software is increasingly built by machines and directed by people. When agentic coding tools accelerate without context, governance, and lifecycle control, teams get speed with chaos. GitLab enables speed with control: customers deploy agents across the software development lifecycle (SDLC) with the orchestration, context, security, and governance to ship trusted software at scale.

The same principles show up in how we work. We build a culture of excellence around Speed with Quality, Ownership Mindset, and Customer Outcomes, and we treat AI as a core productivity multiplier. Every team member is expected to put AI into daily workflows to move faster without losing control. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued.

An overview of this role

As Principal Program Manager, Go-To-Market, you own two equal pillars of go-to-market execution for Product & Technical Marketing (PTM). First, you are the strategic and hands-on architect behind GitLab's high-stakes minor and major launches, redesigning the launch operating model with AI agents at its core so customers discover, adopt, and experience GitLab with precision. 

Second, you run program management on key initiatives that span Product Management and Product Design through Growth Marketing, Comms and Social, and Field Enablement, wherever those motions depend on PTM. PTM team  is responsible for product and solutions marketing, technical writing and documentation, developer advocacy, and globalization, and acts as the glue between these functions across a variety of go-to-market initiatives.

You are AI-first by default. When programs still run on many manual steps, you convert that work into team-wide AI workflows, either by shipping the automations yourself or by partnering with the AI Transformation Owner (ATO) for the marketing organization to drive shared skills, adoption, and governance. You are not a reactive deadline chaser. You drive solutions with stakeholders as dates approach, design decision stages so tradeoffs land early, and redesign stages and workflows when product roadmap, growth priorities, or major launch decisions change. You create clarity in ambiguity: frame the problem, present options and tradeoffs, name owners, and optimize for decision velocity.

In your first year, you institutionalize a dual operating system: a scalable launch framework for 15+ minor and major launches per year, and a portfolio program practice that maps dependencies from Product and Design through PTM into Growth, Comms, and Field. You ship production agent workflows that cut manual coordination, establish benchmarks for quality, and make go-to-market program management achieve relevance in the AI era, and become a trusted partner across the organization. 

Reporting to the VP of Product & Technical Marketing, you operate with significant executive visibility and autonomy. You measure success by what lands for customers and the business: pipeline where it matters, and brand and community impact where business requires it, not by activity volume alone.

Some examples of projects:

  • Orchestrate minor launches that put new platform releases in front of the community
  • Orchestrate major launches tied to company events that move pipeline
  • Orchestrate weekly signal announcements so we stay present in a fast-moving ecosystem
  • Sequence product decisions into PTM and other go-to-market functions, with clear handoffs
  • Keep field enablement on track when they depend on messaging and sales assets
  • Design decision points early so blockers show up before the deadline
  • Scope launches for pipeline and for post-launch adoption when agentic products are involved
  • Build AI workflows that draft briefs, synthesize status, and cut manual program steps
  • Rebuild stages and calendars when roadmap, growth priorities, or launch plans change
  • Run retrospectives that improve the system, and remove process as often as you add it

What you'll do

  • Run a concurrent portfolio of PTM-dependent initiatives with clear owners, dates, and tradeoffs
  • Give leadership the context to decide: risks, options, and a recommendation, not status theater
  • Align go-to-market functions when work streams collide or compete for the same people
  • Codify how programs run so each cycle starts sharper than the last
  • Put quality in the path of the work, then confirm market-facing pieces landed as intended
  • Turn recurring coordination into shared AI workflows the team can run without you in the loop
  • Partner with Marketing's ATO when a workflow needs department-wide adoption or guardrails
  • Escalate early with a clear ask when a call sits above the working team
  • Protect focus with smaller core teams, fewer standing meetings, more working sessions
  • Close the loop on results with the data team, then feed what you learn into the next cycle

What you'll bring

  • Program management for go-to-market across the high-tech industry, with first-hand experience with complex, multi-stakeholder and cross-functional initiatives.
  • Experience building and scaling how programs run in large, distributed orgs, with clear results 
  • Hands-on work with AI agents and automations that real teams used in production
  • A track record of turning manual work into AI workflows and helping others adopt them
  • Comfort standing up launch and program frameworks without adding busywork
  • Strong grasp of how product releases and how they impact go-to-market teams
  • Bias to action for priorities: defining risks and clear options for path forward
  • Habit of measuring success by pipeline, adoption, or consumption, not activity counts
  • Ability to run several high-stakes workstreams at once without dropping quality or trust
  • Clear writing and speaking with executives; gets decisions made across competing priorities
  • Influence without direct authority, including with senior leaders
  • Fluency with project tools with AI automation on top, and the ability to use GitLab
  • Ability to travel if needed and comply with the company's travel policy

About the team

Product & Technical Marketing at GitLab is the engine behind how GitLab positions, launches, documents, and evangelizes its value proposition for enterprises worldwide. We connect GitLab's product capabilities to customers and prospects across technical personas and executive buyers, and we partner closely with Product Management, Product Design, Growth Marketing, Comms and Social, Field Enablement, Sales, and the broader go-to-market organization so what we build lands in market with clarity, impact, and relevance. We operate as one marketing organization with clear roles: PTM carries the message; Growth activates demand; Comms amplifies narrative; work moves when handoffs are explicit.

You serve as the senior operational and program spine inside Product & Technical Marketing. You translate roadmap and positioning strategy into coordinated launches and PTM-dependent initiatives across the go-to-market chain, while building the playbooks and AI-powered workflows that make excellence repeatable at scale. We are building towards an operational model where agents handle the scaffolding of cross-functional programs, freeing team members to focus on strategy and judgement.

Title: Program Manager
Description:
GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. We believe cash transfers are one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid, with the research to back it up. Our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026. 

Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We support high ownership and real professional growth. Curious about what it's really like to work here? Read our values and hear from the people who do. If they resonate, this could be a great fit!

Program Manager

Location: Maputo or Nampula, with extensive travel to program sites (e.g. Nampula, Sofala, Maputo)

Reports to: Program Director

Level: Manager

About GiveDirectly

GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to over 2 million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. We believe cash transfers are one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid, backed by a large and growing body of research. Our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post, and we were named one of Time100's Most Influential Companies of 2026.

In Mozambique, GiveDirectly delivers large-scale unconditional cash transfers to households in Nampula province, is scaling a national cash transfer program in partnership with the Government of Mozambique, and is building MobileAid, a rapid cash-response model for emergencies. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical; we support high ownership and real professional growth.

About This Role

The Program Manager (PM) will own end-to-end field operations for one or more GiveDirectly Mozambique programs. The PM will be instrumental in driving enrollment and payment targets, building and managing field teams, coordinating with telecom and mobile money partners, government counterparts, and community leaders, and surfacing operational and safeguarding risk early. This is a high-autonomy role with significant responsibility for building the team and processes beneath it.

The PM will sit within the GiveDirectly Mozambique senior leadership team, and cross-functionally with Global Programs, Fundraising, Technology, Data, Safeguarding, and Internal Audit teams. We're looking for someone highly independent and solutions-oriented, comfortable moving between strategic ownership and hands-on tactical work, who thrives with limited day-to-day supervision in a fast-paced, tech-driven operating environment.

What You'll Do

Program Management & Delivery (~50%)

  • Own end-to-end operations for enrollment, verification, and payment delivery, setting and tracking quantifiable targets (households enrolled, disbursement timelines, operational efficiency).
  • Serve as GiveDirectly's engine for continuous improvement of enrollment, follow-up, and recipient-experience processes.
  • Coordinate with mobile money and telecom partners (e.g. Vodacom, Movitel) to ensure smooth, secure payment delivery, and lead troubleshooting when payments stall or are delayed.
  • Monitor operational and fraud risk in coordination with GiveDirectly's Internal Audit team; identify and close loopholes.
  • Uphold safeguarding standards across field operations, and design enrollment, payment, and community-engagement processes that prioritize recipients’ safety.
  • Monitor security conditions in areas of operation to keep staff and recipients safe, and adapt field plans as conditions change.
  • Lead survey design and updates, and use data to track performance and inform decisions, working closely with GD's global Data team.
  • Build and maintain program documentation and knowledge-management materials for internal use and product development.

People Management (~20%)

  • Hire, train, and manage field staff (e.g. enrollment officers, field supervisors), building a performance-oriented culture with regular feedback and development.
  • Identify and coach high-potential field staff for advancement onto a quicker promotion trajectory.
  • Reduce dependence on senior management over time by building team capacity and delegating, creating leverage for the organizational leadership.
  • Role-model GiveDirectly's values, fostering a team culture that's ambitious, fast-paced, inclusive, and committed to excellence
  • Monitor team dynamics and morale, and drive team-building efforts.

Partnerships & Government Relations (~15%)

  • Establish and maintain strong relationships with government counterparts, donors, telecom/mobile money operators, and community-based partners.
  • Represent GiveDirectly in local coordination forums, and support hosting of donors, journalists, and other visitors.
  • Support partnership and fundraising efforts, tracking opportunities, contributing to proposals, and reporting to funders such as the World Bank.

Vision, Strategy & New Program Development (~15%)

  • Contribute to the Mozambique country office's overall vision and strategy, partnering with leadership on problem-solving.
  • Work with GiveDirectly’s Product team to design, test, and refine new protocols and highly scalable, tech-enabled program models.
  • Anticipate operational risks, from research partnerships, pilots, or expansion into new geographies and build mitigation plans.

What You'll Bring

  • Exceptional alignment with GiveDirectly's Values and demonstrated core competencies: emotional intelligence, problem solving, project management, follow-through, and fostering inclusivity.
  • A “player-coach” mindset, comfortable owning strategy while doing hands-on execution, including field-level troubleshooting.
  • 5+ years of management experience, ideally including managing managers, in a high-performance, fast-paced environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and in a self-directed manner, while proactively communicating upward about gaps and risks.
  • Strong project management skills, able to run multiple workstreams, distinguish “important” from “critical,” and build more efficient systems along the way.
  • Strong analytical and data skills, comfortable working with incomplete or messy datasets and translating findings into clear recommendations, with high proficiency in Excel.
  • Strong communication skills, written and verbal, across internal teams, government counterparts, and donors.
  • Fluency in Portuguese and English required.
  • Experience in cash transfer programming, social protection, humanitarian response, or a related field is a plus.
  • Comfort operating in both rural and urban field environments.
  • Master's degree preferred.

Our Commitment to Safeguarding

GiveDirectly is committed to observing all local, national, and international laws that protect children, vulnerable adults, and the basic human rights of all people. We maintain a policy of zero tolerance for sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEAH), and expect everyone who works for GiveDirectly to treat the protection and safeguarding of our recipients as a priority. GiveDirectly is a member of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme and conducts background and reference checks on potential hires.

The role will have significant responsibility and a high degree of autonomy in creating and managing a large team. 

What you’ll do 

Project Management: 

The PM will be responsible for managing all aspects of ground operations, including:

  • Owning end-to-end operations for enrollment, verification, and payment delivery, setting and tracking quantifiable targets. e.g., recipients enrolled and operational efficiency
  • Serving as the organization’s engine for continuous improvement of the enrolment and follow-up processes, and overall recipient experience
  • Coordinating with mobile money and telecom partners to ensure smooth, secure payment delivery, and lead troubleshooting when payments are delayed.
  • Monitoring security in the areas of operations to ensure the team and recipients can operate safely
  • Monitor operational and fraud risk in coordination with GiveDirectly's Internal Audit team; identify and close loopholes.
  • Uphold safeguarding standards across field operations, and design enrollment, payment, and community-engagement processes that prioritize recipients’ safety.
  • Lead survey design and updates, and use data to track performance and inform decisions, working closely with GD's global Data team.
  • Build and maintain program documentation and knowledge-management materials for internal use and product development.

People Management: 

  • Assisting the HR Manager in Hiring, training, and managing field staff, building a performance-oriented culture with regular feedback and development.
  • Running performance reviews for direct reports and building their capacity to do the same for their reports
  • Role-model GiveDirectly's values, fostering a team culture that's ambitious, fast-paced, inclusive, and committed to excellence

Vision & Critical Thinking: 

  • Conceiving, developing and testing new protocols and methods before initiating scale-up
  • Anticipating areas of risk and creating mitigation plans 


Data and Analysis: 

  • Leading survey creation and updates for new and existing projects
  • Guiding and supporting direct reports on data inquiries, skill development, and data analysis
  • Working effectively with GD’s global tech team (framing needs and expectations, and holding self and others accountable to agreed timelines)

Partnerships & Government Relations 

  • Establish and maintain strong relationships with government counterparts, donors, telecom/mobile money operators, and community-based partners.
  • Represent GiveDirectly in local coordination forums, and support hosting of donors, journalists, and other visitors.
  • Support partnership and fundraising efforts, tracking opportunities, contributing to proposals, and reporting to funders such as the World Bank.

What you’ll bring 

  • Demonstrated success in a high-performance work environment
  • Exceptional leadership ability with demonstrated success in motivating and developing junior staff
  • Strong interest in advancing the values and mission of GiveDirectly
  • Exceptional communication, organizational, and analytical skills, including a high level of proficiency with G-suite/Google workplace. 
  • At least 4-5 years of management experience, preferably managing managers
  • Excitement about owning challenging management tasks, including mentoring and motivating direct reports and the broader field team
  • Demonstrated ability to work in a highly independent and self-directed manner, while effectively communicating upward about gaps and risks
  • Ability to manage day-to-day operations while simultaneously building more robust and efficient systems
  • Experience overseeing operations aligned to a fixed budget
  • Fluency in English
  • Experience in cash transfer programming, social protection, humanitarian response, or a related field is a plus.
  • Comfort operating in both rural and urban field environments.
  • Master's degree preferred.

 

 

Working at GiveDirectly

Role Description

AI Governance Specialist will handle the day-to-day operational work needed to run the AI Governance Charter, including:

  • Drive governance lifecycle management activities for AI Agents and AI Use Cases.
  • Participate in controls evaluation and risk & controls self-assessments.
  • Partner closely with Business Unit Risk function, Risk, TPRM, Technology, and peer governance teams to ensure synergy and coordinated execution across AI Governance initiatives.
  • Assist in developing governance workflows, inventory management, and reporting activities.
  • Maintain and enhance centralized repositories used to track AI models and AI-enabled solutions.
  • Ensure AI assets are accurately documented, classified, and managed throughout their lifecycle.
  • Supporting use-case review and risk level classification.
  • Support other functions run their AI use-cases ensuring that they understand the guardrails/charter.
  • Monitor evolving AI regulations, standards/trends, integrating them into governance work plans.
  • Building awareness of the AI governance charter through periodic, focused training and workshops.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, Artificial Intelligence, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Law, Public Policy, Business Administration, Risk Management, or a related field.
  • 2/3+ years of hands-on experience in AI governance, technology governance, AI risk management, model governance, compliance, enterprise risk management, cybersecurity governance, or Responsible AI.
  • AI-literate without being a developer: able to understand at a conceptual level how AI and ML systems work, the risks they introduce (bias, hallucination, data leakage, model drift, and similar), and how to translate that into governance language.
  • Familiarity with emerging AI regulations and standards (e.g., NIST AI RMF, FS AI RMF, EU AI Act, ISO/IEC).
  • Exposure to model inventories, metadata management, model documentation, or governance processes is highly desirable.
  • Strong hands-on experience in:
    • Developing AI governance frameworks and policies.
    • Conducting AI risk assessments and model reviews.
    • Supporting regulatory compliance and AI audit activities.
    • Reviewing AI-generated governance documentation and risk assessments.
    • Implementing Responsible AI principles across enterprise AI initiatives.
  • Experience with governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platforms, documentation standards, or enterprise governance tools is preferred.
  • Experience with project management tools (Jira, Azure DevOps, Monday.com, or similar).
  • Excellent analytical thinking, policy writing, risk assessment, stakeholder communication, and written English skills.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to evaluate governance documentation objectively.
  • Ability to facilitate workshops and gather requirements from technical/non-technical stakeholders.
  • A collaborative, self-directed partner who is comfortable with ambiguity and evolving priorities in a function that is being built from the ground up.
  • Organized, reliable, and able to manage multiple requests, track deadlines, and stay composed while handling a steady volume of work.

Title: Software Engineer, Agents Governance
Description:
About Glean:
 
Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles.
 
At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level.
 
Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality.
 
If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more - deeply embedded where people get things done. You’ll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company.

About the Role:

Glean is looking for Backend/Infrastructure engineers to build the platform that makes enterprise agents safe, discoverable, reliable, and governable at scale. You will work on agent publishing, sharing, moderation, policy enforcement, permissions, versioning, observability, and spend management. This is a distributed-systems and security-sensitive problem spanning platform infrastructure, product systems, and enterprise administration.

You will own problems from definition and architecture through production launch and operation, turning ambiguous requirements into durable platform primitives.

You will:

As a Software Engineer at Glean, Own impactful systems from design through reliable production operation.

  • Write clear design documents and make sound tradeoffs across security, reliability, performance, user experience, and cost.
  • Build well-tested backend services and platform components with strong correctness and operational guarantees.
  • Solve distributed-systems problems involving consistency, idempotency, retries, ordering, migrations, and safe rollout.
  • Partner with Product, Security, Infrastructure, and customer-facing teams to turn enterprise needs into scalable capabilities.
  • Make governance decisions auditable: who changed what, which policy applied, why access was allowed or denied, and what happened during a run.
  • Improve monitoring, alerting, debugging, incident response, and operational maturity.
  • Mentor engineers and help shape the roadmap around the highest-leverage platform problems.

About you:

  • BA/BS in computer science, or related degree
  • 6+ years building production backend, infrastructure, or cloud-native systems.
  • Strong coding skills in Go, Python, Java, C++, or a similar language.
  • Experience with distributed systems, APIs, storage, asynchronous workflows, or control planes.
  • Strong instincts around identity, authorization, tenancy, policy enforcement, auditability, and sensitive data access.
  • Able to reason about failure modes, system boundaries, invariants, and operational tradeoffs.
  • Customer-focused, proactive, and comfortable owning ambiguous problems and production issues.
  • Strong technical writing, communication, and collaboration skills.
  • Experience with GCP, AWS, or Azure is a plus.
  • Experience with AI agents, workflow systems, developer platforms, or enterprise administration is a plus.

Location:

  •   This role is in person in Bangalore, India.

Title: Content Marketing Specialist
Description:

Motive empowers the people who run physical operations with tools to make their work safer, more productive, and more profitable. For the first time ever, safety, operations and finance teams can manage their drivers, vehicles, equipment, and fleet related spend in a single system. Combined with industry leading AI, the Motive platform gives you complete visibility and control, and significantly reduces manual workloads by automating and simplifying tasks.

Motive serves nearly 100,000 customers – from Fortune 500 enterprises to small businesses – across a wide range of industries, including transportation and logistics, construction, energy, field service, manufacturing, agriculture, food and beverage, retail, and the public sector.

Visit gomotive.com to learn more.

About the Role:

The Content Marketing Specialist executes high-quality content that drives organic search visibility, supports content operations and programs, and brings an open, builder-oriented mindset to understanding Motive’s industry, customers, and content needs. This role sits within the Content Marketing team and is responsible for producing blog content, supporting content marketing programs by working with cross-functional partners to create content that maintains our standards and pushes our creativity, and identifying and building workflows that improve how the team manages content operations.

At this level, you're producing high-quality content and you're asking how the production process itself can be made smarter, more scalable, and more impactful. You work with structure and supervision, and you're actively building toward the point where you're solving problems before they're handed to you.

What You'll Do:

  • Write and publish high-quality blog content focused on customer stories, industry verticals, product features, SEO- or AEO-optimized topics, and more
  • Support the execution of content across Content Marketing’s cross-functional programs, including supporting some combination of product marketing, demand generation, corporate campaigns, and customer marketing.
  • Explore AI-assisted workflows to improve the team's ability to scale content production, recycle assets reliably, and identify high-value customer proof points
  • Participate in content planning processes, contributing research-backed recommendations on topics, content formats, and production priorities
  • Track content performance for published pieces, using data to refine approach and inform future production priorities

What We're Looking For:

  • 2+ years of content marketing or editorial experience, with a portfolio that demonstrates strong research and writing skills across B2B topics; or equivalent professional experience in content-adjacent fields (communications, journalism, etc.)
  • Demonstrated ability to produce clear, well-structured, accurate content on complex or technical subjects, particularly at the intersection of industry verticals and technology
  • Solid understanding of SEO and AEO principles, with experience applying them in editorial planning or content production a nice to have
  • Highly organized and deadline-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple projects and surface dependencies before they become problems
  • Comfort using data and research tools to inform content decisions, identify gaps, and measure performance
  • Early adopter mindset — curiosity about AI tools and a track record of testing and implementing new approaches to improve output quality or process efficiency
  • Strong collaboration skills; comfortable working across PMM, SEO, campaigns, and other teams to gather information, align on priorities, and keep projects on track
  • Familiarity with the physical operations, fleet management, or transportation space is a plus
  • LOCATION: Must be in the Austin, Texas areas (2 days a week in the office)

Title: Technical Program Manager, Battery
Description:
Gotion Inc. is based in Silicon Valley, CA, currently building a Manufacturing facility in Manteno, IL and has R&D centers in Ohio, China, Japan and Europe. We innovate in the next generation electric vehicle and energy storage technologies (lithium batteries and related systems) with the aim to accelerate electrified transportation and achieve sustainable development. Gotion is powered by a leading power battery technology company that provides solutions for vehicles including the world's first mass commercial e-bus route.

Gotion is a career destination - we are not simply attempting to just fill another job, but to pursue a dream of global green energy together! We offer outstanding opportunities to individuals seeking an exciting and challenging working environment. Everyone is highly valued and plays a vital role in the growth of our organization.

This role is in Irvine CA.

Key Responsibilities: 

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for US customers throughout battery cell and/or pack development programs 
  • Lead customer engagement, including technical discussions, program reviews, issue resolution, and escalation management 
  • Lead and facilitate technical meetings and workshops; ensure clear documentation, action tracking, and alignment with internal teams and customers 
  • Lead cross functional teams throughout RFI/RFQs process and technical proposals in collaboration with engineering and commercial teams 
  • Lead the development of battery cell and pack programs from concept through production, coordinating closely with customers and internal cross functional teams 
  • Develop, maintain, and communicate detailed program schedules, milestones, and deliverables 
  • Identify program risks across technical, schedule, cost, and quality and drive mitigation plans 
  • Coordinate cross-functional teams including engineering, manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and commercial across regions to meet program timing, deliverables and cost 
  • Regularly communicate program status, risks, and key decisions to engineering and executive leadership 
  • Identify and drive innovative solutions to overcome technical and program obstacles while maintaining schedule adherence 
  • Prioritize and track cross-functional action items, balancing resources, risks, and program outcomes 
  • Support on-site customer meetings, technical workshops, and plant visits in the US and China 
  • Support DFMEA, PFMEA, DV/PV, APQP, and PPAP activities as required by customer programs 
  • Up to 30% domestic and international travel 

Qualifications: 

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Mechanical, Electrical, Chemical, Materials, or related discipline) 
  • 3+ years of experience in automotive, EV, or energy storage product development 
  • 5+ years of experience in Technical Program Management, Program Management, or equivalent customer-facing leadership roles 
  • Good understanding of Li-ion battery cell and/or battery pack systems, including development and validation processes 
  • Proven experience working directly with US or global automotive OEM customers 
  • Solid knowledge of automotive product development and launch processes, including DV/PV, APQP, and PPAP 
  • Demonstrated ability to manage complex technical programs involving multiple stakeholders, tight timelines, and evolving requirements 
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, with the ability to clearly communicate with customers and senior leadership 
  • Willingness and ability to travel internationally as required

The base pay range for this role is shown below, and will depend on your skills, qualifications, experiences, and location.

$200,000—$240,000 USD
