Title: Program Manager, Construction & Energy Infrastructure
Description:
Gotion Inc. is based in Silicon Valley, CA, currently building a Manufacturing facility in Manteno, IL and has R&D centers in Ohio, China, Japan and Europe. We innovate in the next generation electric vehicle and energy storage technologies (lithium batteries and related systems) with the aim to accelerate electrified transportation and achieve sustainable development. Gotion is powered by a leading power battery technology company that provides solutions for vehicles including the world's first mass commercial e-bus route.

Gotion is a career destination - we are not simply attempting to just fill another job, but to pursue a dream of global green energy together! We offer outstanding opportunities to individuals seeking an exciting and challenging working environment. Everyone is highly valued and plays a vital role in the growth of our organization.

About the Market Management Department

The Market Management department is the core commercial engine of Gotion Illinois New Energy, established and led by the Head of Market Management (Business Development). The department encompasses sales and business development, BESS power station deployment, Virtual Power Plant and peak shaving programs, commercial EV charging, backup power applications, utility and contract negotiations, government and public affairs, construction and union coordination, and strategic advisory services. This role joins a lean, high-impact team operating at the intersection of business, policy, and clean energy infrastructure.

Position Overview

The Program Manager, Construction & Energy Infrastructure is a dual-function role within the Market Management Center at Gotion Illinois New Energy. This position is responsible for overseeing the planning, execution, and delivery of energy infrastructure projects including the Pioneer Power Station BESS and future hub deployments while simultaneously managing all on-site construction activity, contractor coordination, and project milestones. The ideal candidate brings a strong program management background combined with direct construction field experience and is comfortable operating at both a strategic and hands-on level.

Key Responsibilities:

Program & Project Management 

  • Own end-to-end program planning across energy infrastructure projects, from development through commercial operation date (COD). 
  • Maintain integrated master schedules, track milestones, and proactively flag risks to project timelines and budgets. 
  • Coordinate across internal teams (engineering, procurement, legal, government relations) and external partners (EPC contractors, utilities, interconnection teams). 
  • Manage scope, schedule, and budget performance across concurrent projects, escalating issues as appropriate. 
  • Support preparation of executive updates and project status reports for Director and senior leadership. 

Construction Management 

  • Serve as the Owner's on-site representative during construction phases, managing contractor and subcontractor performance against EPC agreements. 
  • Conduct regular site walks, safety inspections, and progress reviews; document findings and drive corrective actions. 
  • Review and approve contractor submittals, RFIs, change orders, and payment applications in coordination with the project team. 
  • Coordinate with ComEd, permitting authorities, and inspectors to support timely interconnection, energization, and certificate of occupancy milestones. 
  • Ensure construction activities comply with applicable safety standards, OSHA requirements, and site-specific protocols. 
  • Manage site access, logistics, and material staging to maintain an organized and efficient construction environment. 

Cross-Functional Coordination 

  • Collaborate with the Sales Electrical Engineer to align technical specifications with commercial deliverables and customer requirements. 
  • Support hub expansion planning by applying lessons learned from Pioneer to subsequent domestic and international deployments. 
  • Interface with the Power Station Manager on operational readiness and commissioning coordination. 
  • Assist in developing and maintaining project documentation, SOPs, and lessons-learned records to support a repeatable hub model. 

Qualifications & Requirements

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in construction management, Engineering, Project Management, or a related field. 
  • 5+ years of experience in program or project management, with at least 2 years in construction management or owner's representative capacity. 
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex, multi-stakeholder construction or energy infrastructure projects. 
  • Familiarity with EPC contract structures, order management, and contractor oversight. 
  • Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams under deadline pressure. 
  • Proficiency in project management tools (MS Project, Smartsheet, or equivalent) and standard MS Office applications. 
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills; comfortable presenting to senior leadership. 

Preferred:

  • Experience in utility-scale battery energy storage, solar, or grid infrastructure projects. 
  • Familiarity with PJM interconnection processes, ComEd coordination, or Illinois permitting requirements. 
  • Experience working with SPV or joint venture project structures. 
  • PMP, CCM, or equivalent professional certification. 
  • Bilingual (English/Mandarin) is a plus but not required. 

Additional Information:

  • This position requires regular on-site presence at the Manteno, Illinois facility and construction sites. 
  • Occasional travel to other hub sites, partner facilities, or regulatory offices may be required. 
  • Must be able to perform site walks in varying weather conditions and navigate active construction environments.

Title: Staff Engineering Operations Technical Program Manager
Description:
About us

Graphcore is one of the world’s leading innovators in Artificial Intelligence compute. It is developing hardware, software and systems infrastructure that will unlock the next generation of AI breakthroughs and power the widespread adoption of AI solutions across every industry.

As part of the SoftBank Group, Graphcore is a member of an elite family of companies responsible for some of the world’s most transformative technologies. Together, they share a bold vision: to enable Artificial Super Intelligence and ensure its benefits are accessible to everyone.

Graphcore’s teams are drawn from diverse backgrounds and bring a broad range of skills and perspectives. A melting pot of AI research specialists, silicon designers, software engineers and systems architects, Graphcore enjoys a culture of continuous learning and constant innovation.

 

Job Summary

We are seeking a Staff Hardware Engineer to provide advanced operational, diagnostic, and engineering support for Graphcore’s Arm-based hardware platforms across lab and data center environments.

This role focuses on supporting hardware bring-up, validation, and troubleshooting of complex AI compute platforms, including server blades, racks, and rack-scale infrastructure. The successful candidate will collaborate closely with engineering, platform, and data center teams to ensure the reliability and performance of next-generation AI systems.

 

The Team

The Systems Engineering and Hardware Engineering teams are responsible for enabling the bring-up, validation, and operational reliability of Graphcore’s AI infrastructure platforms.

The team works closely with server engineering, firmware teams, platform architects, and data center operations to support the development, testing, and deployment of next-generation AI compute systems.

This collaborative environment enables rapid problem-solving and continuous improvement of Graphcore’s hardware platforms from early development through production deployment.

 

Responsibilities and Duties

  • Lead advanced break-fix troubleshooting for server blades, motherboards, power systems, and rack-scale infrastructure.
  • Support engineering bring-up activities, including component validation and firmware interaction testing.
  • Diagnose system-level failures involving thermal behavior, power anomalies, network configuration, and BIOS/BMC issues.
  • Collaborate with server engineering teams to perform root cause analysis and propose corrective actions or design improvements.
  • Support deployment and rollout of next-generation hardware platforms through structured validation and qualification cycles.
  • Interface with facilities and infrastructure teams to understand environmental factors impacting system reliability.
  • Develop and maintain standard operating procedures (SOPs), troubleshooting guides, and validation documentation.
  • Provide guidance and mentorship to junior technicians and engineers on troubleshooting methodologies and hardware diagnostics.
  • Participate in on-call rotations or off-hours support during critical engineering milestones or hardware bring-up phases.

Candidate Profile

Essential

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related discipline.
  • 8 years of strong experience with server hardware architectures and board-level debugging.
  • Experience analyzing system logs, hardware telemetry, and power/thermal metrics to isolate hardware failures.
  • Hands-on experience with HPC systems, AI compute platforms, or rack-scale infrastructure.
  • Strong collaboration skills and ability to work effectively in fast-paced engineering environments.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Desirable

  • Experience supporting prototype or pre-production hardware bring-up.
  • Familiarity with data center facilities, including liquid cooling and power distribution systems.
  • Experience using Python, Bash, or automation tools for hardware validation or troubleshooting.
  • Exposure to structured failure analysis and reliability engineering methodologies.

 

USA Benefits
In addition to a competitive salary, Graphcore offers flexible working and a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your health, wellbeing and financial future. Our benefits include medical, dental and vision coverage, Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs), Health Savings Accounts (HSAs), disability and life insurance, a 401(k) retirement plan, commuter benefits, wellness services and an Employee Assistance Programme (EAP). We welcome people of different backgrounds and experiences; we're committed to building an inclusive work environment that makes Graphcore a great home for everyone. We offer an equal opportunity process and understand that there are visible and invisible differences in all of us. We can provide a flexible approach to interview and encourage you to chat to us if you require any reasonable adjustments.

Title: Technical Program Manager
Description:
Who we are
Graviton Research Capital is a privately funded quantitative trading firm. We trade across a multitude of asset classes and trading venues using a diverse range of concepts, from time series analysis and stochastic models to machine learning and statistical inference. We analyse terabytes of data to identify pricing anomalies and drive innovation in financial markets.

Role Overview
We are looking for a Program Manager who thrives at the intersection of rigorous engineering and predictable delivery. You will not just "manage tasks" — you will orchestrate the development lifecycle for mission-critical systems. Your goal is to ensure that our elite engineering teams can focus on high-performance code while you own the execution strategy, dependency mapping, and release discipline.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead Agile ceremonies (Sprint Planning, Stand-ups, Retrospectives) tailored for deep-tech engineering teams.
  • Transform high-level trading requirements into granular, executable backlogs. Own capacity planning and burn-down metrics to provide high-visibility delivery timelines.
  • Navigate the complex interplay between engineering teams (e.g., Connectivity, Core Infrastructure, Simulation) to prevent bottlenecks.
  • Build and maintain advanced Jira dashboards, automated roadmaps, and Confluence documentation that serve as the "single source of truth" for stakeholders.
  • Proactively identify technical debt, architectural blockers, or resource gaps that threaten release stability.
  • Continuously refine Agile methodologies to suit low-latency, performance-sensitive development cycles (where "Definition of Done" includes rigorous performance benchmarking).

Eligibility & Required Skills

  • 5+ years of experience as a TPM, Program Manager, or Scrum Lead in a product-engineering environment (HFT, FinTech, Networking, or Kernels/Systems).
  • A strong grasp of the software development lifecycle for high-performance systems. While you won't write code, you must understand concepts like build systems, CI/CD, and performance regressions.
  • Familiarity with capital markets and trading concepts; prior exposure to a trading, quant research, or investment environment is a plus
  • Expert-level proficiency in Jira Service Management/Software and Confluence. Ability to use JQL for advanced reporting.
  • Exposure to low-latency, trading systems, capital markets, networking, or infra software preferred.
  • Exceptional ability to translate complex technical constraints into clear business updates for Engineering Leads and Partners.

Title: IT & CyberSecurity Program Manager
Description:
About Harbinger

Harbinger is an American commercial electric vehicle (EV) company on a mission to transform an industry starving for innovation. Harbinger’s best-in-class team of EV, battery, and drivetrain experts have pooled their deep experience to bring a first-of-its-kind EV platform to support the growing demand for medium-duty EVs and Hybrids. Harbinger: Familiar Form, Revolutionary Foundation.

Role Summary


Harbinger is hiring an IT & Cybersecurity Program Manager to be the operational driver for the IT and Cybersecurity team's roadmap. This person will work side-by-side with the IT & Cybersecurity Director on a daily basis, turning strategy and OKRs into scoped, sequenced, and delivered initiatives. 

What You'll Do:

  • Own the quarterly OKR and project backlog process with the IT Director, scoring, sequencing, and staffing initiatives against team capacity and budget
  • Drive cross-project initiatives spanning IT Engineering, Cybersecurity, and Operations, keeping scope, timelines, dependencies, and risk visible
  • Build and run the IT/Cyber change management program end to end
  • Maintain the reporting and dashboards leadership needs to see program health at a glance
  • Drive the SOX ITGC, SOC 2, and IPO-readiness security roadmap, including remediation of risk assessment and penetration test findings
  • Track vulnerability management, access reviews, and vendor risk assessments against SLAs with Cybersecurity
  • Lead vendor evaluations and system implementations from requirements to go live and beyond
  • Facilitate planning and resolve cross-team dependencies across IT/Cyber and partner functions (Engineering, Operations, People Ops, Legal, Finance)

Experience

  • Experience running programs in a fast-paced, high-growth or pre-IPO environment strongly preferred

Technical Competencies

  • Strong working knowledge of IT infrastructure, enterprise applications, and security fundamentals (identity/access management, network segmentation, vulnerability management) sufficient to make informed scoping and design tradeoffs
  • Advanced Jira and Confluence usage: workflows, automation rules, JQL, dashboards, cross-project linking
  • Familiarity with change management/ITIL practices and SOX ITGC or SOC 2 control frameworks
  • Comfortable reading vendor documentation, RFP responses, and security assessments critically

Soft Skills

  • Excellent written and verbal communication. Able to translate between technical detail and executive level summary
  • Strong bias to action and follow-through. Comfortable being the person who drives a decision to closure rather than waiting for one
  • Trusted, low-ego operator who can work in lockstep with the IT Director as a true partner

  • Annual Vacation Bonus
  • Wellness & Fertility Benefits

  • Complimentary Meals & Stocked Kitchens

Title: Future Special Education Teacher Opportunities
Description:
Future Special Education Teacher Opportunities

Location: Philadelphia, PA                                                                                           

Compensation:  $55,000 - $88,000 (more details below)                                                      

Contact: jobs@hebrewpublic.org

About Hebrew Public

Hebrew Public is a small and growing network of schools operated by Hebrew Public: Charter Schools for Global Citizens. Hebrew Public is a secular organization that welcomes candidates of all backgrounds into a supportive and inclusive community.

Across the network, Hebrew Public schools serve children from all backgrounds and help students become global citizens who are strong problem solvers, aware communicators, and lifelong learners committed to making a positive difference in the world around them. Our schools are models of racial and economic integration, academic excellence, and world language learning.

Why PHP?

As part of Hebrew Public, Philadelphia Hebrew Public teachers and staff bring our mission to life with students from more than 40 zip codes across Philadelphia, primarily Black and Brown students whose brilliance, curiosity, and potential drive our work every day.

PHP is rooted in the belief that every student deserves excellent teachers and an outstanding education. Through rigorous academics, strong relationships, and a globally minded education, we help students expand what they see as possible for themselves.

We also invest in educators. Teachers receive coaching, collaborative planning, professional development, certification support, and opportunities to grow into leadership roles. Our compensation model recognizes teacher skill, growth, and classroom impact, not simply years of experience. After their first year, eligible teachers may qualify for 5% up to 10% annual salary increases based on their impact in the classroom, without needing additional graduate coursework. 

For educators who want to make a meaningful difference while growing their own careers, PHP offers the opportunity to do both.

You don’t need to speak Hebrew to apply, and we strongly encourage candidates from traditionally underrepresented groups to join our community.

The Opportunity

We are always open to meeting skilled, student-centered educators who may be a strong fit for future Special Education Teacher opportunities. Philadelphia’s education community is a small world, and we value building relationships with excellent teachers, even when we do not have an immediate opening.

This evergreen talent-pipeline posting may not represent a current vacancy. Applications will be reviewed as staffing needs arise, and our Talent Team may contact candidates whose experience aligns with an available opportunity.

Special Education roles at PHP vary based on student needs. Teachers may provide push-in or pull-out services or lead a classroom serving students with moderate support needs. Across settings, Special Education Teachers deliver highly individualized instruction, implement IEPs, monitor student progress, and collaborate closely with families, general education teachers, service providers, and school leaders.

Teachers who lead classrooms for students with moderate support needs are also responsible for leading and supporting paraprofessionals, establishing clear roles and routines, providing ongoing guidance and feedback, and ensuring that instructional, behavioral, and individualized supports are implemented consistently.

What You’ll Do

  • Deliver highly individualized, standards-aligned instruction based on each student’s strengths, needs, and IEP goals
  • Provide push-in, pull-out, small-group, and/or specialized classroom instruction depending on the role
  • Lead a classroom serving students with moderate support needs, when applicable
  • Develop, implement, and monitor high-quality Individualized Education Programs (IEPs)
  • Use assessment and progress-monitoring data to adjust instruction and accelerate student growth
  • For moderate-needs classroom roles, lead and support paraprofessionals by setting clear expectations, coordinating student supports, and providing ongoing guidance and feedback
  • Partner with general education teachers to adapt curriculum, instruction, accommodations, and classroom supports
  • Maintain high expectations while creating a structured, inclusive, and supportive learning environment
  • Support students’ academic, social-emotional, behavioral, and functional development
  • Collaborate with families, related-service providers, teachers, and school leaders
  • Maintain accurate documentation and meet special education timelines and compliance requirements
  • Advocate for students and ensure they have meaningful access to rigorous learning experiences
  • Participate in coaching, collaborative planning, professional development, and feedback
  • Model our OLAM values: outstanding problem-solving, lifelong learning, aware communication, and making a difference

Who You Are

  • You believe in the limitless potential of every student and that all children deserve excellent teachers and an outstanding education
  • You are committed to urban education and closing opportunity and achievement gaps
  • You hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution
  • You believe students with disabilities deserve rigorous, individualized, and inclusive learning experiences
  • You understand differentiated instruction, accommodations, modifications, and evidence-based interventions
  • You can design and deliver highly individualized instruction responsive to a wide range of student needs
  • You use assessment and progress-monitoring data to make informed instructional decisions
  • You can develop and implement meaningful, measurable IEP goals
  • If leading a moderate-needs classroom, you are comfortable directing, coaching, and supporting paraprofessionals as part of a coordinated classroom team
  • You build strong relationships with students and families while maintaining high expectations
  • You welcome feedback and demonstrate the OLAM values in your work

Pennsylvania teacher certification in an applicable middle-level or subject area, or active progress toward certification, is preferred. Experience working with middle school students in urban school communities and familiarity with high-quality, standards-aligned instructional practices are also preferred. 

Benefits

Potential benefits* include:

  • Medical and dental coverage with 85% of premiums covered by the employer
  • Employer-paid vision coverage
  • A 5% employer retirement match with no vesting period
  • Paid time off, school holidays, and 6 weeks paid parental leave
  • Mental-health and employee-assistance resources
  • Professional development and certification partnerships
  • Additional stipends, performance-based compensation, and global travel opportunities

*Benefits packages vary depending on the role.

Our Commitment

We are committed to building a team that reflects the communities we serve. Candidates of color and those from backgrounds that are underrepresented in school leadership roles are strongly encouraged to apply.

If you need accommodations or assistance due to a disability, please reach out to us at jobs@hebrewpublic.org. This information will be treated as confidential and used only for the purpose of determining an appropriate accommodation for the interview process.

For more information please visit our websites below. 

  • CMO Website: www.hebrewpublic.org
  • School Website: https://philadelphiahebrewpublic.org/ 

Apply today at jobs@hebrewpublic.org and join PHP, where you can make a lasting impact on students while growing your practice and your career.

Title: Senior Technical Program Manager
Description:
Who we are:

Hellbender Inc. is a Pennsylvania Benefit Corporation who partners with innovators to mature their Artificial Intelligence enabled computing sensors and produce their solutions onshore at prototype to high volumes. 

Hellbender is intentionally forming an inclusive work environment and is committed to uplifting the historically marginalized identities including veterans, women, transgender people and underrepresented races in our community and industry.

Must be a U.S. Person

The Senior Technical Program Manager (STPM) leads cross-functional programs that bring Hellbender's hardware and software products from concept through production launch. This role coordinates engineering, manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and program stakeholders to ensure technical programs are delivered on schedule, within budget, and to specification. The STPM serves as the central point of accountability for program timelines, risk management, and cross-team communication in a multi-shift technology manufacturing environment.

  • Plan, schedule, and drive execution of complex, cross-functional technical programs from requirements definition through design, prototyping, testing, and production release

Competitive salary based on qualifications and experience

Benefits

  • 7.5 weeks total Paid time off

Pittsburgh

Hellbender is a growing business and follows a policy that prioritizes internal promotions. As new positions are created, new opportunities for advancement will be created as well.

Title: Product Manager - Workflows
Description:
About Us

Herald is transforming how commercial insurance gets sold. We combine modern API infrastructure with industry-specific AI that can read emails, extract data, generate quotes, and guide brokers through submission workflows end-to-end. The result: faster placement, cleaner operations, and meaningful revenue growth. The market is huge, the need is obvious, and the product we’re building doesn’t exist yet. If you want to help shape the operating system for modern insurance, we’d love to work with you.

We’re a team of insurtech veterans with experience at At-Bay, Kin,  and Insurify. We’ve raised our Series A funding from top-tier VCs (Lightspeed, Brewer Lane,  Afore, Underscore) along with a panel of insurtech founders (At-Bay, Marble), insurance executives (CRC), and early employees of other successful API infrastructure companies (Plaid, Alloy).

The Role

As a Product Manager you’ll own the Herald placement application — the primary working surface brokers use to manage commercial submissions end to end. This is a high-ownership, user-facing role where you'll translate real broker workflows into product decisions and ship features that meaningfully reduce manual effort in the insurance placement process.

You'll work directly with users from day one, partner closely with engineering to ship fast, and use AI both as a personal productivity tool and as a lens for identifying where automation can meaningfully change how brokers work. When projects require it, you'll also own the carrier work needed to bring new markets or capabilities into the platform, but the broker experience is your primary focus.

AI is a core part of how we expect this role to operate. You'll reach for AI tools habitually in your own work, and you'll help identify where AI and agentic workflows can be layered into the product to reduce coordination overhead, surface the right information at the right time, and let brokers focus on the work that actually requires their judgment.

What You'll Do

The core product you'll own is the Placement System — Herald's platform for managing a commercial submission from intake through bind. It includes:

  • Application intake and form management — dynamic application forms that adapt to coverage type, prefill from uploaded documents via AI extraction, and surface what digital carriers still need
  • Market outreach — digital submission to carrier APIs and templated offline outreach, with a unified view of where every market stands
  • Quote review and comparison — structured quote data across digital and offline markets, coverage-level detail views, and exportable comparison outputs
  • AI-assisted coordination — submission-scoped chat, AI summaries, and agentic actions that let brokers delegate routine coordination

Beyond the core workspace, your project backlog will span the broader placement product — work like:

  • Improving document extraction accuracy and coverage for the prefill and data-capture flows
  • Expanding agentic capabilities: defining where the platform should act autonomously, where it should surface recommendations, and where a human needs to stay in the loop
  • Scoping and launching new carrier integrations when they're required to unlock new market access for users
  • Improving monitoring and self-healing for the integration layer that feeds market data into the workspace

 

What You'll Bring

Required

  • 2–3 years of experience in product management or a closely adjacent role (e.g., product engineering, solutions engineering, implementation PM, or technical program management) in a B2B SaaS environment
  • Habitual, fluent use of AI tools in your own work — you reach for AI to draft communications, investigate problems, synthesize information, and reduce repetitive effort; you have well-developed instincts for where AI helps and where it falls short
  • Strong instincts for UX and an ability to simplify complex processes — the placement workflow is multi-step, involves many stakeholders, and has real consequences; you design for clarity under that complexity
  • Comfort working with engineering teams building AI-powered products — you understand how to design features that build trust in AI outputs, what it means to evaluate them, and where human oversight needs to stay
  • Demonstrated ability to work with real users, understand operational pain, and translate what you learn into crisp product decisions
  • Strong writer — you communicate product rationale clearly in specs, Slack, and in the room with skeptical users
  • Clear communicator and fast executor — you move quickly, write things down, and pull the right people in at the right time

Nice to Have

  • Experience in commercial insurance, insuretech, or a closely adjacent vertical — familiarity with carrier-distribution dynamics and how quoting, submission, and binding workflows operate
  • Prior experience at a company building workflow automation, document processing, or AI-assisted tools for enterprise users
  • Experience designing or scoping AI-assisted or agentic workflows — you understand where automation adds value, how to evaluate AI outputs in operational contexts, and how to build processes that keep humans appropriately in the loop
  • Familiarity with REST APIs and how they underpin product features — you can read API documentation, understand what's technically feasible, and have informed conversations with engineers about integration design
  • Prior startup experience at a company in a similar stage (Series A–C); you know how to operate with lean support structures and build process where there isn't any

Full compensation packages are determined based on candidate experience. Please note that some roles may include variable compensation (such as commission, bonuses, and/or equity) that are not outlined here. This range is depicting base pay only. Any variable compensation will be discussed throughout the hiring process.

Title: Content Marketing Manager
Description:
Higher Logic exists to connect people, knowledge, and ideas to improve lives and organizations. Through our community solutions, we empower growth-stage businesses and associations to build a more engaged and meaningful relationship with their customers and members. Higher Logic serves more than 3,000 customers, representing over 350,000 online communities with greater than 200 million users in more than 42 countries worldwide. 

Our team is a thriving community of authentic people with diverse experiences and perspectives. We are honest and genuine and believe that sharing ideas and feedback openly helps us to be successful. We believe that diversity and empathy bring us #AllTogether to make us stronger. We learn from failure and successes because both help us to grow and learn. We strive to understand the why behind our actions and bring our best selves to work every day. 

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

Higher Logic is looking for a Content Marketing Manager to help us create useful, engaging content for two core audiences: associations and B2B companies. 

Reporting to the Senior Content Marketing Manager, this person will contribute ideas to Higher Logic’s broader content strategy and independently manage content projects from concept through publication and promotion. The role is highly hands-on and includes writing and editing blog posts, ebooks, guides, webinar content, website copy, and organic social media content. 

This person will also help manage Higher Logic’s social media presence. Social media experience is highly preferred, but this is not solely a social media position.  

The right candidate will be an adaptable writer and thoughtful marketer who enjoys working across formats, helping brands tell compelling stories, and turning business priorities into clear, valuable content. 

Higher Logic is a high-trust, collaborative organization. Some projects will begin with an established brief or campaign direction, while others will give this person the opportunity to recommend an approach and shape the work themselves. We are looking for someone who can become comfortable with our audiences, products, and voice and then confidently move projects forward without extensive day-to-day direction. 

Essential Duties and Responsibilities 

  • Create blog posts, ebooks, guides, webinar content, website copy, organic social content, and occasional email or campaign copy.  
  • Contribute ideas to the broader editorial calendar by identifying audience needs, industry developments, and timely content opportunities.  
  • Manage assigned content projects from initial concept through research, drafting, stakeholder review, revision, publication, and promotion.  
  • Help manage Higher Logic’s organic social media channels, including content planning, writing, scheduling, publishing, engagement, and performance reporting.  
  • Create social media carousels, short-form videos, and other visual content using established design templates.  
  • Interview and collaborate with subject matter experts to translate complex ideas, product information, research, and industry trends into clear and useful content.  
  • Adapt messaging for different audiences, formats, and channels while maintaining a consistent Higher Logic brand voice.  
  • Apply SEO and digital discoverability best practices to content planning and production.  
  • Manage freelance writers and other external content partners when projects are outsourced, including developing briefs, providing feedback, and maintaining deadlines and quality standards.  
  • Review content and social performance to identify lessons and opportunities for improvement.  
  • Collaborate closely with demand generation, product marketing, customer marketing, brand, design, subject matter experts, and other partners across Higher Logic.  
  • Conduct all business in accordance with Higher Logic values, policies, and procedures.  

Knowledge and Abilities Required 

  • At least three years of relevant experience in content marketing, editorial, communications, or a related field.  
  • Experience writing and editing both long-form and short-form content for multiple formats. 
  • Working knowledge of SEO principles and their application to content creation.  
  • Comfort using AI-powered tools and documented workflows to accelerate content development, streamline repeatable tasks, and improve team efficiency, while maintaining strong editorial judgment and quality control. 
  • Strong editorial judgment and the ability to turn complex or loosely defined topics into accessible, audience-focused content.  
  • Strong project-management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines.  
  • The initiative and judgment to move work forward independently while knowing when to seek input or collaboration.  
  • Comfort using performance data to evaluate content and inform future work.  
  • Experience collaborating with designers, marketers, subject matter experts, and other stakeholders.  
  • A bachelor’s degree in marketing, communications, journalism, or a related field, or equivalent relevant professional experience.  

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Experience managing organic social media channels for a brand or organization.  
  • Experience managing freelance writers, agencies, or content vendors.  
  • Familiarity with B2B SaaS, associations, membership organizations, online communities, or marketing technology.  
  • Familiarity with tools such as WordPress, Semrush, GA4, HubSpot, Salesforce, Hootsuite, Canva, ChatGPT, or Riverside.  

What You Can Expect 

  • A remote working environment, with access to Higher Logic’s Arlington-area headquarters for employees located near Washington, D.C.  
  • A collaborative marketing team that values thoughtful ideas, open feedback, and strong cross-functional partnerships.  
  • Meaningful ownership of projects and the autonomy to determine how your work takes shape.  
  • The opportunity to work across content formats, audience segments, and channels rather than being limited to one area of marketing.  
  • A team that is actively experimenting with AI and improving the way content work gets done.  

You’ll earn: 

  • Competitive compensation.
  • Comprehensive health benefits package. 
  • 401(k) plan with employer match. 
  • Healthcare and dependent-care flexible spending account. 
  • Company short-term and long-term disability insurance. 
  • Company culture that recognizes its employees. 
  • Room for growth and development and management that cares about your professional growth and will help you achieve your goals. 
  • Significant advancement opportunities for outstanding performers.

Title: Operations Program Manager - Safety & Sustainability
Description:
Founded in 2013, Home Chef is the leading meal solutions company with both a retail and online presence. Available online at homechef.com and in retail at more than 2,100 Kroger grocery stores, Home Chef is committed to inspiring and enabling more people to cook simple, delicious meals, no matter how busy they are.

In 2023, Home Chef introduced a new brand, Tempo! Tempo features a rotating selection of ready-to-heat meals delivered directly to your door. These meals are better-for-you versions of familiar favorites, designed to save you time and reduce stress while maintaining a healthy lifestyle. Our Tempo menu includes options that are protein-packed, fiber-rich, calorie and carb conscious, keto-friendly, and dietitian-approved.

Similar to our recipes, we recognize that variety is the spice of life, and therefore, our employees also bring their uniqueness and color to our fantastic team. We’re eager to work with humble team players and pragmatic next-level thinkers to innovate on Home Chef’s offerings.

 

The Safety & Sustainability Manager oversees the development and sustainment of all Safety, Health, and Environmental (EH&S) policies for all Home Chef facilities.

Detailed Responsibilities

Develops and Implements Health and Safety Policies, Programs, and Systems:

  • Promotes the strategy for the development and sustainability of the safety culture at Home Chef Facilitates network alignment to policies and regulatory compliance. Collaborates with site leadership to be proactive and identify the most impactful programs to prioritize
  • Responsible for integrating the strategies of the Home Chef Operating Systems into our everyday EH&S work, projects, and execution of our plant teams.

Training:

  • Ensures all required safety training content is created and implemented across all Home Chef facilities 
  • Develops a hopper of training opportunities and builds content with the associate learning experience in mind. 
  • Partners with department heads of sanitation, maintenance, and warehouse to ensure role specific safety training is developed and maintained. 
  • Creates an assessment and prioritization system to identify the most impactful training opportunities and where the current gaps are. 

Safety Metrics:

  • Maintains safety KPIs for Home Chef and generates reports to share with the broader Ops teams. Harnessing the data provided to create a culture that is proactive around safety.  
  • Translates the behavioral operation and incident management programs into actionable intel, and then enables our site leads to act with efficiency and accuracy. 
  • Builds and owns the framework for cross-network best practice sharing ensuring that actions taken in one location are effectively deployed at all locations to keep our teams safe. 

Incident Support: 

  • Creates standard documentation and response templates for regulatory inquiries, and supports the file development that the site Safety Manager needs to complete their response.
  • Enables site Safety Managers to focus entirely on actions and engaging with local regulatory teams, like OSHA, through research into compliance and effective management of incident documentation. 
  • Partners with HR and the plant Safety Managers on mitigating Workers Compensation claims, leveraging program strategy to affect existing claims and future proof against new claims. 

Sustainability:

  • Identifies and drives strategic initiatives to further Home Chef’s sustainability goals and remain ahead of local compliance, as well as, generate savings in food waste alternatives. 
  • Supports Home Chef goals for reducing utility usage and generating efficient facility operation. 
  • Partners with local and national providers to streamline Home Chef’s food and material waste processes.   

General Responsibilities:

  • Serves as the company’s subject matter expert for safety and is the point of escalation for all OSHA interactions
  • Takes on the responsibility of creating and maintaining a strong safety culture within Home Chef
  • Establishes a strong working relationship with Plant Managers and site Safety Managers
  • Partners closely with the Facilities Compliance Manager to ensure the Contractor Safety program is up to date and any PSM audit findings are corrected 
  • Seen as the subject matter expert of Safety for all corporate initiatives including, but not limited to, automation integration, facility improvements, and sanitation chemical additions 

This position requires 25% travel.

Qualifications

The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability needed for this role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities.

  • 1 - 5 years of experience in EHS team capacity preferred
  • Proficient in MS Office Suite or G Suite, specifically in PowerPoint/Google Slides and Excel/Google Slides
  • Ability to prioritize, meet strict deadlines, and maintain confidentiality
  • Must be available to respond to work related inquiries nights and weekends
  • Completion of a four-year degree program in a related field: Environmental or occupational safety & health or related field

More About Us

Perks and benefits

  • Candidates can experience Home Chef as a customer - enter promo code PEOPLE30 for $30 off your first order!
  • Medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurance available
  • Paid holidays, sick time and vacation time
  • 401k program
  • Flexible spending accounts for qualified medical, dependent care, parking, or transit expenses

How We Work Together

We are humble team players.
We are warm and gracious with team members and customers. We seek feedback to improve ourselves - and respectfully listen to and accept input.

We are pragmatic next-level thinkers.
We come up with novel and unique ideas. We explore new strategies to avoid being constrained by conventional thinking.

We take ownership.
We approach ambiguous problems, prepared to dive in, get curious, and learn more. We are results-driven, always challenging ourselves to exceed goals.

Be at Home at Home Chef

We all show up authentically at Home Chef. Our team includes individuals with a variety of identities, backgrounds, and perspectives. You can trust that you’ll be able to bring your whole self to an inclusive and enjoyable workplace.

We welcome people of all races, colors, religions, national origin or ancestry, sex (including sexual identity), age, physical or mental disabilities, pregnancy, veteran or military status, unfavorable discharge from military service, genetic information, sexual orientation, marital status, order of protection status, citizenship status, arrest record or expunged/sealed convictions, or any other legally recognized protected basis under federal, state, or local law.

Home Chef is committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, Home Chef will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations. If reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, or to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please contact our People team at hr@homechef.com.

Title: Director, Revenue Readiness
Description:
Reports to: VP, Revenue Operations

Location: Remote US

Compensation Range: $190,000 to $210,000 base plus bonus and equity

 

What We Do:

Huntress is a fully remote, global team of passionate experts and ethical badasses on a mission to break down the barriers to cybersecurity. Whether creating purpose-built security solutions, hunting down hackers, or impacting our community, our people go above and beyond to change the security game and make a real difference.

Founded in 2015 by former NSA cyber operators, Huntress protects all businesses—not just the 1%—with enterprise-grade, fully owned, and managed cybersecurity products at the price of an affordable SaaS application. The Huntress difference is our One Team advantage: our technology is designed with our industry-defining Security Operations Center (SOC) in mind and is never separated from our service.

We protect 3M+ endpoints and 1M+ identities worldwide, elevating underresourced IT teams with protection that works as hard as they do. As long as hackers keep hacking, Huntress keeps hunting.

What You’ll Do: 

You will lead across the revenue organization to establish the governance, operating standards, learning systems, and program discipline needed to prepare sellers and frontline managers consistently across roles, segments, motions, and geographies. You will shape priorities with senior GTM leaders, make clear investment and sequencing decisions, and lead your team and cross-functional partners through execution.

Perfect Imperfection guides how you work. You create enough structure to scale while continuing to learn and improve the model. You Give a $h*t about whether people are genuinely prepared to perform. You bring Candor when ownership or expectations are unclear, build trust by giving more than we take, and demonstrate Warrior Spirit as you lead meaningful organizational change. You are Outcome-Obsessed about building organizational readiness that helps Huntress execute its growth priorities.

Responsibilities: 

  • Set and lead the global Revenue Readiness vision, strategy, operating model, and multi-year roadmap, aligned with Huntress's growth priorities and the capabilities revenue teams need to execute them.
  • Serve as the senior functional leader for Revenue Readiness, advising GTM executives on organizational preparedness, capability needs, investment priorities, and the risks associated with major business changes.
  • Own the Revenue Readiness portfolio and make decisions about priorities, sequencing, capacity, and resource allocation based on business impact and the organization's ability to absorb change.
  • Build the foundational readiness infrastructure for Huntress, including program intake and prioritization, learning governance, delivery standards, reinforcement expectations, content lifecycle management, platform administration, and measurement.
  • Establish a consistent readiness architecture across new hire onboarding, role-based ramp, frontline manager readiness, major business changes, and ongoing development.
  • Create a scalable process for translating identified business needs, performance gaps, product launches, system changes, and new go-to-market expectations into structured readiness programs.
  • Partner with Sales Ops Business Partners to understand prioritized business needs and define the capabilities, behaviors, and measures of preparedness required to address them.
  • Establish clear ownership across Revenue Readiness, Sales Ops Business Partners, Sales Leaders, Product Marketing, GTM Systems, Technical Sales, and other subject matter experts. Revenue Readiness owns program architecture and operationalization, domain experts own subject matter accuracy, and Sales Leaders own coaching, reinforcement, and team execution.
  • Lead the planning and orchestration of company-level readiness initiatives, aligning senior stakeholders on objectives, ownership, timing, reinforcement, and measures of success.
  • Set direction and accountability for the operational health of the learning ecosystem, including the LMS, learning calendars, program records, learner communications, reporting, and content standards.
  • Develop scalable readiness programs for Huntress selling practices and workflows, including MEDDPICC, Digital Sales Rooms, Mutual Action Plans, and AI-supported ways of working.
  • Define how Huntress measures readiness across participation, preparedness, competency, adoption, and behavior change. Use those insights to improve programs and guide future investment while maintaining Sales Leader accountability for business performance.
  • Build, lead, and develop the Revenue Readiness team. Establish the organizational structure, capabilities, role clarity, operating rhythms, and performance expectations needed to support a growing global revenue organization.
  • Represent Revenue Readiness in senior GTM planning and decision-making, ensuring major initiatives account for the time, support, and reinforcement teams need to adopt change successfully.

What You Bring To The Team:   

  • You have 10+ years of experience across revenue readiness, sales enablement, learning operations, sales effectiveness, or related go-to-market functions, including 5+ years leading teams or major functional programs.
  • You have led a revenue readiness, enablement, or sales effectiveness function in a scaling B2B SaaS organization and have built or significantly evolved its strategy, team, infrastructure, and operating model.
  • You have influenced senior executives, shaped cross-functional priorities, and made investment and resource tradeoffs across a portfolio of competing business needs.
  • You understand how to build organizational readiness and assess whether teams are prepared to execute, reinforce new expectations, and sustain change.
  • You have designed scalable systems for program intake, prioritization, learning operations, onboarding, reinforcement, content governance, and readiness measurement.
  • You are an effective cross-functional operator who can bring together business leaders, operational partners, systems teams, and subject matter experts while maintaining clear ownership.
  • You can establish clear roles and decision rights across Revenue Readiness, Sales Ops Business Partners, Sales Leaders, Product Marketing, GTM Systems, Technical Sales, and other contributors.
  • You understand B2B SaaS selling across multiple roles, segments, motions, and levels of complexity, including the critical role frontline managers play in coaching, reinforcement, inspection, and accountability.
  • You can lead a team and senior stakeholders through meaningful organizational change, creating clarity, building alignment, and establishing the priorities, governance, and operating practices needed for a scalable Revenue Readiness function.
  • You use data and judgment to evaluate preparedness, identify readiness risks, improve programs, and communicate investment tradeoffs to senior leaders.
  • You can orchestrate multi-step AI workflows and reusable systems that improve analysis, program development, learning operations, prioritization, and decision quality while applying sound judgment to the outputs.

What We Offer: 

  • 100% remote work environment - since our founding in 2015
  • Generous paid time off policy, including vacation, sick time, and paid holidays
  • 12 weeks of paid parental leave
  • Highly competitive and comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits plans 
  • 401(k) with a 5% contribution regardless of employee contribution
  • Life and Disability insurance plans
  • Stock options for all full-time employees 
  • One-time $500 reimbursement for building/upgrading home office
  • Annual allowance for education and professional development assistance 
  • $75 USD/month digital reimbursement
  • Access to the BetterUp platform for coaching, personal, and professional growth

Title: Technical Program Manager (Mechanical Hardware)
Description:
Hyliion is committed to creating innovative solutions that enable clean, flexible and affordable electricity production. The Company’s primary focus is to develop distributed power generators that can operate on various fuel sources to future-proof against an ever-changing energy economy.

Job Purpose

The Technical Program Manager owns the planning and coordination of hardware programs focused on our additive technology and other traditionally manufactured power generation components. This role helps bridge the gap between engineering, supply chain, manufacturing, and operations—ensuring our beta-stage designs make a successful leap to production.

 

Duties and Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities:

  • Drive the end-to-end program execution for mechanical components, from prototype validation to initial production ramp.
  • Partner with mechanical design engineers and manufacturing engineers to ensure designs are manufacturable and scalable.
  • Develop and maintain detailed project timelines, tracking milestones, budgets, and risk mitigation plans.
  • Lead cross-functional meetings to align engineering, operations, procurement, quality assurance and external vendors around shared goals.
  • Coordinate testing and validation of parts, including mechanical, thermal, and durability testing in real-world power generation applications.
  • Assist in supplier sourcing, DFM (Design for Manufacturability) reviews, and process validation with AM (Additive Manufacturing) partners.  Track any ECRs resulting from modifications needed from design issues, testing, DFM or DFMEA activities.
  • Report regularly to leadership on program status, blockers, and key decision points.

Project Coordination & Support:

  • Deep dive into the Mechanical hardware program blocks .
  • Track project milestones, tasks, and deadlines, proactively identifying, flagging potential delays or risks, and actively problem solve to mitigate the risk in the delays.

Description:

The Technical Program Manager owns the planning and coordination of hardware programs focused on our assembling and other traditionally manufactured power generation components and deliverables. This role helps bridge the gap between engineering, supply chain, manufacturing, and operations, ensuring our beta-stage designs make a successful leap to production.

 

AI at Hyliion

Title: Corporate Governance Attorney - Assistant Vice President / Vice President
Location: New York, New York, United States
Description:
About the Role

iCapital is seeking a Corporate Governance Attorney to join the Legal team. The ideal candidate will support and enhance iCapital's Global Corporate Governance program and provide legal guidance on a broad range of corporate governance matters affecting domestic and international subsidiaries. This individual will work closely with senior members of the Legal team to ensure compliance with applicable corporate laws, governance requirements, and regulatory obligations while supporting strategic corporate initiatives.

Responsibilities

  • Draft, review, and maintain corporate governance documentation, including board and shareholder resolutions, meeting minutes, consents, governing documents, certificates, and other corporate records.
  • Advise on corporate governance matters impacting U.S. and non-U.S. entities, including applicable legal and regulatory requirements.
  • Prepare and maintain powers of attorney, incumbency certificates, officer appointments, and related corporate documentation.
  • Coordinate with registered agents and external service providers to obtain good standing certificates, certified filings, and other corporate records.
  • Assist in the development, implementation, and enhancement of corporate governance policies and procedures in response to evolving regulatory requirements.
  • Support entity formations, dissolutions, restructurings, mergers, and other corporate transactions while maintaining related records within the entity management system.
  • Provide legal support for subsidiary governance matters and corporate entity compliance, including KYC requests, regulatory inquiries, requests for information, and audits.
  • Lead the legal preparation, coordination, and execution of board and committee meetings, including agendas, materials, minutes, resolutions, and action item tracking.
  • Respond to requests for corporate governance information and documentation from auditors, regulators, business partners, and internal stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with colleagues across Legal, Compliance, Finance, Tax, and other business functions on governance-related initiatives and special projects.
  • Support other legal matters and strategic projects as assigned.

Qualifications

  • Juris Doctor (JD) degree is required
  • Admission to practice law in at least one U.S. jurisdiction is preferred
  • 3-7 years of corporate governance, corporate law, entity management, or related legal experience, preferably within a law firm or in-house legal department
  • Experience supporting multinational corporate structures and subsidiary governance programs
  • Strong understanding of corporate governance principles and entity lifecycle management
  • Excellent drafting, analytical, and problem-solving skills
  • Able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced and evolving business environment
  • Highly organized and detail-oriented with strong judgment and communication skills
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word and Excel

Benefits

The base salary range for this role is $150,000 to $175,000.  iCapital offers a compensation package which includes salary, equity for all full-time employees, and an annual performance bonus. Employees also receive a comprehensive benefits package that includes an employer matched retirement plan, generously subsidized healthcare with 100% employer paid dental, vision, telemedicine, and virtual mental health counseling, parental leave, and unlimited paid time off (PTO).

Title: Print Operations Program Manager II
Description:
ICON is looking for a Print Operations Program Manager to manage and develop Process, Planning, & Quality Programs. This role is critical in developing, documenting, and implementing operational processes and quality standards across Print Operations. The primary responsibilities of this role includes developing process documentation, checklists, workflows, and SOPs aimed at improving Print Ops operations and quality. In this role you will be responsible for the detailing of our processes in Miro flow charts, Google Sheets, and Procore. You will work with Print Operations Management to refine and implement these processes in line with discovered best practices. You will also be responsible for coordinating efforts surrounding all process improvement for Print Operations including data aggregation and analysis, scheduling process improvement meetings, and communication / coordinating, quality control procedures and documentation, and the rollout of new processes. This role is based primarily at ICON’s HQ in Austin, TX but may require some (25%) travel, at local or deployed job sites dependent on departmental needs. This role will report to the Print Workforce Manager, Print Operations. You will collaborate regularly with the Print Operations and Print Logistics Managers, as well as with deployed teams in the field.  



RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Meet regularly with Print Operations management and work directly on-slab in the field to identify opportunities for process improvement and develop improvement strategy.
  • Collect, interpret and evaluate process metrics data to provide data driven insights for process improvement.
  • Lead the development of process documentation, workflows, checklists, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) to enhance efficiency, consistency, and quality in field operations.
  • Document Print Ops processes in a variety of software tools suites, including but not limited to Palantir, Procore, Miro, and the Microsoft software suite.
  • Own the upload and administration of all Procore documentation for field facing procedures, and act as the implementation lead for Print Ops.
  • Accountable to the enforcement of process compliance for all Print Operations processes.
  • Work cross-functionally with Print Logistics & Print Operations management, Project & Construction Management teams, and Software team to gather requirements for planning printer suite & support equipment deployment, and site planning. 


MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related field.
  • 5+ years of experience in construction, manufacturing, surveying, or other industries with dynamic team structures and fast-paced implementations/improvements/iteration.
  • Exceptional documentation skills, ensuring compliance with ICON’s standards and accurate records.
  • Strong oral and written communication skills in a fast-paced environment.
  • Passion to improve efficiency and contribute to innovation.
  • Ability to flex working hours as required to support business needs.
  • An in depth understanding of equipment setup process and dimensions, mobilization process, and printer setup requirements / logistics.
  • Excellent prioritization and time management skills, with the ability to thrive in dynamic, fast-paced environments.


 PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Familiarity with construction or factory production environments and the ability to think and stay ahead for the needs of the operation.
  • ACC, Revit or similar CAD software experience in planning site layouts.
  • Advanced proficiency in operating heavy machinery to ensure smooth function.

ICON Build is looking for a Program Manager with roots in architecture and construction who brings more than delivery skills — someone who thinks visually, writes clearly, and can turn complex project information into compelling documents and presentations. We’re especially interested in candidates who combine architectural training with fluency in construction technology and digital tools — people who understand that clean processes and scalable systems are what let great design actually get built. This role will report to the Senior Program Manager, ICON Build at our Miami, FL office.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Support ongoing assessment of ICON Build delivery workflows across assigned functional areas — identifying process gaps, documentation deficiencies, and coordination breakdowns that affect team performance and project outcomes.
  • Implement and maintain standardized processes, SOPs, and decision frameworks developed in partnership with senior program leadership, ensuring they are current, accessible, and actively used by project teams.
  • Maintain and update the ICON Build playbook — organizing role-specific templates, checklists, and process guides, tracking version control, and ensuring content reflects current delivery standards and lessons learned.
  • Embed with project teams during key delivery phases — business development, preconstruction, buyout, field execution, or closeout — to support workflow adoption, surface friction in real time, and document how established processes perform under field conditions.
  • Track adoption and usage of tools including BuildOS across assigned projects; flag gaps between intended and actual use, compile feedback from project managers and field staff, and bring structured findings to senior program leadership.
  • Support print operations coordination by maintaining project documentation, managing internal communication workflows between design and operational stakeholders, and ensuring schedule and deliverable alignment across handoffs. 


MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 5–10 years of experience in architecture, design-build delivery, or AEC — with direct exposure to design coordination, preconstruction, or project execution across multiple phases.
  • Fluency in construction technology and digital tools — comfortable evaluating, adopting, and building workflows around software platforms used in AEC project delivery.
  • Demonstrated visual communication ability — a portfolio or work samples showing document and presentation output is strongly preferred.
  • Proficiency with presentation and document tools: Google Suite plus at least one design-adjacent tool (Adobe Creative Suite, Figma, InDesign, Canva Pro, or equivalent).
  • Experience building or improving processes and systems — the kind that reduce friction, improve consistency, and scale as a team grows.
  • Familiarity with construction project documentation — drawing logs, submittal registers, RFIs, meeting minutes, and schedule formats.
  • Comfort with construction management platforms: Procore, Autodesk Construction Cloud, or similar. 

 

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Exposure to 3D modeling or visualization tools: Revit, Rhino, SketchUp, Enscape, or similar.

Title: Data Governance Manager/Strategist
Description:
About impact.com
impact.com is the world’s leading commerce partnership marketing platform, transforming the way businesses grow by enabling them to discover, manage, and scale partnerships across the entire customer journey. From affiliates and influencers to content publishers, brand ambassadors, and customer advocates, impact.com empowers brands to drive trusted, performance-based growth through authentic relationships. Its award-winning products—Performance (affiliate), Creator (influencer), and Advocate (customer referral)—unify every type of partner into one integrated platform. As consumers increasingly rely on recommendations from people and communities they trust, impact.com helps brands show up where it matters most. Today, over 5,000 global brands, including Walmart, Uber, Shopify, Lenovo, L’Oréal, and Fanatics, rely on impact.com to power more than 225,000 partnerships that deliver measurable business results.

Your role at impact.com:

We are seeking a strategic, collaborative leader to bridge the gap between business objectives and data integrity. In this role, you will partner closely with key business stakeholders to translate high-level organizational goals into clear, actionable data governance frameworks.

Rather than focusing solely on day-to-day administrative execution, you will act as a strategic advisor—using your understanding of data structures to envision possibilities, define standards, and ensure our Salesforce and operational data environments directly support business growth, compliance, and decision-making.

Key Responsibilities:

Title: Governance and Controls lead
Description:
Job Description – Governance and Controls Lead

Location, UK, Manchester, (Hybrid)

About Inizio
Inizio is a global partner to health and life sciences organisations, delivering specialist expertise across the product and patient journey. Through Global Finance Services (GFS), we provide high-quality, efficient and compliant finance operations that support business performance worldwide.

Role Overview
Reporting to the Head of Global RTR, we are seeking a Governance and Controls Lead within RTR to own the GFS SOX control framework, act as the primary liaison for internal and external audit within RTR, and drive governance, controls and compliance with primary focus on RTR.

Each Head of Function owns the control set for their process tower. This role sets GFS-wide standards and coordinates with the Governance and Compliance Lead in OTC and the PTP Process Excellence Lead to ensure consistency, providing the governance infrastructure underpinning GFS's control and compliance obligations. The role coordinates audit activity at a GFS level, consolidating outcomes and reporting across towers in partnership with the Governance and Compliance Lead, OTC and the PTP Process Excellence Lead.

In addition to the controls remit, the role owns master data governance for vendors and customers, is responsible for data quality and integrity across GFS, and reports on service quality performance across GFS process towers including KPIs, SLAs and error trends.

Direct reports include a Data Accountant and a Master Data Lead; the role is also responsible for the GFS intern programme. The role provides GFS leadership with clear insight on control effectiveness, process health and emerging risks.

Here's what you'll be doing

Governance, Controls & Compliance

  • Maintain and evolve the GFS SOX control framework across all process towers.
  • Set standards for control documentation, evidence quality and cross-process consistency.
  • Lead the CSA programme within RTR and coordinate CSA activity across GFS in partnership with the Governance and Compliance Lead, OTC and the PTP Process Excellence Lead, ensuring consistent methodology, evidence standards and follow-through on findings.
  • Act as the primary liaison for internal and external audit within RTR, coordinating management testing, reviewing outcomes and driving remediation.
  • Coordinate audit activity at a GFS level, consolidating outcomes and reporting across towers in partnership with the Governance and Compliance Lead, OTC and the PTP Process Excellence Lead.
  • Own quality standards across GFS through KPI, SLA and error trend monitoring.
  • Lead master data governance and data quality standards for vendors and customers.
  • Identify and escalate operational, financial and compliance risks across GFS, working with Heads of Function and tower governance leads to ensure risks are addressed and lessons learned are embedded into process design.
  • Act as the governance gate for new processes, system implementations and scope migrations into GFS, ensuring control readiness is demonstrated before go-live within RTR and that GFS-wide standards are applied consistently across towers.
  • Provide governance reporting and insight to GFS and Finance leadership.
  • Report on service quality performance across GFS process towers, including KPI, SLA and error trend analysis, providing GFS and Finance leadership with clear and timely insight on process health and emerging risks.

Leadership

  • Lead and develop the master data and performance insight team.
  • Manage the GFS intern programme in partnership with a local university.

Continuous Improvement

  • Use CSA results, audit outcomes and service quality data to identify emerging risks and improvement opportunities, escalating findings to the relevant Head of Function or tower governance lead and tracking remediation to closure.

What you'll bring

Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional qualification in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration or a related discipline.
  • Professional accountancy qualification (ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent) required.
  • Significant experience in SOX compliance, internal controls and audit management within a global Shared Services Centre (SSC) or Global Business Services (GBS) environment, with significant RTR process exposure - essential.
  • Experience leading control frameworks, designing and operating CSA programmes and coordinating internal and external audit activity across a multi-process shared services environment required.
  • Experience owning or governing finance master data, including vendor and customer master data, within a controlled shared services environment is advantageous.

Technical & Operational Expertise

  • Strong knowledge of SOX, internal controls and GFS process environments (RTR, PTP, OTC and Payroll).
  • Master data governance, KPI reporting and performance management expertise.
  • Strong stakeholder management and ability to influence senior leaders.

Problem Solving & Innovation

  • Resolve complex governance, audit and quality issues.
  • Challenge remediation plans and assess control readiness for change.

Stakeholder Management & Communication

  • Build trusted relationships with Finance leadership, Global Process Owners and auditors.
  • Communicate governance risks, audit outcomes and control standards clearly.

Performance, Impact & Ways of Working

  • Independent judgement and strong governance mindset.
  • Collaborative leader focused on quality, compliance and continuous improvement.

Why join us

You'll play a central role in shaping how Global Finance Services manages its control environment, master data integrity and governance standards across a $2B global organisation. This is a high-visibility role with direct access to GFS leadership and external audit, combining deep RTR governance expertise with GFS-wide standards leadership and a team focused on data quality and performance insight.

Don't meet every job requirement? That's okay! Our company is dedicated to building an inclusive and authentic workplace. If you're excited about this role, but your experience doesn't perfectly fit every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right person for this role or others.
