Title: Research & Development Technical Program Manager
Description:
Silvus Technologies, a leading provider of advanced MANET and MIMO communications systems, is reshaping mesh network technology for mission-critical applications – on the ground, in the air and at sea. Its battle-proven StreamCaster family of MANET radios and proprietary MN-MIMO waveform provides the vital communications link for defense, law enforcement and public safety agencies around the world, and in the toughest operational environments. 

Silvus Technologies is a wholly owned subsidiary of Motorola Solutions, Inc.

Would you like to join an incredibly talented group of people, doing very challenging work, with the prime directive of “Keeping Our Heroes Connected”?

THE OPPORTUNITY

Silvus Technologies, the global leader in advanced MIMO mesh networking solutions for defense, industrial, and public safety applications, is seeking an R&D Technical Program Manager reporting to the Vice President of Research and Development. The successful individual in this role will drive execution excellence across our next-generation products.

This is a foundational Technical Program Manager role, offering a unique opportunity to build and shape the program management discipline within Silvus’ growing Engineering and R&D organizations. You’ll partner closely with senior R&D and engineering leadership, and all functional and product teams to define best practices, drive cross-functional execution, and deliver high-impact products to our customers.

You will be part of a passionate team redefining RF sensing, electronic warfare and wireless connectivity in the most demanding environments, from battlefield networks and autonomous systems to public safety and industrial applications. You will work alongside world-class engineers solving real-world challenges, with opportunities to grow, innovate, and lead as our organization scales.

If you’re ready to help shape the future of communications and electronic warfare and establish the foundation of Silvus’ Program Management organization, we’d love to meet you.

The R&D Technical Program Manager position will be based at Silvus Technologies’ headquarters in the heart of vibrant West Los Angeles, CA, and is on a hybrid schedule, a minimum of 3 days onsite per week is expected. On-site days are Mondays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays.

The following is a list of at least some of the current essential job functions of the position. Management may assign or reassign duties and responsibilities at any time at its discretion.

ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Lead end-to-end program execution across the full engineering lifecycle, from concept and design through implementation, integration, validation, and productization.
  • Own program schedules, milestones, and deliverables, ensuring alignment across cross-functional teams including Systems, FPGA, Software, RF, Hardware, and QA.
  • Facilitate cross-team collaboration to identify and resolve technical or schedule blockers, driving timely and data-driven decisions.
  • Track risks, dependencies, and issues; develop mitigation strategies and communicate impacts proactively to leadership.
  • Drive engineering cadence and communication, including design reviews, design syncs, and status updates with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Maintain project documentation and dashboards (e.g., Confluence, JIRA) for clear visibility into goals, progress, and key metrics.
  • Prepare executive reports and presentations, communicating program status, milestones, and risk assessments to senior management.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field plus a minimum 5 years of relevant program management and/or engineering experience in a technology-driven organization
  • Proven experience managing complex hardware/software or wireless/networking programs in a fast-paced R&D or product development environment.
  • Must be a U.S. Citizen (due to requirements of U.S. government contracts).
  • All employment is contingent upon the successful clearance of a background check.

PREFERRED KNOWLEDGE SKILLS AND ABILITIES

  • Master’s degree in EE, ECE, or a related field with 8+ years of relevant industry experience.
  • Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple programs and shift priorities.
  • Exceptional communication and presentation abilities with a track record of influencing across technical and non-technical teams.
  • Demonstrated success in hands-on product development, technical program management, or engineering leadership roles.
  • Technical fluency in one or more of the following areas: wireless systems design, RF engineering, networking, firmware/software integration, or test/validation.

Title: Sr. Manager, Program Management (Enterprise Data Platform)
Description:
About SimpliSafe

We’re a high-tech home security company that’s passionate about protecting the life you’ve built and our mission of keeping Every Home Secure. And we’ve created a culture here that cares just as deeply about the career you’re building. Ours is a no ego culture of collaboration and innovation where those seeking their next challenge can find big opportunities and make a huge impact on the lives of all those who we protect. We don’t just want you to work here. We want you to grow and thrive here.

We’re embracing a hybrid work model that enables our teams to split their time between office and home. Hybrid for us means we expect our teams to come together in our state-of-the-art office on two core days, typically Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday – working together in person and choosing where they work for the remainder of the week. We all benefit from flexibility and get to use the best of both worlds to get our work done.

Why are we hiring?

Well, we’re growing and thriving. So, we need smart, talented, and humble people who share our values to join us as we disrupt the home security space and relentlessly pursue our mission of keeping Every Home Secure. 

About the Role

SimpliSafe is investing in a multi-quarter Enterprise Data Platform (EDP) program to migrate our data and analytics stack onto a modern platform and stand up the architecture, governance, and operating model needed to support AI/ML, personalization, and data-driven decision-making at scale. We're looking for a Sr. Manager, Program Management to run the day-to-day delivery of this program — coordinating vendors, engineering, governance, and business stakeholders across every phase, from platform build through migration and adoption.

What You'll Do

You will be responsible for the planning, execution, and oversight of the EDP program's complex, cross-functional workstreams from initiation to completion. You will directly report to the Sr. Director of Enterprise Data. You will work closely with engineering, architecture, governance, procurement, legal, and business teams to ensure the program is delivered on time, within budget, and in scope. The ideal candidate is resilient, comfortable owning ambiguity, and has a keen eye for detail — someone who can zoom into the mechanics of a single vendor contract one day and drive the multi-phase migration roadmap the next.

EDP Program Delivery

  • Own end-to-end delivery of platform implementation — from vendor signature through onboarding, build, and phased migration — ensuring each phase lands on time, in scope, and within budget.
  • Lead contract execution for platform and implementation vendors — partner with Procurement, Legal, and Finance to move MSAs, SOWs, and change orders from negotiation through signature, and track terms, deliverables, and payment milestones.
  • Drive vendor onboarding — stand up new implementation partners and technology vendors from kickoff through steady-state delivery, including (not limited to) access provisioning, working agreements, and communication cadence.
  • Manage phased migrations — sequence and execute the program's multi-phase migration from current-state infrastructure, through optimization, to the new platform, tracking cross-team dependencies, cutover readiness, rollback plans, and go/no-go criteria for each phase.
  • Design and run the program's intake and prioritization process — build the mechanism for capturing, scoring, and sequencing new data and platform requests, then operate and evolve it as demand and priorities shift.
  • Drive rollout of data models, architecture standards, and governance — partner with engineering and architecture to launch new data models and reference architecture, and stand up governance bodies (e.g., Steering Committee, Data Governance Council, Architecture Review Board), driving adoption across the business.

Core Program & Project Management

  • Operate at both the project and program level — able to lead a single EDP workstream to completion (a vendor contract, a migration phase) and also run the multi-workstream program, managing interdependencies, aligning teams to shared outcomes, and balancing competing priorities across leaders.
  • Develop comprehensive project and program plans with clear timelines, resource allocation, and critical milestones — at the right level of detail for each.
  • Coordinate effectively across functions — including engineering, architecture, data governance, InfoSec, Procurement, Legal, Finance, and business stakeholders — acting as a central point of contact and ensuring clear communication,alignment, and timely action.
  • Monitor progress and develop risk mitigation strategies to address emerging issues and keep work on track, at both the project and program level.
  • Conduct regular WBR, QBR sessions to ensure the program tracking is transparent and risks are escalated. 
  • Strategically manage resources, including not limited to allocation (as needed by the Senior Director), to optimize team productivity and achieve goals across the portfolio.
  • Own budget tracking across legacy and new-platform environments during the transition period, including reconciling cost figures across reporting cycles and flagging discrepancies before they reach executive/board level. 
  • Own ongoing budget tracking post-migration — track platform run-rate and consumption against forecast, surface optimization opportunities, and feed accurate figures into annual planning and vendor renewal cycles 
  • Provide regular updates and reports to stakeholders and senior leadership, including the EDP Steering Committee — tailoring depth and altitude to the audience.
  • Maintain comprehensive documentation — vendor contract trackers, governance charters, and RAPID/RACI matrices — and prepare clear, concise reports for stakeholders.
  • Identify gaps in process, iterate for continuous improvement, and build playbooks that reduce rework, redundancy, and re-creation.
  • Manage and shape expectations across company stakeholders. 
  • Evaluate and select the right tools and communication mechanisms for each workstream based on scope, complexity, and stakeholder needs.
  • Motivate and influence team members to achieve objectives; provide support to cultivate a collaborative, positive work environment.
  • Conduct post-phase and post-program evaluations to assess performance, identify areas for improvement, and apply lessons learned.
  • Go beyond tactical execution — learn the EDP program deeply enough to become a strategic partner and influencer to program leadership. Be the R (Recommend) in the RAPID framework: bring analysis, point of view, and recommendations, not just status updates.

What Values You’ll Share

  • Customer Obsessed - Building deep empathy for our customers, putting them at the core of our work, and developing strong, long-term relationships with them.
  • Aim High - Always challenging ourselves and others to raise the bar.
  • No Ego - Maintaining a “no job too small” attitude, and an open, inclusive and humble style.
  • One Team - Taking a highly collaborative approach to achieving success.
  • Lift As We Climb - Investing in developing others and helping others around us succeed.
  • Lean & Nimble - Working with agility and efficiency to experiment in an often ambiguous environment.

What We Offer

  • A mission- and values-driven culture and a safe, inclusive environment where you can build, grow and thrive  
  • A comprehensive total rewards package that supports your wellness and provides security for SimpliSafers and their families (For more information on our total rewards please click here)
  • Free SimpliSafe system and professional monitoring for your home. 
  • Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) that bring people together, give opportunities to network, mentor and develop, and advocate for change.

The target annual base pay range for this role is $140,000 to $187,000

This target annual base pay range represents our good-faith estimate of what we expect to pay for this role. We use a market-based compensation approach to set our target annual base pay ranges and make adjustments annually. We carefully tailor individual compensation packages, including base pay, taking into consideration employees’ job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location, and other relevant business factors. 

Beyond base pay, we offer a Total Rewards package that may include participation in our annual bonus program, equity, and other forms of compensation, in addition to a full range of medical, retirement, and lifestyle benefits. More details can be found here.

We’re committed to fair and equitable pay practices, as well as pay transparency. We regularly review our programs to ensure they remain competitive and aligned with our values.

We wholeheartedly embrace and actively seek applications from all individuals, no matter how they identify. We are committed to cultivating a diverse and inclusive workplace, and we believe our work is enriched when we incorporate a multitude of perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences. We want everyone who works here to thrive and contribute to not only our mission of keeping every home secure, but also to making our workplace safe and supportive for others. Program Manager

Company: Defense-technology company (name shared under NDA)

Confidential Search · Defense Technology

About the Client

A defense-technology company building mission-ready sensor and edge hardware for the toughest problems in defense and intelligence — where the gap between a system that works in a lab and one that works in the field is where programs live or die.

About the Role

As Program Manager, you'll own that gap for the company's most critical Army and Joint program office engagements: driving cost, schedule, and performance across contracts that directly support operational units, while also making sure individual product orders ship on time and on spec. You'll be the connective tissue between a team of 12-15 engineers and subcontractors and the government customers who depend on what they build. This isn't a coordination role - you're accountable for outcomes the customers actually count on.

Responsibilities

  • Own cost, schedule, and performance (CSP) tracking across the highest-priority contracts, escalating risks before they become problems rather than reporting them after the fact
  • Serve as primary point of contact for government program offices, running program reviews, status updates, and deliverable coordination

  • Partner with the Director of Contracts on subcontractor performance and deliverables - technical coordination and quality, not contractual/invoicing ownership
  • Support capture and proposal efforts as a past-performance and technical credibility resource

Must-Haves

Nice-to-Haves

  • Program Management certification
  • Experience supporting proposal or capture efforts as a past-performance/technical resource

Compensation & Benefits

  • Health coverage, fully covered - premiums paid 100% for you and your dependents
  • 401(k) with company contribution - a 4% contribution on your behalf regardless of your own contribution level
  • Unlimited PTO - average employee takes 3-4 weeks

Process

This position supports U.S. Government-related work. Applicants must be U.S. persons. The hiring company is an equal opportunity employer. Title: Technical Writer
Description:
Company Overview

At Skild AI, we are building the world's first general purpose robotic intelligence that is robust and adapts to unseen scenarios without failing. We believe massive scale through data-driven machine learning is the key to unlocking these capabilities for the widespread deployment of robots within society. Our team consists of individuals with varying levels of experience and backgrounds, from new graduates to domain experts. Relevant industry experience is important, but ultimately less so than your demonstrated abilities and attitude. We are looking for passionate individuals who are eager to explore uncharted waters and contribute to our innovative projects.

Position Overview

We are seeking a highly skilled Technical Writer to translate complex robotic intelligence into clear, accurate, and user-friendly documentation. In this role, you will be the connective tissue between our researchers, engineers, and the customers, operators, and developers who deploy our systems in the real world. You will own documentation across the full stack—from software architecture, APIs, and SDKs to deployment guides, operational procedures, and troubleshooting runbooks for robotic fleets in the field. Because our robots operate in diverse and challenging customer environments, your documentation must serve audiences ranging from ML researchers to field operators with no engineering background.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain comprehensive documentation for robotic intelligence software, including architecture overviews, APIs, SDKs, and codebases, serving both internal engineering teams and external developers and partners
  • Author clear deployment, configuration, maintenance, and troubleshooting documentation that enables operators and customers to run and manage fleets of robots in production environments
  • Collaborate closely with robotics researchers, ML engineers, software architects, and infrastructure teams to gather information, understand complex technical concepts, and accurately reflect product functionality and design
  • Own the documentation lifecycle end to end—from planning and drafting through review, publication, and ongoing updates—ensuring materials stay current, accurate, and easily accessible as products evolve rapidly
  • Establish and champion documentation best practices, style guidelines, and tooling; continually improve processes and content quality, and conduct peer reviews of documentation produced across teams
  • Maintain consistency in terminology, style, and tone across all documentation, tailoring content for audiences ranging from expert developers to non-technical field operators

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Technical Communication, English, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
  • Experience as a technical writer producing documentation in a fast-paced, highly technical environment
  • Demonstrated ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly and accurately to diverse audiences
  • Familiarity with software development concepts and comfort reading code (e.g., Python, C++, or similar)
  • Proven track record documenting complex software systems, including APIs, SDKs, and software architecture, and shipping high-quality documentation at scale

Title: Freelance Content Creator
Description:
ABOUT OGILVY SOCIAL.LAB 

Ogilvy Social.Lab isn't your typical agency. We're built for the social age, understanding that social isn’t just another channel; it’s where brands connect with their audience, engage, and thrive. This reality demands a social-first approach to brand building—one where creativity, community, culture, and creators intersect to drive impact. 

As WPP’s deep social specialist and Ogilvy’s Centre of Excellence in Social, we are purpose-built for the social era. From our HQ in Belgium and teams across Europe, we bring bold ideas, entrepreneurial spirit, and innovative strategies that challenge convention and deliver real business results. We thrive on shaping the future of brand communications, pushing boundaries and setting the pace for what’s next in social-first marketing. 

About the Role 

As a Content Creator at Ogilvy Social Lab, you are at the absolute forefront of where the advertising industry is going. Content is no longer just a support mechanism. Today, it is the driving force of modern brand storytelling. In this role, you will transition from traditional creative ideation to becoming a full-stack maker. You will have the autonomy and with the Strategy/Intelligence department to spot cultural trends, pitch format ideas, and physically bring those concepts to life from A to Z. 

You will be a key player in shaping how our clients show up in the digital world, while simultaneously taking the lead in defining how Ogilvy Social Lab presents itself to the industry. 

Key Responsibilities 

End-to-End Content Production (A to Z)

  • Ownership of Ideas: You are responsible for finding social-first content ideas and taking those ideas from initial spark to final execution. 
  • The Maker Mentality: You don't just brief production; you produce. You will script, shoot, edit, and deliver high-quality content independently. 

Creative Alignment & Team Collaboration

  • Collaborate & Innovate: Brainstorm and build on creative ideas alongside a talented team of content producers and creatives. 
  • On-Set Execution: Attend and help direct shoots when working on larger-budget, full-scale productions. 
  • End-to-End Ownership: Take full ownership of smaller-scale projects—from concept to final delivery—when working independently. 

Directing Agency Strategy & Channels

  • You will define, refine and roll out a distinct internal and external content strategy for the agency. Indeed, as the lead producer for Ogilvy Social Lab’s own social channels. You will create engaging, high-impact content centered around our award-winning work, agency culture, events, and talent initiatives. 

Commercial, Strategic & Competitive Intelligence

  • Strategic Ownership: Define, refine, and execute a distinct internal and external content strategy for Ogilvy Social Lab. 
  • Brand Voice & Channels: Act as the lead producer across all of Ogilvy Social Lab’s own social channels. 
  • Creative Content Creation: Concept and produce high-impact, engaging content highlighting our award-winning work, agency culture, live events, and talent initiatives. 
  • Be Our Creative & Trend Radar - Keep a constant pulse on the global content landscape. You’ll track how leading agencies and competitor brands are innovating, positioning yourself as our go-to expert on emerging social trends, formats, and best practices. 
  • Commercial & Story-Driven Mindset - Ensure every piece of content is rooted in a deep understanding of our clients’ business goals, commercial targets, and core messaging. Social content should be engaging, but it must also drive real business results—creating work that both tells a story and moves the needle. 

Guardians of Quality

  • Together with the agency's other Content Creator(s), you will act as the "guardian angel" of our content output. You will set, maintain, and champion the benchmark for what high-quality, impactful content creation looks like at Ogilvy. 

Lastly, have fun

  • The opportunities in this space are endless, you should want to explore them with curiosity, energy, and a sense of play. You view this shift not just as a job change, but as a playground for innovation. 

Profile 

  • Proven experience in a similar role, demonstrating your ability to contribute to creative excellence.  
  • Native or equivalent level of Dutch is mandatory. Good working knowledge of English. 
  • Creativity and originality that align with the innovative spirit of Ogilvy Social Lab.  
  • Effective teamwork and communication skills, fostering collaboration within the creative team.  
  • A natural curiosity for current trends in popular and digital culture, coupled with foresight into future advertising landscapes.  
  • Insight into human behavior and motivational needs, demonstrating a deep understanding of your audience.  
  • A keen sense of color and form to contribute to the visual and aesthetic aspects of the creative process.  
  • Ability to work well under pressure, meeting tight deadlines while maintaining the quality of work.  
  • Interest in immersing yourself in award annuals to explore and appreciate outstanding work in the field.  
  • A strong desire to learn and upskill, showcasing a commitment to personal and professional growth.  
  • Conceptualization skills that bring forth brave, fresh, and world-class ideas.

Title: Senior Finance Data Governance Consultant (Contract)
Description:
Why Sony Interactive Entertainment?

Sony Interactive Entertainment isn’t just the Best Place to Play — it’s also the Best Place to Work. Sony Interactive Entertainment (SIE) is the company behind the PlayStation brand. As a subsidiary of Sony Group Corporation, we’re part of a proud legacy of innovation and excellence. SIE is a dynamic technology company, delivering cutting-edge hardware and network services to more than 100 million people and an entertainment leader, home to some of the most beloved and recognizable intellectual properties (IP) in the world. Our role at SIE is to create and nurture the experiences under the PlayStation brand, a name synonymous with entertainment excellence and creativity.

Senior Finance Data Governance Consultant (Contract)

*This is a 12 month temporary assignment 

Sony Interactive Entertainment is seeking an experienced, hands-on Finance Data Governance consultant to help establish and operationalize SIE’s Finance Data Governance capability. The role will partner across Finance and Technology to define governance standards, document critical Finance data and lineage, establish data quality controls, govern master data and hierarchies, and support priority Finance data products.

The ideal candidate should have 8+ years of experience in data governance, Finance transformation, or Finance data management, with strong knowledge of financial processes and systems. Experience with SAP S/4HANA, Snowflake, data catalog/governance platforms such as Atlan or Collibra, and enterprise reporting tools is preferred. The candidate should be comfortable working independently in a greenfield environment and translating complex Finance and technical requirements into practical, sustainable governance processes.

Responsibilities:

Establish the Finance Data Governance Foundation

  • Assess the current maturity of Finance data governance, documentation, ownership, controls, and data management practices.
  • Design and implement a practical Finance Data Governance operating model, including roles, decision rights, governance forums, workflows, escalation paths, and operating cadences.
  • Create governance standards, procedures, templates, decision logs, issue-management routines, and approval processes that Finance and Technology teams can use in practice.

Build the Finance Data Inventory and Business Glossary

  • Identify and inventory priority Finance data domains, systems, tables, reports, interfaces, data products, calculations, mappings, and critical data elements.
  • Document business definitions, ownership, stewardship, approved usage, security classification, refresh frequency, and downstream dependencies.
  • Resolve conflicting definitions across Accounting, FP&A, management reporting, statutory reporting, and regional Finance teams.
  • Prepare metadata for publication in an enterprise data catalog and establish workflows for maintaining, reviewing, approving, and retiring governance documentation.

Document Data Lineage and Finance Transformation Logic

  • Map data from source systems through integration, transformation, consolidation, reporting, and analytical consumption.
  • Document business rules, transformation logic, mappings, allocations, eliminations, adjustments, currency translation, and reconciliation points.
  • Identify manual transformations, uncontrolled spreadsheets, duplicated logic, missing ownership, and lineage gaps, and support impact assessments for upstream changes.
  • Partner with technical teams to distinguish business lineage from physical and technical lineage.

Establish Data Quality and Financial Data Controls

  • Define practical Finance data quality standards, rules, thresholds, monitoring requirements, and acceptance criteria.
  • Build a data quality rule inventory and support issue identification, triage, root-cause analysis, ownership, remediation, escalation, and closure.
  • Develop data quality scorecards and maintain traceable and auditable evidence for approvals, exceptions, reconciliations, and remediation activities.

Govern Finance Master Data and Hierarchies

  • Document and govern Finance master data, reference data, mappings, and hierarchies, including accounts, cost centers, profit centers, entities, products, regions, currencies, scenarios, and reporting periods.
  • Define ownership, approval, versioning, effective dating, and change-control requirements.
  • Partner with master-data and technology teams on future hierarchy-management and Master Data Management initiatives, including business requirements, process design, testing, and downstream-impact assessment.

Support Priority Finance Data Products

  • Apply governance standards to priority Finance data products and procedures.
  • Support documentation and validation of SAP financial and consolidation data, including ACDOCA and ACDOCU where applicable.
  • Help document data flows and reconciliation requirements across SAP, consolidation and reporting platforms, Snowflake, Domo, planning tools, and downstream reports.·      
  • Support the development of governed enterprise context and semantic layers for reporting, analytics, and AI-enabled Finance use cases.

Drive Adoption and Manage Delivery

  • Facilitate workshops, prepare executive-ready updates, develop training materials, and coach data owners and stewards on their responsibilities.
  • Translate complex Finance and technical concepts into clear documentation and decisions.
  • Establish a repeatable onboarding approach for new data domains and data products.
  • Promote governance as an enabler of faster, more reliable reporting and analytics rather than as an administrative exercise.
  • Develop and maintain a prioritized governance backlog with defined owners, deliverables, dependencies, and completion criteria.
  • Work independently, identify missing requirements, and move ambiguous work toward resolution.

Required Qualifications:

  • Eight or more years of experience in data governance, Finance data management, Finance transformation, financial systems, data quality, metadata management, or related consulting roles.
  • Demonstrated experience establishing or materially improving a data governance and data strategy capability in a complex enterprise.
  • Strong understanding of Finance processes, including general ledger, management reporting, financial consolidation, planning, forecasting, close, and reconciliation.
  • Experience documenting financial data definitions, business rules, mappings, hierarchies, lineage, controls, and data quality requirements.
  • Experience partnering with Finance, Accounting, FP&A, data engineering, business intelligence, security, and enterprise technology teams.
  • Ability to distinguish business ownership and governance responsibilities from technical platform and engineering responsibilities.
  • Strong facilitation skills and the ability to drive decisions across stakeholders with different priorities.
  • Demonstrated ability to create detailed, usable deliverables with limited existing documentation or structure.
  • Strong written communication skills with the ability to produce both detailed working documentation and executive-level summaries.
  • Experience working in a consulting, transformation, or contractor environment where measurable deliverables and knowledge transfer are required.
  • Ability to operate independently in an ambiguous, fast-moving, greenfield environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with SAP S/4HANA Finance and related financial data structures, consolidation, or group reporting (e.g., ACDOCA, ACDOCU).
  • Experience with cloud data platforms, enterprise analytics/reporting tools, and data governance/catalog platforms (e.g., Snowflake, Tableau, Power BI, Domo, Atlan, Collibra, Purview, or similar).
  • Strong understanding of data quality and architecture, including SQL, data profiling/reconciliation, dimensional modeling, semantic layers, hierarchies, and modern data architectures.
  • Experience working with Finance data in SOX-controlled or audit-sensitive environments, including data supporting automation and AI; consulting, Finance transformation, or enterprise data advisory experience preferred.

Title: Global Content Communications Senior Specialist
Description:
Why Sony Interactive Entertainment?

Sony Interactive Entertainment isn’t just the Best Place to Play — it’s also the Best Place to Work. Sony Interactive Entertainment (SIE) is the company behind the PlayStation brand. As a subsidiary of Sony Group Corporation, we’re part of a proud legacy of innovation and excellence. SIE is a dynamic technology company, delivering cutting-edge hardware and network services to more than 100 million people and an entertainment leader, home to some of the most beloved and recognizable intellectual properties (IP) in the world. Our role at SIE is to create and nurture the experiences under the PlayStation brand, a name synonymous with entertainment excellence and creativity.

Global Content Communications Senior Specialist

San Mateo, CA (Collab)

 

Role Overview

Within Global Content Communications, this role will help shape how PlayStation collaborates with game publishers and developers, and will take a prominent role in planning, creating, and managing content focused on third-party titles published on PlayStation. Our goal is to elevate our third-party partners and create the most engaging content for gamers around the world.

This role will identify and develop content opportunities around exciting upcoming games of all shapes and sizes working with Sony Interactive Entertainment's Global Developer and Publisher Relations team as well as external studios and publishers. Content types will include news articles on PlayStation.Blog, as well as gameplay videos and other socially optimized content for PlayStation social channels including Instagram, TikTok, and more. The ideal candidate will combine deep knowledge of the games industry with strong content-creation instincts, social media expertise, and an ability to build trusted relationships with internal teams and external partners.

The role will sit within Global Content Communications and partner closely with teams across Sony Interactive, including Global Communications, Global Third-Party Marketing, Third-Party Portfolio, and Games Account Management, as well as external game publishers and developers.

 

Job Responsibilities

  • Maintain deep knowledge of upcoming games, publisher plans, industry trends, and player interests to proactively identify promising content opportunities.
  • Proactively develop and pitch creative ideas for PlayStation Blog, social media, video, and other Sony Interactive-owned channels that give players new reasons to engage with upcoming games.
  • Shape content plans around major third-party game campaigns, identifying the moments, stories, and content most likely to resonate with PlayStation audiences globally.
  • Pitch and develop content opportunities including game reveals, new gameplay, developer interviews, hands-on coverage, original social content, and other creative storytelling.
  • Develop simple, scalable processes that help the team organize upcoming third-party campaigns and content opportunities.
  • Partner closely with Sony Interactive Third-Party Marketing, Games Account Management, and other internal teams to develop content opportunities for third-party games.
  • Work across Sony Interactive teams to connect third-party content opportunities with broader PlayStation priorities, including PlayStation Plus and PlayStation Store.
  • Develop content plans with Sony Interactive’s international social media teams in mind, identifying opportunities that can extend across markets and collaborating with regional teammates to support global campaigns.
  • Help publishers understand the value of partnering with PlayStation by sharing content performance, audience insights, and learnings from previous campaigns.

 

What We're Looking For

  • 3-5 years of relevant experience in social media management and content creation, editorial content creation, corporate communications, content strategy, games marketing, or a related field.
  • Experience working in the video game industry is strongly preferred, given the need for this role to have deep and broad knowledge of the landscape. Candidates with a background in social media, editorial and content creation, communications, publisher relations, marketing, or third-party games will have the most relevant experience for this role. Candidates with relevant experience in entertainment, media, or other consumer-facing industries -- and a deep knowledge of games -- will also be considered.
  • Strong understanding of major social platforms and the types of content, formats, and storytelling approaches that resonate with their audiences.
  • Deep knowledge of the video game industry, including major publishers, developers, independent games, franchises, industry trends, and how games are communicated and marketed to players.
  • Strong editorial and creative instincts, with the ability to quickly identify what makes a game, announcement, asset, or developer story interesting to an audience.
  • Highly proactive and comfortable identifying and pursuing opportunities rather than waiting for assignments or incoming requests.
  • Experience working directly with external partners, with the confidence to pitch ideas, respond to opportunities, provide constructive feedback, and build trusted working relationships.
  • Experience developing content for global audiences and an understanding of how campaigns and creative ideas can be adapted or extended across international markets.
  • Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple games, campaigns, deadlines, and stakeholders simultaneously.
  • Comfortable working creatively within constraints, including developing compelling content opportunities when assets, timing, or resources may be limited.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly articulate ideas and build alignment across internal and external stakeholders.
  • Collaborative, curious, and comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where priorities and opportunities can change quickly.

Title: Content Security & Compliance Engineer
Description:
Sony Pictures Imageworks is located on the unceded traditional territory of the Musqueam, Squamish, and Tsleil-Waututh First Nations. We are committed to respecting traditional lands, and working with communities towards reconciliation.

Sony Pictures Imageworks Canada Inc.

658 Homer Street., Suite 405, Vancouver, BC, V6B 2R4

Benefits per company policy: include healthcare, tuition reimbursement, RRSP's, Sick and Vacation leave, standard increases as applicable

Job Summary
We are seeking a motivated and technically skilled Content Security & Compliance Engineer to join our Content Protection & Compliance team. In the Media & Entertainment industry, our most valuable assets are our stories, digital content, and production technologies. This role will contribute to our security controls, compliance requirements, and engineering practices effectively protecting our intellectual property while enabling efficient production workflows.

As a member of the Content Protection & Compliance team, you will collaborate  with Engineering, Security Operations, Production, Infrastructure, and Audit teams to assess risk, validate security configurations, operate compliance monitoring tools, and integrate security into technology solutions and production processes. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys combining hands-on technical work with security analysis, compliance, and collaboration across multiple technology disciplines.

Education and Certifications

Formal Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

Preferred Certifications

  • CISSP – Certified Information Systems Security Professional
  • CCSP – Certified Cloud Security Professional
  • AWS Certified Security – Specialty
  • SABSA
  • Trusted Partner Network (TPN) Assessor
  • Or equivalent industry-recognized cybersecurity certifications

Primary areas of responsibility will include:

  •  Initiates business and technical gap assessments to identify security, compliance, and operational risks.
  •  Leads risk assessments and track remediation efforts through completion.
  •  Develops and maintains security standards, procedures, technical documentation, and compliance artifacts.
  • Assess, implement, configure, and operate security compliance monitoring, SIEM, and security validation tools.

  • A key contributor to the Security Operations team, supporting operational security initiatives and incident response activities as needed.

Experience:

  • Experience operating security compliance, vulnerability management, SIEM, or configuration assessment tools.
  • Strong working knowledge of cloud security principles and common cloud security controls.
  • Understanding of industry security frameworks and standards such as NIST, CIS Benchmarks, ISO 27001, SOC 2, or similar.

Title: Program Manager, Alternative Investments Fellowship Program (AIFP)
Location: New York, New York, United States
Description:
Title: Program Manager, Alternative Investments 

Department: SEO Career & Alternative Investments

Report to: Senior Resident, AIFP 

Compensation: $70,500 - $83,000

FLSA: Exempt  

Employee Type: Full-Time, Regular

Location: New York, NY

Work Arrangement: Hybrid - 3 days/week in the SEO office at 55 Exchange Place, New York, NY 10005

 

ABOUT SEO 

Founded in 1963 during the Civil Rights Movement, SEO closes educational and career opportunity gaps for 7,000 ambitious young people annually.


POSITION OVERVIEW

The Program Manager, Alternative Investments supports the Associate Director, Alternative Investments and Senior Resident, AIFP in the day-to-day coordination and execution of SEO's Alternative Investments programming for the Alternative Investment Fellowship Program (AIFP). At times, this position may work with the Project Manager for the other programs in the Alternatives Investments portfolio, including Level Up: Alternative Investments and Investment Academy to encourage pipeline development and joint activities. 

While the Program Manager will have exposure to participants and contribute to their development journey, the core of the work centers on keeping programs running smoothly — managing logistics, tracking deliverables, coordinating across coaches and vendors, maintaining program data, and supporting the Senior Resident and Associate Director in executing against strategic priorities. This role serves as an operational backbone for the Alternative Investments Fellowship Program, ensuring that programming is well-organized, information flows effectively across stakeholders, and nothing falls through the cracks.

Program Coordination & Operations (40%)

  • Support the end-to-end coordination of AIFP programming, including scheduling, logistics, communications, and event execution for workshops, bootcamps, roadshows, partner-led sessions, and other program touchpoint.
  • Maintain and update program calendars, participant trackers, coach schedules, and operational documentation to ensure the Associate Director and the broader team have accurate, real-time visibility into program status and upcoming deliverables.
  • Assist in coordinating logistics for the SEO Alternative Investments Conference and other marquee program events, supporting planning activities and on-site execution.
  • Assist in sourcing and coordinating with vendors, third-party training providers, and external coaches, managing scheduling and follow-through to ensure programming is delivered on time and to standard.
  • Support the coordination of partner-led events, including materials preparation, firm communications, and post-event follow-up, in collaboration with the Partnerships and Events teams.
  • Serve as a consistent point of contact for program participants on logistical and administrative matters, directing substantive coaching and advising questions to the appropriate team member or coach.

Project Management & Cross-Functional Collaboration (30%)

  • Support the Associate Director in managing work streams across the Alternative Investments portfolio, tracking progress against program milestones, flagging risks or delays, and helping to keep deliverables on schedule.
  • Liaise with the Pathways team to coordinate participant readiness updates, ensure timely information-sharing about candidate pipeline status, and support the matching and placement process for AIFP participants.
  • Coordinate with the Program Manager supporting Level Up: Alternative Investments and Investment Academy to support the pipeline for alternative investments roles, ensuring scheduling and logistics are aligned.
  • Collaborate with coaches and AIFP mentors supporting the Alternative Investments programs — coordinating their schedules, managing session logistics, and tracking participation and completion — to ensure coaching is well-integrated and consistently delivered across the portfolio.
  • Assist in the development and maintenance of program curriculum materials, sourcing publicly available resources and coordinating with third-party training providers as directed by the Associate Director and Senior Resident.
  • Draft written content for participant communications, program marketing materials, newsletters, and engagement updates.

Participant Engagement Support (15%)

  • Support the onboarding of new AIFP participants, including communicating program expectations, distributing materials, and tracking completion of intake requirements.
  • Assist in the fellow and participant selection process for AIFP, coordinating application logistics, scheduling interviews, and managing candidate pipeline tracking in collaboration with the Associate Director and Senior Resident
  • Facilitate participant engagement touchpoints — including information sessions, check-ins, and group workshops — as directed, with a focus on connecting participants to the right resources, coaches, and program opportunities at each stage of their development.

Data Management & Reporting (15%)

  • Maintain program data across tracking systems and databases, ensuring participant records, engagement logs, coach activity, and outcome data are current and accurate.
  • Support the preparation of regular program performance updates and reporting for the Associate Director and Senior Resident, compiling data on participants engaged, coaching sessions completed, and placement and conversion outcomes across the Alternative Investments portfolio.
  • Track key program metrics — including AIFP fellows class formation, participant engagement rates, and placement rates — and flag data gaps or discrepancies to the Associate Director and Senior Resident for resolution.
  • Respond to ad hoc data and reporting requests from the Associate Director, Senior Resident and other program team members with accuracy and appropriate urgency.
  • Perform other assigned duties in support of SEO Career & Alternative Investments program goals and the overall mission of the organization.

QUALIFICATIONS 

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited four-year institution required.
  • 3–5 years of professional experience in program coordination, project management, operations, or a related field; experience in nonprofit, education, or financial services a plus.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple workstreams, track deliverables, and coordinate across stakeholders in a fast-paced environment.
  • Familiarity with or interest in alternative investments, private equity, or financial services preferred; candidates with a demonstrated interest in the industry and an understanding of the career landscape are encouraged to apply.
  • Experience with CRM or program management tools (e.g., Salesforce, Monday.com) a plus; strong proficiency in Microsoft Office required.

COMPETENCIES & SKILLS

  • Passion for SEO’s Mission: A deep curiosity and awareness of the barriers to entry and obstacles for career launch in the alternative investments industry, and a dedication to closing opportunity gaps.
  • Project Management: Highly organized and process-oriented, with a demonstrated ability to manage program logistics, track multiple workstreams simultaneously, and keep a team running smoothly. Comfortable building and maintaining systems that create operational clarity. 
  • Collaboration: Skilled at working across teams — including coaches, Career Mentors, the Pathways team, and external vendors — to coordinate support, share information, and drive cohesive program outcomes. A strong team player who builds trust through follow-through and clear communication. 
  • Attention to Detail: Meticulous in data management, communications, and logistics; understands that operational precision is foundational to a high-quality participant experience and credible program reporting. 
  • Communication: Able to communicate clearly and professionally — in writing and in person — across a diverse range of stakeholders including participants, coaches, program team members, and senior leadership. 
  • Initiative & Problem Solving: Proactive in identifying what needs to get done, anticipating logistics challenges before they arise, and escalating issues in a timely manner. Comfortable operating with a degree of autonomy on coordination tasks. 
  • Critical Thinking & Flexibility: Able to manage shifting priorities, respond to unexpected changes, and contribute constructively to a team navigating a dynamic, deadline-driven program environment. 
  • Technical Proficiency: Proficient in MS365, Box, Monday.com, and Excel; experience with Salesforce or comparable CRM and tracking platforms a plus; adept at learning new tools and systems quickly. 

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS  

SEO offers a competitive compensation package and comprehensive benefits plan including low-cost health, vision, and dental options, a generous holiday schedule and PTO policies, disability coverage, fully paid time off for new parents, and employer contributions to health reimbursement and retirement accounts. We are constantly working to improve our benefits each year based on the needs of our employees. We value wellness and strive to put people first and foremost.

Consistent with applicable law, compensation will be determined based on the skills, qualifications, and experience of the applicant along with the requirements of the position, and SEO reserves the right to modify this pay range at any time. 

EEOC Policy

At SEO we are committed to cultivating a team that embodies the backgrounds and experiences of the constituencies we serve and the communities we live in, and a workplace that reflects the impact we make in the world. Candidates from all communities – including people of color, women, members of the LGBTQIA+ Community, veterans, and people with disabilities – are strongly encouraged to apply.

Equal Employment Opportunity is not just the law, it is our commitment.

Sponsors for Educational Opportunity is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer – M/F/D/V. We will consider all qualified applicants for employment regardless of race, color, ethnicity, religion, sex, gender, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, age, marital status, veteran status, pregnancy, parental status, genetic information or characteristics, or any other legally protected status.

If you need accommodation while applying for a role with SEO, due to a disability, please email SEO Talent.

THE ORGANIZATION

Established in 1963 by Michael Osheowitz, SEO (Sponsors for Educational Opportunity) is an educational non-profit founded on the belief that talent is everywhere; but opportunity is not. Our programs are designed to educate, train, mentor, and amplify the voices of our participants to give them a seat at the table – every table. We propel human potential.

SEO is an innovator in education, mentorship, and creating educational career opportunities that maximize the full potential of our participants. Each year SEO serves 7,000+ participants nationally, and the organization is widely recognized for developing best-in-class programs with exceptional results.

Not every SEO participant is on the same journey, but all are hungry for opportunity and SEO creates an ecosystem of excellence. Learn more about SEO's programs here: https://www.seo-usa.org/our-programs/.

Title: Program Manager, PMO – Ellucian ERP SaaS Transformation
Description:
Strata Information Group (SIG) is a trusted leader in higher‑education technology consulting, supporting colleges and universities with ERP/SIS modernization, digital transformation, CRM, cybersecurity, and strategic advisory services. As a long‑standing and deeply embedded partner within the higher‑education sector, SIG brings together technical depth, operational insight, and a culture rooted in integrity, collaboration, and exceptional client service. Our heritage is built on hands‑on expertise, genuine relationships, and a commitment to delivering value with humility and excellence—values that continue to define us as we scale. 

Program Manager, PMO – Ellucian ERP SaaS Transformation 

Job Purpose Statement 

The Program Manager, operating within the Project Management Office (PMO), provides strategic leadership and oversight for large-scale Ellucian ERP transformation programs, including complex on-premise to SaaS migrations within higher education institutions.  

This role is responsible for managing programs consisting of multiple interconnected workstreams and project managers, ensuring alignment between client objectives, technology solutions, third-party and vendor stakeholders, and organizational change initiatives.  

The Program Manager serves as a trusted advisor to client executive leadership, translating complex technical and program issues into clear, concise executive-level summaries, and guiding stakeholders through complex enterprise transformations while ensuring successful program delivery, risk mitigation, timely decision making, and overall program governance.  

As a senior leader within the PMO, this role also directly coaches, and mentors Project Managers, building delivery capability and supporting their professional growth. The ideal candidate combines extensive Ellucian ERP implementation expertise with strong consulting, executive communication, people leadership, and stakeholder management capabilities. 

 

Job Responsibilities: 

  • Lead complex Ellucian ERP (Banner and/or Colleague) transformation programs, including on-premise to SaaS/cloud migrations, from initiation through stabilization, ensuring alignment with institutional goals and strategic priorities. 
  • Develop and maintain comprehensive program governance frameworks, including steering committees, executive reporting structures, and decision-making processes. 
  • Coordinate multiple concurrent project workstreams, ensuring dependencies, risks, resources, and timelines are effectively managed. 
  • Partner with institutional executives and project sponsors to establish program objectives, success metrics, and strategic outcomes. 
  • Provide oversight of implementation teams to ensure consistent delivery methodologies and adherence to program objectives. 
  • Operate as a senior member of the PMO, establishing and enforcing consistent program and project management standards, methodology, tools, and reporting cadence across the ERP transformation portfolio. 
  • Monitor and manage multi-million-dollar program budgets, resource allocation, forecasting and burn downs, and overall financial performance across the program portfolio. 
  • Identify, assess, and proactively manage program-level risks, issues, and dependencies. 
  • Develop and execute program communication strategies, including translating complex technical and program issues into clear, concise summaries for executive and client leadership audiences. 
  • Collaborate with functional and technical leaders to ensure implementation decisions support long-term institutional goals. 
  • Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure program success and realization of benefits. 
  • Ensure project teams maintain high-quality deliverables, documentation, and implementation standards. 
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for client executive sponsors, presenting program status, risks, and recommendations at the executive level in a clear, concise, and actionable manner. 
  • Support business development initiatives through thought leadership, proposal support, and client relationship management as needed. 

 

Required Job Qualifications 

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience. 
  • Ten or more years of experience leading large-scale ERP, SaaS, or enterprise software implementation programs within Higher Education. 
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex, multi-year transformation initiatives involving multiple projects and stakeholder groups. 
  • Direct experience with Ellucian Banner and/or Colleague ERP platforms is preferable; familiarity with Workday, Oracle, or other Higher Education ERP platforms is a plus. 
  • Experience delivering programs using the Ellucian Implementation Methodology is preferable. 
  • Proven success managing program governance, executive communications, and strategic stakeholder relationships. 
  • Strong understanding of on-premise to SaaS/cloud migration methodologies, organizational change management, and business process transformation. 
  • Experience managing multi-million-dollar program budgets, forecasts, resource planning, and financial reporting across a portfolio of concurrent initiatives. 
  • Ability to effectively engage and influence executive leadership, including Presidents, Provosts, Vice Presidents, CIOs, CFOs, and other senior stakeholders, with the ability to distill complex technical and program issues into clear, concise, executive-level summaries. 
  • Exceptional written, verbal, presentation, and facilitation skills. 
  • Strong analytical, organizational, critical thinking, and problem-solving abilities. 
  • Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams in complex and rapidly changing environments. 
  • Experience operating in matrix-managed environments, coordinating effectively with Ellucian Partner Network team, as well as other third-party vendors, without direct authority over all contributors. 
  • Experience coaching, and developing Project Managers assigned to Program Managers project(s) 
  • Ability and willingness to travel to client campuses as needed, up to approximately 25%. 
  • Experience utilizing project and program management tools such as Smartsheet, Microsoft Project, Jira, or similar platforms. 

 

Preferred Job Qualifications  

  • Previous higher education consulting experience. 
  • PMP, PgMP, or other related certifications; Ellucian-specific certifications or training a plus. 
  • Experience leading cloud migration or enterprise modernization initiatives; familiarity with Ellucian's Navigate to SaaS (N2S) methodology is a plus. 
  • Experience overseeing multiple ERP implementations simultaneously. 
  • Experience operating within a formal PMO, establishing or maturing program/project management standards, governance, and methodology.

Title: Senior Implementation Manager, Education Technology
Description:
Thanks for your interest in Success Academy! Running a large, fast-growing, and high-performing network of public charter schools takes a village - families, children, teachers, staff and faculty, advocates, and supporters alike. We are growing fast in New York and expanding to Florida, and we would love to welcome you to our community! We work tirelessly every day to ensure children have access to a fun, rigorous, whole-child education regardless of zip code or economic status. When you join SA, you play a part in giving every student who walks through our doors a fair shot at reaching his or her potential.

About this Role

We are looking for a Technology Planning & Implementation Lead to own the implementation of one of Success Academy's most consequential technology initiatives: the full replacement of our academic technology stack with an integrated ecosystem of Canvas, Learnosity, and a new Content Management System serving 20,000+ scholars across our network.

This role reports to the Head of Educational Technologies and sits at the center of a complex, multi-year program. This person owns the implementation: the pilot, the release process, the coordination across workstreams, and the organizational work that determines whether the technology actually lands. They will partner closely with our Leader of Schooling Systems, who will own the technical design, architecture, and build, as well as our Schooling and Education Institute teams, who own the learning design and educational outcomes. 

At its core, this role is an integration function. The program involves a set of forces that do not automatically align — what the business wants, what the technology can do, and what teachers and scholars need. This person's job is to understand all of those forces deeply and hold them in tension productively. That requires genuine curiosity. This person needs to actively seek out the perspective of teachers, school leaders, and business stakeholders, not just at the start of the project, but continuously, and use what they learn to keep the program grounded in reality as it evolves. This person must be comfortable stepping into gaps, picking up what isn't being owned, and doing whatever the program needs without waiting for clarity that may not come. 

The right candidate has led complex implementations before, thrives in ambiguous environments, and measures themselves by outcomes rather than the tidiness of their scope.

Key Responsibilities

Integration Across Business, Technology, and Constraints

  • Develop and maintain a complete, current picture of the program across all its dimensions
  • Serve as the connective tissue between technical, operational, and school-based stakeholders, ensuring that decisions made in any one of those contexts account for the constraints and realities of the others
  • Surface conflicts early and drive those conflicts to resolution before they become problems
  • Represent the overall goals and constraints of the program in every room, ensuring that no workstream optimizes for itself at the expense of the whole

Voice of the Customer and the Business

  • Actively and continuously seek out the perspective of teachers, school leaders, and business stakeholders throughout the program 
  • Synthesize what you hear into insight that is actually useful
  • Bring that insight into planning conversations, pilot design, release sequencing, and stakeholder communications, ensuring the program stays grounded in how real users experience the technology, not just how it performs in design

Pilot Design and Release Management

  • Own the design and execution of all pilots prior to full migration: define the sample, set success criteria, manage the process end to end, and translate findings into a clear recommendation for rollout
  • Own the release management process for the full implementation: the sequencing of feature releases, readiness criteria, and the coordination required to bring each phase to launch
  • Ensure each release reflects what has been learned from the previous one, and that lessons are captured, shared, and applied

Program Coordination and Momentum

  • Own the coordination machinery for the academic tech migration: workstream tracking, milestone management, risk identification, decision documentation, and cross-functional communication
  • Run the communication cadence that keeps the Head of Educational Technologies, senior leadership, and key stakeholders oriented 
  • Maintain momentum across a long, multi-stakeholder program

School Adoption and Change Management

  • Partner with the Schooling and EI teams on the strategy for school-facing adoption: how the new tools get introduced to teachers and school leaders, how training is structured, how readiness is assessed, and how problems surface and get resolved
  • Own release readiness on the school-facing side: confirm that schools and operational processes are ready before each phase goes live
  • Ensure that the pace and structure of the rollout reflect what you are hearing from schools — adjusting the approach when adoption patterns suggest the plan needs to change

What We're Looking For

This list of must-haves is short, but the bar is high. We would rather hire someone with excellent instincts and limited sector experience than someone with years in education technology who cannot move fast, make decisions, or operate without structure.

Non-Negotiables

  • You are a natural integrator: you instinctively pull together information from disparate sources, find the tensions, and work to resolve them before they become problems
  • You are deeply curious about how things actually work: you seek out the perspective of end users and business stakeholders not because it is on a checklist, but because you genuinely want to understand what they are experiencing
  • You have owned outcomes in complex, cross-functional environments
  • You have startup or high-growth experience and know what it means to operate without institutional scaffolding or clean swim lanes
  • You are a strong enough communicator to write a tight executive memo, run a sharp meeting, present to skeptical senior stakeholders, and have hard conversations when they are needed
  • You are politically intelligent: you read rooms accurately, understand what people actually care about, and navigate competing interests without losing momentum
  • You are a self-starter who identifies what needs to happen and does it

Core Competencies We Hire For

We evaluate every candidate against five attributes that predict success at Success Academy, regardless of role:

  • Critical Thinking. You get to the bottom of problems quickly and rigorously. You don't accept the first explanation, you interrogate assumptions, and you can distinguish between what's true and what's merely plausible.
  • Communication. You write with clarity and economy, and you're effective in person. You know that real communication means understanding your audience's perspective well enough to actually move them, not just transmit information at them.
  • Entrepreneurial Drive. You take full ownership of your outcomes. You are assertive about removing obstacles, you don't wait to be told what to do next, and you measure yourself by results rather than effort.
  • Resilience. You receive hard feedback and use it as fuel rather than a reason to disengage. You hold yourself to a high standard, and when someone raises the bar, your instinct is to rise to it.
  • Curiosity. You want to understand how things actually work, from the systems you're building to the teachers and scholars at the end of the chain. You trace your work through to its real-world impact and care about the details and edge cases you find along the way.

Strong Candidates Will Also Have

  • 8–12 years of total professional experience, with at least 4–5 years owning complex cross-functional implementations with real organizational stakes
  • Demonstrated experience as an integrator across technical, business, and user-facing workstreams: someone who has held the whole picture and used it to drive better decisions across all three
  • Experience working at the intersection of technology and business operations: not as an engineer, but as someone who has worked closely with technical teams, understands system constraints, and has successfully translated between technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • A track record of actively seeking out and incorporating end-user feedback
  • A background in high-growth or fast-moving organizations — media, publishing, content platforms, EdTech, or adjacent consumer technology industries are particularly relevant
  • Experience in K–12 education is a plus, but explicitly not a requirement; what matters more is experience delivering complex programs to end users at scale in organizations that move fast and expect a lot

Compensation, Benefits & Perks

At Success Academy, we invest boldly in our Network team with a comprehensive package designed to support your health, financial future, and overall well-being:

  • Day-One Health & Wellness: Medical, dental, and vision coverage starting your first day (SA covers 82% of our core medical plan), plus a free One Medical membership and confidential mental health support via EAP/Talkspace.
  • Financial Security: 403(b) retirement plan with a 3% employer match, up to $2,400/year in employer HSA contributions, employer-paid life/disability insurance, and Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) eligibility.

  • Perks & Stipends: A $50/month cellphone stipend ($600/year), pre-tax commuter benefits, backup family care, and performance-based earning incentives.
